adam she-banefesh — the 'man' aspect within the soul (one of the four chayot at the nefesh level), comprising both poor (miskenei) and rich (atirei), per 'the man became a living soul'
'vayehi ha-adam le-nefesh chayah' — verse Genesis 2:7 'and the man became a living soul,' prooftext for the man-aspect within the soul containing poor and rich

completion of the deficiency — the filling of a lack or want (shleimut ha-chisaron), whereby the spirit of life drawn through the Torah (linked to the melafum vowel, 'full mouth') makes whole what is missing, as in 'Open your mouth wide and I will fill it'
've-yiten lekha mishalot libekha' — verse Psalms 20:5/37:4 'may He grant you your heart's desires,' signifying the filling/completion of the lack (chisaron)

Teshuvah — repentance: the spiritual act of returning to God from sin, restoring oneself (and the displaced sparks/letters) to their divine source; the penitential movement of 'returning to Hashem' (וְשַׁבְתָּ עַד ה' אֱלֹקֶיךָ). Not תשובה in the sense of a reply/answer to a question.

the scriptural phrase "and my heart is slain/hollowed within me" (Psalms 109:22, ve-libi chalal be-kirbi), expounded in Likutey Moharan 6 as the heart emptied of the evil inclination — the slaughtered yetzer — signifying repentance and silence before God

Chavah (Eve), the first woman of Genesis — the proper name חַוָּה, invoked as a symbolic aspect (of the Holy Tongue/speech, honor, Malkhut/Oral Torah, the feminine counterpart of Adam); not the verb ח-ו-ה 'to declare' (יְחַוֶּה) nor 'to bow'
've-lailah le-lailah yechaveh' — verse Psalms 19:3 'night to night declares knowledge,' wordplay yechaveh/Chavah identifying Eve with the speech of the Holy Tongue

Keter (Crown) — the highest sefirah in the kabbalistic order, the supernal Crown associated with the Divine Name Ehyeh, which encircles, delimits, and settles the intellect (mochin), standing as a partition below the Ein Sof; linked homiletically to waiting (kattar li ze'eir), silence, and the upper point of the letter alef
'u-mi-Tziyon yisadeka' — verse Psalms 20:3 'from Zion may He support you,' expounded as tziyun (sign): eating and pleasures drawn from the letter-signs marked in every thing

Love (ahavah) — the spiritual quality/emotion of love: the attribute (middah) of Abraham corresponding to Chesed, the attachment of spirit to spirit (love of God and between souls), including 'holy loves' (ahavot di-kedushah); the noun אַהֲבָה, not any other word

"and the priest shall take a fistful" (ve-kamatz ha-kohen, Leviticus 5:12) — the priestly kemitzah, scooping a fistful of the meal-offering, which Likutey Moharan I:54 reads as the aspect of holy love (ahavah di-kedushah)

ruach-mem: Rabbi Nachman's letter-permutation of romach (lance) into ruach (spirit/wind) plus the letter mem — the spirit of life joined to the mem signifying the forty days in which the Torah was given (as in 'the spirit of God hovering over the waters')
've-ruach Elokim merachefet al pnei ha-mayim' — verse Genesis 1:2 'the spirit of God hovered over the waters,' the ruach-mem: the spirit of life residing in the Torah given in 40 days

nodes.he: כשמכה כף אל כף בשעת התפלה
nodes.gloss: clapping palm to palm during prayer — the act of striking one's hands together while praying, a segulah for memory per 'my soul is in my palms always'

the moon (levanah) — the celestial luminary that has no light of its own and receives its illumination from the sun; in Likutey Moharan the paradigm of the receiver (Malkhut, the disciple, Yehoshua, Yitzchak) vis-à-vis the sun/giver
've-tachat raglav ke-maaseh livnat' — verse Exodus 24:10 'under His feet like a pavement of sapphire (livnat),' expounded as levanah (the moon), the lower point/Yehoshua

chirik — the Hebrew vowel point (a single dot written beneath the letter), understood kabbalistically (Tikkunei Zohar, Intro 7a) as the lower dot of the letter Alef, the 'footstool beneath His feet' formed through silence (demimah/shetikah)
've-tachat raglav' — the phrase 'under His feet' (Exodus 24:10) as the chirik vowel-point positioned beneath, in the alef/throne symbolism

darkness (choshech) — the noun denoting absence of light, used as the symbolic aspect opposed to light: deeds of the wicked, the Other Side, death, sorrow, dimmed sight/night, and (paradoxically) the concealing depth of hidden Torah ('He made darkness His secret place'); not the verb 'to withhold' (chasach)

the biblical phrase 'and his eyes were too dim to see' (Genesis 27:1, of Isaac's failing eyesight in old age), cited as a prooftext for the aspect of darkness/night and constricted consciousness (mochin d'katnut)
adam she-baTorah — the 'man' aspect among the four chayot within Torah: 'this is the Torah, a man,' containing lenient and stringent laws (poor and rich)
'zot haTorah adam' — verse Numbers 19:14 'this is the Torah: a man,' prooftext identifying Torah with man, whose lenient/stringent laws parallel poor and wealthy
kelipot surrounding the Supernal Heart — the husks of impurity dwelling around the upper Heart (Jerusalem set amid the nations), subdued through the sage's discourse
'zot Yerushalayim... betokh ha-goyim' — verse Ezekiel 5:5 'this is Jerusalem, I have set her amid the nations,' prooftext for kelipot surrounding the Heart (Jerusalem)

the blemish/defilement of wisdom (pegam ha-chokhmah) — the spiritual flaw caused by failing to use wisdom (e.g., building without seikhel), punished by impoverishment, as in 'the wisdom of the poor man is despised' (Eccl. 9:16)
'chokhmat ha-misken bezuyah' — verse Ecclesiastes 9:16 'the wisdom of the poor man is despised,' signifying the blemish of wisdom punished by impoverishment
one who has blemished his covenant (pegam ha-brit — a person guilty of sexual sin/wasted seed, violating the covenant of circumcision)
'cherev piyot' — 'double-edged sword' (Psalms 149:6, sword of mouths), the prayer-weapon unavailable to one who blemished his covenant, whose waters turned bitter
"yadber amim tachteinu" (Psalms 47:4) — the verse "He subdues peoples beneath us," prooftext for Israel's commandment to wipe out the seed of Amalek (Sanhedrin 20b)
tzaddik elyon — the "upper tzaddik," kabbalistic term for the higher of the two tzaddikim between whom the Shekhinah rests, aspect of "they ascend to heaven"
"ya'alu shamayim" (Psalms 107:26) — the phrase "they go up to the heavens," prooftext identified with the upper tzaddik (as opposed to "they descend to the depths" = lower tzaddik)
"yakem se'arah lidmamah" (Psalms 107:29) — the verse "He stills the storm to a whisper," figure for subduing one's storm-wind (fallen speech of ketz kol basar) under holy speech
katzar milma'lah v'rachav milmatah — the shofar's physical shape, narrow at top and wide at bottom, embodying "from the narrow place I called... answered with expansiveness" (Ps 118:5)

prayers (tefillot, plural of tefillah) — acts of petition and praise directed to God, e.g. the many prayers brought to the tzaddik/Mashiach for elevation or whose abundance brings forgiveness of sin; NOT the homograph tiflut (תִּפְלוּת, frivolity/lewdness)
chamra — Aramaic for donkey (in "karna d'chamra," the donkey's horn of the Athens-elders dialogue), symbol of Yissachar's donkey and of rebuke; not wine
"Yissachar chamor garem" (Genesis 49:14) — Jacob's blessing "Yissachar is a strong-boned donkey," prooftext linking the donkey (chamra) to rebuke/Torah-bearing
"kavod v'lo yidom" (Psalms 30:13) — the phrase "glory, and it shall not be silent," perfected honor achieved by drawing the letter vav (added holiness, shmirat habrit) into kavod, versus kevad-peh
the sun (chammah) — the solar luminary, the radiant giver of light paired with and illuminating the moon (levanah); distinct from chemah 'wrath' and chomah 'wall'

"in the heat of the day" (ke-chom ha-yom, Genesis 18:1) — the scriptural phrase describing Avraham sitting at his tent opening, used as the aspect of Avraham's level of solar heat/kindness, linked to the sun (chamah) and hot bread (the Showbread)
withdrawal/departure of holiness or divine vitality (histalkut) — the removal of the divine presence that leaves an empty void (chalal), as in the desolation caused by desecrating Shabbat
"ki yimatzei chalal ba'adamah" (Deuteronomy 21:1) — the verse "when a slain corpse is found in the land," prooftext linking chalal (corpse/void) to chilul Shabbat and withdrawal of holiness
Shimon — son of Jacob, whose name (from "God heard that I am hated") stands for the hated rebuker; the aspect one lacks when unrectified and unable to rebuke
"ki shama HaShem ki senu'ah anokhi" (Genesis 29:33) — Leah's words at Shimon's naming, "God heard that I am hated," prooftext that the true rebuker is hated
ein hasekhel bishleimut — the deficient state in which the intellect lacks wholeness ("my eyes fail"), causing loss of trust (bitachon) and impaired articulation of speech
"kalu einai" (Psalms 69:4) — the phrase "my eyes fail," eyes standing for the intellect in its unfinished, failing state

"k'mar'eh adam alav milma'lah" (Ezekiel 1:26) — the Merkavah phrase "a likeness as the appearance of a man upon it from above," the man seated on the throne above the firmament formed via the alef's inner vav

emunat chakhamim — faith in the Sages: trust in the Torah authority and guidance of the wise (per Deut. 17:11, 'do not deviate from the matter they tell you, right or left'), enabling clear judgment and restored faith
"lechem cham" (I Samuel 21:7) — "hot bread," i.e., the Showbread (lechem hapanim), heat marking Avraham's chesed of "the heat of the day"

Money / material wealth (mamon) — a person's monetary possessions, riches (ashirut), and livelihood (parnasah), treated in Likutey Moharan as one spiritual category ('a man's money that stands him on his feet'), figured as a wall, face, feet, the left side, etc.; not any homographic word, and distinct from the craving for money (ta'avat mamon) as a vice, which appears only as a partner concept here
"bread from heaven" (Exodus 16:4) — the manna, heavenly sustenance given without toil; emblem of effortless livelihood (parnassah beli torach) attained through tikkun ha-brit
"likro khulam b'shem HaShem" (Zephaniah 3:9) — the phrase "that all call upon the Name of God," identified with faith (emunah) that perfects the letters/speech into a "pure language"
it'aruta dil'eila — Aramaic kabbalistic term for "arousal from Above," divine-initiated awakening, aspect of "Who is like You among the mighty, O God"
"mi khamokha ba'eilim HaShem" (Exodus 15:11) — the Song-at-the-Sea verse "Who is like You among the mighty," prooftext for it'aruta dil'eila (arousal from Above)

the Evil Inclination (yetzer hara) — the personified inner drive toward evil that entices a person to sin (opposed to the yetzer tov), identified in Likutey Moharan with strict judgment, folly ('the old and foolish king'), and the kingdom of the Sitra Achra
"melekh zaken u'khsil" (Ecclesiastes 4:13) — the "old and foolish king," Talmudic epithet for the yetzer hara, malkhut of the Sitra Achra that spurns wisdom
kol hatekiot — the audible sound of the shofar blasts (tekiah-shevarim-teruah), which breaks the body's brazenness, aspect of the voice of sighing
"mikol anchati" (Psalms 102:6) — the phrase "from the voice of my sighing," the groan-sound identified with the shofar blasts that shatter the body

"He stretches out the heavens like a curtain" (noteh shamayim ka-yeri'ah, Psalms 104:2) — the scriptural phrase describing God spreading the heavens, expounded in Likutey Moharan I:54 as the aspect of the unification of the Tzaddik and Knesset Yisrael, manifested in business dealings (masa u'matan)
"nirgan mafrid aluf" (Proverbs 16:28) — "a whisperer separates the intimate friend," prooftext for slanderers and quarrel-makers (regel/meraglim wordplay) who divide man from fellow and God

the revealed Torah (torah she-be-nigleh) — the exoteric, openly-taught dimension of Torah (Scripture, halakhah, Talmud) accessible to all, contrasted with the hidden/esoteric Torah (nistar, sitrei oraita)
"ayin b'ayin" (Numbers 14:14) — the phrase "eye to eye," standing for the revealed dimension of Torah (nigleh), linked to Mordekhai/omer

point (nekudah) — the concentrated dot/point of wisdom in Likutey Moharan 34: graphically the yud, symbolizing Chokhmah as a wellspring that illuminates outward (into the vav/Binah), and the unique good point present in each person; not nikkud as a mere vowel-sign, nor the verb 'to punctuate'
"pi yedaber chokhmot" (Psalms 49:4) — "my mouth shall speak wisdom," the illuminated point (nekudah) activated by speaking privately before one's Creator
haTorah hakedoshah — our holy Torah itself, aspect of "pesal lekha," contrasted with the counterfeit torahs (pesilim/idols) of the Sitra Achra
"pesal lekha" (Exodus 34:1) — God's command "carve for yourself [two tablets]," wordplay (pesal/pesolet/pesilim) marking the holy Torah against the idol-torahs of the Other Side
Yesod d'Atzilut — the sefirah Yesod within the world of Atzilut, where the light of Chesed remained after the Breaking of the Vessels; "tzaddik yesod olam"
tamar bikdushah — the date-palm on the side of holiness, "the tzaddik flourishes like the palm" (Ps 92:13), opposed to the tamar/kotevet-date of the Sitra Achra (leaven, harsh judgments)

the scriptural phrase "Tzaddik katamar yifrach" — "The righteous one shall flourish like a date-palm" (Psalms 92:13), cited as the aspect of the holy date-palm (tamar of holiness) and of the sweetening of harsh judgments
the Supernal Heart (Lev HaElyon) — the divine upper heart, source of warm speech and Torah explanations, identified with 'Rock of my heart' (Ps. 73:26), opened through prayer to bestow words of Torah

"Tzur levavi" — the phrase "Rock of my heart" from Psalms 73:26 (צוּר from the root meaning rock/stone, not צור as besiege or form), denoting the heart in its aspect of rock/stone: read as the Supernal Heart that is the rock-source of speech, and as the stony heart that must be turned to water (per "who turns the rock into a pool of water")

healing of the soul (refu'at ha-nefesh) — the spiritual cure and restoration of the nefesh, effected through Torah wisdom, which sweetens judgment and returns the soul to its root (as opposed to bodily healing)
"shemesh tzedakah u'marpei bikhnafeha" (Malachi 3:20) — "a sun of righteousness with healing in its wings," healing of the soul via Jacob/Chokhmah, mochin d'gadlut

hairs (se'arot, שְׂעָרוֹת with sin) — bodily/head hairs, understood kabbalistically as motrei mochin, the surplus overflow of the mentalities/brains; distinct from she'arim 'gates' (שְׁעָרִים), though Rabbi Nachman links the two by wordplay

"the gates of Zion" (sha'arei Tziyon, Psalms 87:2) — the scriptural phrase for Zion's gates, expounded in Likutey Moharan I:20 via the sha'ar/se'ar wordplay as the aspect of hairs (nimin) and linked to 'the staff of Your strength sent from Zion'

"shifkhi libekh kamayim nokhach pnei HaShem" (Lamentations 2:19) — "pour out your heart like water before God's face," the "water" of heart-outpouring prayer in the Athens-elders riddle of distance from water

Kisses (neshikin) — the kabbalistic/Zoharic term for kisses as the mystical union of spirit with spirit (hitdabkut rucha be-rucha); in Likutey Moharan I:12, the spiritual kiss whereby the spirit of the Tanna cleaves to the spirit of one who studies his Oral Torah rulings in holiness (Yaakov kissing Rachel; 'his lips are lilies'). Not a physical kiss per se, nor any homograph of the root נש"ק (e.g., weaponry, nesheq).

"His lips are lilies" (Song of Songs 5:13) — the scriptural phrase שִׂפְתוֹתָיו שׁוֹשַׁנִּים, invoked as the aspect of kisses (neshikin) and the cleaving of spirit to spirit, linked to the upper lips (supernal Netzach and Hod) arousing union

the absence/privation of speech (he'der ha-dibbur) — the state of speech being withheld or lacking, silence as the negation of the faculty of speech; in LM I:60 the aspect of the tekiah shofar-blast, contrasted with teruah as speech
"taka'ta lazar kapekha nokashta b'imrei fikha" (Proverbs 6:1–2) — "you struck your hands for a stranger, are snared by your mouth's words," prooftext making tekiah the aspect of absence of speech

the supernal Eden (Eden Ila'ah) — the upper, hidden Eden of Kabbalah, identified with supernal Wisdom (Chokhmah Ila'ah), the 'father,' the hidden realm, and the aspect of 'we will hear' (nishma) and prayer, as opposed to the lower Eden (Eden Tata'ah)

Father (Av/Abba) — the paternal principle in Kabbalah denoting Chokhmah, supernal wisdom: the partzuf Abba paired with Imma (Binah), and 'father' as the intellect/higher level ('av b'chokhmah', supernal Eden, the complete utterance) relative to the son; not a biological father as such

forgetfulness (shikhchah) — the noun denoting the state or force of forgetting, the loss of memory/awareness (especially of Torah learning and of the World to Come), opposed to zikaron (memory/remembrance)
aveidah — a lost object: the prenatal teaching forgotten at birth, which one must seek back by traveling to the tzaddik (the forgetter is called "one who loses," Avot 5)

the Hebrew letter shin (ש), the three-headed letter interpreted homiletically — its three branches/heads symbolizing triads (e.g., the three divisions of thought, the three Patriarchs as the shin of 'Shabbat'), and serving as the numeral 300

the Patriarchs (Avot) — Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov as forefathers of Israel, embodying the sefirot Chesed, Gevurah, and Tiferet (not the tractate Pirkei Avot, and not 'fathers' in a generic biological sense)
hirhurim shel niuf — lustful/adulterous thoughts, the "father of fathers of impurity" (avi avot hatum'ah), aspect of a corpse, from which charity saves ("tzedakah saves from death")

avi avot ha-tum'ah — the halakhic term 'father of fathers of impurity,' the supreme grade of ritual defilement (classically the corpse), here the ultimate source of impurity identified with death and adulterous thoughts
sitra dimsa'ava — Aramaic "side of impurity," the defiled Other Side (embodied in Avimelekh) from which scoffers claimed Isaac's judgment-nature derived, God forbid
Avimelekh — the Philistine king of Gerar, whom the generation's scoffers claimed impregnated Sarah; emblem of the impure side (sitra dimsa'ava) as a false source of Isaac's din

Truth (emet) — the divine attribute and spiritual quality of truthfulness/veracity, the aspect of Jacob ('titen emet le-Yaakov'), opposed to falsehood (sheker), through which one attains faith, blessing, and God's indwelling presence

the tzaddik of the generation (tzaddik ha-dor) — the singular preeminent righteous leader of each generation, an aspect of Moshe/Mashiach, foundation of the world and channel who elevates Israel's prayers and nurtures them with his Torah

Even Shetiyah — the Foundation Stone in the Holy of Holies of the Temple, the rock from which the world was founded (nishtat), used as the aspect of the supernal source (the tzaddik of the generation / Holy of Holies) from which the world is established and judgments are sweetened

the Holy of Holies — the innermost sanctum of the Temple containing the Foundation Stone (Even Shetiyah), used as the aspect of the supreme locus of holiness from which all judgments are sweetened (not the sacrificial category 'most-holy offerings')
stones (avanim, plural of even) — physical rocks used as a symbol: the stones of Yaakov/the Foundation Stone identified homiletically with souls (lm1:61) and with the letters/words of speech (lm2:79)
Abraham (Avraham) the biblical patriarch, who in Likutey Moharan embodies chesed (lovingkindness), love (ahavah), faith, and the 'right side' — the archetype of the attribute of loving devotion
"be'er mayim chayim" — the well of living water, one of the three bounties Moshe drew down; aspect of Avraham, waters of chesed, who began digging wells

"Sixty are the queens" (shishim hemah melakhot) — the scriptural phrase from Song of Songs 6:8, where melakhot means 'queens' (not 'kingdoms'), expounded in Likutey Moharan I:15 as the aspect of Avraham/Chesed and linked to the letter samekh (numerical value sixty) and the 'sixty houses' of Hagronya
ilan — the tree (Aramaic ilana) in which the bird perched in the Talmudic tale; per Maharsha, the aspect of Avraham's eshel-planting, the thread of chesed shielding from the serpent

a limb of the Shekhinah (אֵיבָר מֵהַשְּׁכִינָה) — an individual organ/member of the Divine Presence, the aspect that each person's prayer constitutes, corresponding to the limbs of the Tabernacle (Likutey Moharan I:2)
evrei haMishkan — the limbs/components of the Tabernacle: each individual prayer is a limb of the Shekhinah, which together are the Mishkan's limbs

Adam / man — the archetypal human being (אָדָם), the pinnacle of creation identified with Torah ("zot ha-Torah adam"), speech, Israel, and the Divine name Havayah spelled with alfin (gematria 45 = מ"ה); the status one attains through tzedakah and fasting ("na'aseh adam"), and the first man paired with Chava. Not the color-word אָדֹם ('red'), the nation אֱדוֹם, or the participle מְדַבֵּר ('speaker').

tzedakah — charitable giving; the act of giving money/alms to the poor or to the deserving (the mitzvah of charity, צְדָקָה), as a spiritual practice and rectification; not the abstract quality of righteousness (צֶדֶק) nor a proper name

Fasting (ta'anit) — the religious-ascetic practice of abstaining from eating and drinking as a devotional act, which weakens the body's four elements, subdues the liver/anger before the brain, breaks the craving for food, elicits peace and joy, and rectifies speech; equated with tzedakah ('the reward of the fast is charity') and likened to the World to Come, in which there is no eating or drinking. Not the Talmudic tractate Ta'anit, and not affliction/suffering in general.

Israel — the Jewish people as a collective spiritual entity (Knesset Yisrael), the nation called 'adam,' bearers/supporters of the Torah; not the patriarch Jacob as an individual, nor the Land of Israel
the letter Alef — whose inner vav is the firmament (fire-and-water heavens, totality of colors/shame), forming the "man upon the throne"; adam = alef + dom (silence)

the man seated upon the Throne — the anthropomorphic figure of Ezekiel's Merkavah vision ('a likeness as the appearance of a man upon it from above,' Ezek. 1:26), the supernal Adam enthroned above the firmament, whom Rebbe Nachman identifies variously with the perfected Alef/silence and with the Da'at of the sage

Adonai — the Divine Name אֲדֹנָי (numerical value 65), denoting God's Lordship/Malkhut, identified with divine speech per "Adonai, open my lips" (Ps. 51:17); not the plural/possessive 'my lords' (אֲדֹנַי) nor the sockets of the Tabernacle (אֲדָנָיו/אֲדָנִים)
Shabbat u'brit — the pair Shabbat and the covenant (brit), the faith-sources (the "skeins" of the Athens-elders well riddle) by which sustenance is drawn inward as Showbread

will/desire (ratzon) — the faculty of volition and yearning, both the Divine will and the human will/longing directed toward God, identified as an aspect of soul (nefesh), love, glory, and yearning (kisufin)

oneness (echad) — the number/attribute "one" as divine unity, per "HaShem is One and His Name is One" (Zech. 14:9): the undifferentiated unity of kindness and judgment that is entirely good (gematria of ahavah, love); not the ordinal "first" nor the pronoun "someone"
reproach/disgrace (ḥerpah) — verbal shame and humiliation inflicted on a person, identified via Genesis 34:14 with the foreskin (orlah); not ḥoref (winter) or the verb le-ḥaref
ahavah nefulah — 'fallen love': love broken/degraded into evil loves via the shattering of the vessels, equated with disgrace and the foreskin of the heart (Gen 34:14)
shoresh ha-chasadim she-ba-Da'at — kabbalistic root of the Chasadim (kindnesses) within the sefirah Da'at, the source from which illumination is drawn in the lulav kavvanot
ahavah she-ba-Da'at — the supernal love located in Da'at, above time and the middot, in which Chesed is rooted

"Be silent before the LORD" (dom la-Hashem, Psalms 37:7) — the scriptural phrase of silent stillness/submission before God, which Likutey Moharan 6 links to repentance, the hollowed heart, Ehyeh, and Keter (not the noun dam, 'blood')

Ehyeh (אֶהְיֶה, "I Will Be") — the Divine Name of Exodus 3:14, often written euphemistically as אקי"ה; associated in Kabbalah with the sefirah Keter and, in Likutey Moharan 6, with repentance (teshuvah) and silence — the state of "I am ready to be" (אנא זמין למהוי), potential existence prior to actualization. Not the ordinary first-person future verb "I will be" in mundane usage.
the person who keeps silent (macharish) under insult — an action-state through which one attains the aspect of the Name Ehyeh (Ps 50:21)
kodem ha-teshuvah — the temporal state 'before repentance,' when Ehyeh remains hidden since one has not yet prepared himself to exist
Ehyeh in hastarat panim — the divine Name Ehyeh ('I will be') concealed from a person prior to teshuvah, its face hidden from him

firmament (rakia) — the outstretched heavenly expanse/sky of Genesis 1:6 that divides and screens; homiletically the vav within the letter Alef, a tent-like dividing surface, and the aspect of obstacles/screens and of the soul
ohel — the Tent (of Meeting, from which Yehoshua departed not; Ex 33:11), symbolizing the firmament stretched 'like a tent' (Isa 40:22), the vav within the letter alef
be-ne'emnei — 'the faithful [of the land]' (Ps 101:6), midrashically identified as Aharon the priest, aspect of mishpat/judgment

Aharon (Aaron) the High Priest, brother of Moshe — the biblical personage who in Likutey Moharan embodies the aspects of judgment (mishpat, per 'And Aharon shall bear the judgment of the Children of Israel'), faithfulness, and the right side (yemina) opposite Korach's left
the wise men (chachamim) — Torah sages/scholars, the bearers of wisdom (as opposed to any other sense of the root ח-כ-ם, e.g. the abstract quality of wisdom itself)
avvazei — the geese of Rabbah bar bar Chanah's desert tale (Bava Batra 73b), dream-symbol of wisdom ('one who sees a goose in a dream anticipates chokhmah,' Berakhot 57a)
one's enemies falling before him — the defeat of accusers/adversaries achieved through fasting, which nullifies the liver-anger that arouses Esav/Edom the accuser

nodes.he: כל מה שמרבה לתן צדקה ליותר אנשים
nodes.gloss: the practice of giving tzedakah to ever more people — each additional recipient enlarges the expanse of still, pure air formed by mutual love
acquiring friends and lovers through charity — tzedakah as 'storing up souls' (Munbaz, Bava Batra 11a), gaining ohavim whose love purifies the air

the air of the Land of Israel (avira de-Eretz Yisrael) — the Aramaic term for the holy atmosphere of the Land of Israel that makes one wise, identified in Likutey Moharan 37 with the sinless holy breath (hevel she-ein bo chet) of schoolchildren's Torah, through which the patriarchs are revealed and prophecy/ruach ha-kodesh is received
the ability to sing and thank God ('azamrah le-Elokai be-odi,' Ps 146:2) — praise made possible by the 'od,' the remaining good point one finds in oneself

light (or, luminosity/illumination) — the noun 'light' as in the light of creation and of day, opposed to darkness (chosech); the aspect associated with glory, day, and the deeds of the tzaddikim; not fire, skin (עוֹר), or the place-name Ur

day (yom, יוֹם) — the daytime/period of light named by God in Genesis 1:5 ('And God called the light day'), expounded in Likutey Moharan I:14 as the aspect of light and hence of domestic peace (shalom bayit), in the phrase 'le-yom chageinu'

the returning/reflected light (or ha-chozer) — the kabbalistic-optical counterpart of direct light (or ha-yashar): the power of sight that strikes the seen object and rebounds back to the eyes, forming the image and enabling perception/knowledge (as in 'from afar He knows')
'mi-merchak yeda' — 'He knows from afar' (Ps 138:6), scriptural phrase denoting or chozer, the reflected/returning light of perception

Yir'ah — fear/awe of Heaven: the devotional quality of reverence before God (identified in Likutey Moharan with Malkhut, earth, prayer, and the vessel that receives blessing); the noun יִרְאָה, not the verb יִרְאֶה 'he will see' and not רֵאָה 'lung'

the direct light (or ha-yashar) — the outward-extending ray/emanation, as in the power of sight extending from the eyes to the seen object, contrasted with the returning/reflected light (or ha-chozer)

nodes.he: כח התפשטות הראות מעיניו להדבר הנראה
nodes.gloss: the outgoing extension of the visual ray from the eyes to the seen object — the optical model of or yashar, direct light
the light that shines to a person toward teshuvah — divine illumination (linked to Shaddai/'enough') that awakens him to return

"Vayichan penei ha'ir" (Genesis 33:18) — the phrase 'and he [Jacob] encamped before / graced the face of the city,' read midrashically (Shabbat 33b: Jacob instituted coinage) as denoting the shining of the face upon the city and the rectification of the coin/money-craving
faith in God's divinity (emunat Elokut) — belief in the Godhead, which shines as the light of the divine countenance and rectifies the craving for money, opposite of the darkness of idolatry
Jacob (Yaakov), the biblical patriarch — third of the forefathers, son of Isaac, embodying in Likutey Moharan the aspects of intellect/wisdom, truth, tiferet, and related qualities

nodes.he: מתביש ביותר, ונתגלה הבושה על פניו
nodes.gloss: the state of intense shame visibly revealed on one's face — embarrassment before the King that manifests after knowledge grows
or ha-tefillin — the 'light of the tefillin,' the radiance on the face identified with holy shame/bushah revealed upon the countenance

"He wraps [Himself in] light as a garment" (Psalms 104:2) — the scriptural phrase describing God enveloped in light, expounded in LM1:54 as the aspect of full light attained through contentment (histapkut)
or malei — 'full light,' the complete spelling of me'orot attained by the contented tzaddik ('wraps in light as a garment,' Ps 104:2), opposite the deficient me'erat of the wicked

the Zoharic dictum "he is a sign (ot) within His host" — reading the Divine Name Tzeva'ot as tzava + ot, i.e. the tzaddik is the distinguishing sign/letter within God's host, linked to the sign of the covenant
the sign of the covenant (ot brit) — circumcision as the covenantal mark borne by the tzaddik, identifying him as a distinguished 'sign' (ot) within God's host

The Hebrew letter dalet (ד), fourth letter of the alphabet with numerical value four — as a symbolic entity in Likutey Moharan denoting Malkhut, which 'has nothing (de-leit) of her own,' and standing for fourfold structures (four kingdoms, four cups, four species, fourfold song, four corners/wings); the letter itself, not the homograph דֶּלֶת 'door'
the Four Species (lulav, etrog, myrtle, willow) of Sukkot — the festival's fourfold set paralleling the four cups and fourfold Mishnah review
the Four Cups of wine at the Pesach seder — Pesach's instance of the fourfold pattern present in each pilgrimage festival
hevel peh — the breath of the mouth, symbol of the letter Heh (vs. the voice as vav) in Torah study and prayer
the Hebrew letter Heh (ה, fifth letter of the alphabet), as a mystical symbol — e.g. the heh of the divine Name (as in Avraham's added heh, the heh-filling of Havayah, or the breath of the mouth)
da'at Hashem — knowledge of God Himself (beyond human knowledge), the aspect of the letter heh; lacking it one is a 'minor' who cannot beget

completeness/perfection of da'at — the perfected state of holy knowledge and awareness of God (the construct phrase שְׁלֵמוּת הַדַּעַת, 'wholeness of the mind/knowledge'), associated with the letter heh, achieved through answering the questions of converts/students, and sustained via the lung and breath
Tzeva'ot — the divine Name 'of Hosts,' expounded as 'He is an ot (sign/letter) within His host'
Yetzirah, the kabbalistic World of Formation — third of the four worlds (Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah), corresponding to the letter Vav of the Divine Name and to the weekdays
the drawing-down (hamshakhah) from intellect to fear of God — the connecting flow symbolized by the letter vav, the diagonal stroke of the alef

Binah (Understanding) — the kabbalistic sefirah of comprehension and discursive understanding, the supernal 'Mother' (Imma) that receives and expands the point of Chokhmah (likened to a river flowing from the wellspring, the heart, wine, the sukkah, the letter heh of Y-H); also the corresponding cognitive faculty of understanding what one studies
ha-olam — the created world itself, aspect of the letter vav since it was created in six days (paired with Torah as yud)
vavei ha-amudim — 'the hooks of the pillars' (Ex 27:10), title for Israel as supporters of the Torah, embodying the letter vav
supporters of Torah (Aramaic 'tamchei oraita') — those who uphold and materially sustain the Torah and its scholars, likened to the hooks/pillars supporting it

staff/club (makel; Aramaic alvata) — the rod engraved with Divine Names ('Ehyeh') used to strike the wave in Rabbah bar bar Chanah's tale, identified by Rabbi Nachman with the shape of the letter vav and with Torah study that beats down the yetzer hara; a wooden striking-stick, not any other sense of the letters מקל

the Hebrew letter yud (yod) — the smallest letter, a single point, numerical value ten — invoked as a symbolic aspect (of Chokhmah/wisdom, the primal point/wellspring, Torah, the tzaddik, the World to Come, the ten types of melody, holiness); NOT the word יָד 'hand' or the ordinal 'tenth' as a number-word
Aseret ha-Dibrot — the Ten Commandments, the yud-point of the melupum vowel atop the six-by-six Tablets (vav)

the perfection/completion of the letters (shlemut ha-otiyot) — the wholeness of the Hebrew letters through which the worlds were created, achieved via the yud, the final point completing each letter's form; identified in Likutey Moharan I:18 with the purpose of all created things and the World to Come

"the doors of my womb" (daltei vitni, Job 3:10) — the two doors of the woman's womb, identified with the placenta/afterbirth (shilya) where the fetus rests, whose two dalet-letters form the closed mem
mem setumah — the closed final-mem letterform composed of the womb's two dalet-doors (Job 3:10), chamber of the fetus and the 40 days of its formation

circle / roundness (Aramaic igula, Hebrew iggul) — the geometric-kabbalistic figure of the encompassing circle, contrasted with the square (ribu'a); e.g., the round letter samekh, the numerical sixty, encircling paths (ma'agalim), and surrounding faith

the Hebrew letter samekh (סָמֶ״ךְ), fifteenth letter of the alphabet with numerical value sixty and a closed circular shape, expounded homiletically (e.g., as the circle/iggula, the sixty queens, and the root of 'samkhuni'/support)
'samkhuni' — 'sustain me' (Song 2:5), word expounded as the letter samekh (support), aspect of prayer
ha-olamot — the worlds that fell in the shattering of the vessels at creation, which are constituted of letters scattered into sparks
letters (otiyot) — the twenty-two letters of the Hebrew alphabet as the building blocks of holy speech, Torah, and creation (not 'signs/miracles', otot)
wife of (eshet, construct state of ishah 'woman/wife'), expounded homiletically as an acronym/aspect — e.g. the letters of faith or prayer signified by 'the wife of'
subduing one's evil inclination (kofeh et yitzro) — the act that makes the rav 'like an angel of Hashem Tzeva'ot,' a mighty one who does His word

the thirty-two occurrences of the Divine Name Elokim in the Genesis account of Creation (ma'aseh bereishit), the supernal source ('lev'=32) from which the letters in all created things are drawn and from which the heart is nourished
the letters present within every created thing — deriving from the 32 'Elokim' of the creation account, source of the heart's (lev=32) illumination
shevirah — the kabbalistic Breaking of the Vessels, understood as letters that shattered and fell into every thing of this world
the eleven spices of the ketoret (incense) — symbol of the holy sparks rising from among the idolatrous nations, linked to cutting off Amalek's seed
kesher shel tefillin — the knot of the head-tefillin at the back, what Moshe was shown as God's 'back' (Berakhot 7a)
achorai — 'My back' (Ex 33:23), the divine hind-aspect revealed to Moshe, identified with the tefillin knot

Acher ("the Other"), the epithet of Elisha ben Avuyah, the Talmudic sage-turned-heretic who "cut the saplings" after seeing the angel Metatron seated and erring to posit two authorities (Chagigah 14b–15b) — not the ordinary adjective אַחֵר meaning "other/another"

nodes.he: מי שמתקרב להצדיק ומקצץ בנטיעות וכופר בכל
nodes.gloss: the disciple who draws near the tzaddik yet 'cuts the saplings' and denies all — the heretic-type of Acher (Elisha ben Avuyah), with filth in his heart

din — divine judgment/severity: the kabbalistic attribute of strict judgment (Gevurah), the constricting harsh force opposed to mercy (rachamim/chesed), associated with the name Elohim, Malkhut, and Isaac (not a courtroom lawsuit, legal ruling, or the verb 'to judge')

"After the things/words" (achar ha-devarim, Genesis 22:1) — the biblical phrase homiletically read as speech that comes after (i.e., precedes or lacks) thought, symbolizing constricted consciousness (mochin de-katnut) and stern judgments; not the ordinary narrative sense of 'afterward'

"the end of all flesh" (ketz kol basar, Genesis 6:13) — the destructive force / great accuser that brings an end to all flesh, identified in Likutey Moharan 38 with the stormy wind (ruach se'arah), the serpent's contamination, and "after the things," which sucks vitality from unrectified speech
shayish tahor — the 'pure marble' of the Pardes ascent (Chagigah 14b), symbol of existence after actualization (yesh), when 'pure' applies

"after the actualization" (achar ha-pe'ulah) — the state following the act of Creation, in which reality has emerged from potentiality into actual, independent existence (yesh), the stage at which the term "pure" (tahor) becomes applicable; contrasted with "before the actualization," when all existed only in potential within the divine Oneness (LM I:51, on "pure marble")

the End of Days (acharit ha-yamim) — the eschatological final era of history, the biblical phrase for the ultimate future/messianic end-time (as in Jeremiah's 'hope for your future' and Jacob's 'end of days'), used by Rabbi Nachman as the aspect of faith and of the temporal 'end' (keitz)

speech with knowledge (dibbur be-de'ah) — spoken words of Torah/prayer uttered with conscious understanding and da'at, contrasted with 'speech without knowledge' (stammered, uncomprehended words); in Likutey Moharan I:74 identified with Simchat Torah, Jacob, tzedakah, and the Tree of Healing (ilana de-asvata)

the tree of healing (Aramaic 'ilana d'asvata', Zoharic term): the Tree of Life planted above through Torah study, which is entirely healing — identified with Torah/speech-with-knowledge as remedy for the soul
lo — the word 'not' (Jer 23:24) as symbol of ayin, nothingness/naught, God's self-showing in humility to the one who hides himself in lowliness

Ayin (אַיִן) — 'Nothingness' as a kabbalistic noun: the divine no-thing-ness / self-nullification preceding creation, identified with true humility and inclusion in the Ein Sof (as in 'wisdom is found from ayin'); not the ordinary negation particle אֵין ('there is not')

humility (anavah) — the character trait of self-effacement and lowliness before God, the opposite of arrogance (gadlut/ga'avah); in Likutey Moharan the bechinah of ayin (nothingness), prerequisite for Torah, awe of God, holy honor, kingship, and guarding the covenant
gai (גיא) — 'the valley' where Moses was buried (Deut 34:6), read as bittul/ayin (self-nullification into nothingness) via Isaiah 40:4 'every valley shall be raised'; not gei as mere topography

Moses (Moshe Rabbeinu), the biblical prophet and leader of Israel, treated as the archetype of the true tzaddik/leader of the generation — the aspect of da'at (knowledge), prophecy, humility (ayin), and faithful shepherd (raya mehemna)

doing the mitzvot with joy (asiyat ha-mitzvot b'simchah) — the devotional practice/state of joyful mitzvah-performance, linked to the thought's pursuit of the Ein Sof light in 'reaching and not reaching'

the state 'before creation' (kodem ha-beriah) — the primordial reality preceding the created order, identified with the Ein Sof and the 'beginning,' where the complete utterance/prayer inheres, as opposed to the created worlds which are only a half utterance
oneg Shabbat — the mitzvah-state of Sabbath delight, whose holy eating accomplishes what fasting does (subduing the liver/enemy), rendering fasts unnecessary
galgalta d'mocha atum b'tum'ah — Aramaic kabbalistic image of the skull (galgalta) enclosing the brain being sealed/blocked by ritual impurity, so the voice cannot resound as thunder
ein kolo nishma — the state of 'his voice is not heard': one's prayer-voice fails to resound as thunder because the skull/brain is blocked by impurity (per Berakhot 24b idiom)
ein kashin lo mezonotav — the reward-state that one's livelihood does not come with difficulty: sustenance without toil, earned by honest business dealings that make Heaven's Name beloved

Divine lifting/showing of the face (nesi'ut panim) — God's gracious countenance and show of favor, as in the priestly blessing 'May Hashem lift His face toward you' (Berakhot 20b); the opposite of hastarat panim (concealment of the face), attained by breaking the lust for eating and linked to the illumination of truth

nodes.he: אין שום פקידות ושררה להעזי פנים
nodes.gloss: the condition that the brazen-faced (azei panim) hold no appointment or authority — denial of office/serarah to the impudent, dependent on restored holy Malkhut/honor

one who pursues honor — a person who actively chases after his own honor/glory (kavod), who thereby (per Likutey Moharan I:6) attains not the honor of God but only the scrutinized 'honor of kings,' inviting investigation and dispute against himself

nodes.he: אינו עושה צל, ומקבל אור השם יתברך
nodes.gloss: casting no shadow and receiving God's light — the state of one whose deeds make no 'shadow' blocking the ever-flowing divine light, so no lack (children, livelihood, health) befalls him

man (ish) — the male partner in the man/woman (ish/ishah) pair, used as the symbolic masculine principle representing the Holy One / Mordekhai / love / truth in union with the feminine (Shekhinah / Esther / fear / faith); not 'fire' (esh) or a personal name
'this counsel' (etzah zot) — Rabbi Nachman's specific advice of finding God's light even in darkness/descents (exits through the openings of another's fall), enabling lifelong integrity

nodes.he: איש כשר באמת כל ימי חייו
nodes.gloss: ish kasher be'emet kol yemei chayav — the state of being a truly upright/kosher person one's whole life, attained by ever reviving oneself through the truth that is God's own light

eating — the act of consuming food (the verbal noun akhilah), treated as a spiritual practice whose sanctity or kashrut affects the intellect, unifications, and the kelipot; not a specific food item or meal
'teref natan lire'av' (Ps 111:5) — the verse 'He gave prey/food to those who fear Him,' linked to the altar in the portion of Binyamin 'the ravener' (toref); emblem of eating in kashrut/holiness

converts/proselytes (gerim) — non-Jews who come to convert to Judaism, understood by Rabbi Nachman as sparks of holiness (fallen faith, swallowed vitality) extracted from the Other Side and returned to holiness; not the homograph גָּרִים 'dwelling/residing'

Da'at — the noun "knowledge/awareness" as the unifying mental faculty and sefirah of Knowledge: holy consciousness that joins Chesed and Gevurah (the five kindnesses and five strengths) into oneness, associated with Moshe, the Temple, Shabbat, peace, and the manna; not any verbal form of the root יד"ע nor the plural דעות
the triad of eating, drinking, and garments (akhilah, shetiyah, malbushim) — the three bodily provisions all contained within and flowing from da'at of the Torah (manna, well, clouds of glory)

Matzah — the unleavened Passover bread (contrasted with chametz/leaven), expounded homiletically for its spelling with hei and its wordplay link to strife (matsuta/merivah), speech, and pure unleavened consciousness
Birkat ha-Mazon — the Grace after Meals blessings, by which food is blessed through arousing and illuminating the holy letters (of the 32 Elokim of Creation) present in the food

the laughter of the fool (sechok ha-kesil, cf. Ecclesiastes 7:6) — the hollow, mocking merriment of the kesil identified in Tikkunei Zohar (Tikkun 3) with the spleen/Lilith, mother of the Erev Rav, i.e. the 'other god' who laughs with the wicked through worldly wealth and then kills them
el acher — 'the other god,' the idolatrous demonic power identified in Tikkunei Zohar with the fool's laughter/spleen/Lilith, mother of the Erev Rav; not the word 'other' generically

the Shekhinah — the indwelling Divine Presence, the feminine immanent aspect of God identified in Kabbalah with the sefirah Malkhut, which suffers exile and is unified with the Holy One, blessed be He

Elohim — the Divine Name E-l-h-i-m (אֱלֹהִים), God as manifested in the attribute of judgment (din/gevurah); in Likutey Moharan the bechina associated with Malkhut, fear, and constricted consciousness (katnut ha-mochin) — not the generic noun for 'gods' or 'judges'
katnut ha-mochin — constricted consciousness/immature mentalities, the stagnant mind-state of the divine name Elokim and stern judgments, opposite of renewal of mind

Isaac (Yitzchak), the biblical patriarch, son of Abraham — treated in Likutey Moharan as the archetype of Gevurah/holy judgment (din), constricted consciousness, and laughter/joy (from the root tz-ch-k), and via letter-play (keitz chai) as an allusion to time

mochin d'katnut — constricted/immature consciousness; the kabbalistic state of diminished mental faculties (mochin) associated with harsh judgments (dinim), confusion, forgetfulness, and spiritual sleep, opposite of mochin d'gadlut (expanded consciousness)

"His Name" (shemo) — God's Name as in "the Lord is One and His Name is One" (Zech. 14:9), denoting the divine Name as distinct from YHVH itself; identified in Likutey Moharan I:4 with Elohim, the aspect of judgment, and with Malkhut (via "David made a name", II Sam. 8)
panim d'Sitra Achra — the 'faces of the Other Side': dark countenances (anpin chashokhin) of melancholy and idolatry ('other gods upon My face'), borne by those sunk in money-craving

"other gods" (elohim acherim) — the biblical term for false deities/idolatry from Exodus 20:3, used as the demonic-idolatrous aspect of the Sitra Achra, associated with darkness and the craving for money

machaloket — dispute, strife, controversy; the state of division/quarrel between parties (or contradictory ideas), opposed to peace (shalom); as in 'dispute for the sake of Heaven' and the dispute of tzaddikim. Not the sense of an administrative division/section (machleket) or priestly watch (machlokot).
'these waters' — the waters of dispute/machaloket, the Mei Merivah (waters of strife, Num 20:13), the peleg-channel from which controversy and its resulting books of questions-and-answers flow
alfei (in Ps 68:18 'alfei shin'an') — 'thousands' read as the alufei (chieftains) of Esav, the impure powers nullified through receiving of the Torah

the chieftains of Esav (alufei Esav, Genesis 36) — the tribal chiefs of Esav, rendered by Onkelos as 'ravrevei Esav' (the great ones of Esav), representing the 'rav of the kelipah,' the leader-figure of the side of impurity from whom the wicked draw their spirit

the 'rav of the kelipah' (רַב דִּקְלִפָּה) — the false master/leader belonging to the husk of impurity, the unholy counterpart of the true tzaddik-teacher, identified with Esav ('yesh li rav') and the chieftains of Esav, from whom the wicked receive their spirit of impurity
nashin shapirin — Aramaic 'beautiful women' whom R. Shimon bar Yochai saw and called 'idols' (Zohar Kedoshim), emblem of lustful thoughts as idolatrous folly
elilim — 'idols' of Lev 19:4 ('turn not to the idols'), applied by R. Shimon bar Yochai to beautiful women: lustful fantasies equated with idol-worship's madness

silence (shetikah) — the noun for keeping silent / restraint of speech: remaining quiet in the face of insult and disgrace, and the meta-verbal stillness above speech (as in 'a fence for wisdom is silence'); not stillness of matter or any homograph
ilmim — 'the mute/silent ones': silence (shetikah) personified as muteness, the guarded restraint of speech as a spiritual practice/state
em — 'mother' as title of the tzaddik of the generation, who nurses Israel with the milk of his Torah (Song 4:11 'honey and milk under your tongue'); not the conditional word 'im'

nodes.he: אם זוכה יכול לקבל פי שנים
nodes.gloss: 'if he merits, he can receive double' — the Elisha-like opportunity at a tzaddik's passing to receive pi shenayim (a twofold portion) of his revealed descending spirit
returning people in teshuvah — the tzaddik's action of bringing others to repentance, equated with 'extracting the precious from the vile' (Jer 15:19)
'im totzi yakar mi-zolel' (Jer 15:19) — the verse 'if you extract the precious from the vile,' prooftext for making converts and penitents, whereby glory is elevated

sukkah — the covered festival booth (the mitzvah-structure of Sukkot), understood as a sheltering canopy/covering (root ס-כ-ך, 'to screen over'), which Rabbi Nachman identifies with Binah ('mother who covers her children'), chesed/embrace, the shade of the divine hand, encompassing lights (makifim), and divine effluence — not the verb סָכָה 'to gaze/see' (though homiletically linked to it), nor any other same-lettered word
the spleen (techol) — the bodily organ associated with black bile (melancholy), identified in the Tikkunei Zohar with Lilith, sadness, and the kingdom of wickedness
the mother of the Erev Rav (mixed multitude) — an epithet of Lilith in Tikkunei Zohar (Tikkun 3), identified with the spleen, melancholy, and the fool's laughter of the Sitra Achra

tefillin (phylacteries) — the leather boxes containing Torah passages bound on the head and arm; in Likutey Moharan the aspect of 'pe'er' (glory/adornment), mochin (divine intellect/consciousness), and life
ima al bera — kabbalistic term 'Mother upon the Son' (Binah brooding over Ze'ir Anpin), the configuration embodied in tefillin per Tikkunei Zohar, linked to 'im la-Binah tikra'
covenant (berit) — the holy covenant of circumcision (berit kodesh), i.e., sexual purity and its rectification (tikkun ha-berit), corresponding to the sefirah Yesod and the tzaddik
amah bat shishah tefachim — 'the cubit of six handbreadths' as Talmudic euphemism for the male organ/brit, whose six units correspond to the seraph's six wings (sod of milah)
the 'faithful city' (kiryah ne'emanah, Isaiah 1:21,26) — the biblical epithet of Jerusalem, read as the aspect of faith (emunah) dwelling amid the nations
our seeking and yearning for Eretz Yisrael — the practice of praying for kisufin/ga'agu'im (longings) for the Land of Israel, a segulah against anger and sadness

earth / land (אֶרֶץ, the physical ground or terrestrial realm; incl. Aramaic cognate אַרְעָא) — used homiletically as a base 'bechina' term that Rabbi Nachman identifies via prooftexts with fear ('eretz yar'ah'), the soul ('nafshi ke-eretz'), faith ('shekhan eretz u-re'eh emunah'), and the body (earth vs. heaven = body vs. soul)
Elokei avikha — 'the God of your father' (I Chr 28:9), signifying inherited emunah: faith in God as the God of our fathers ('deeds of their fathers in their hands')
yir'at ha-onesh — fear of punishment, the lower of the two fears (vs. yir'at ha-romemut, awe of God's exaltedness), termed 'tzedek'
'the clarification/birur of the foods' — the kabbalistic sorting of holy sparks in food, accomplished through emunah (faith beyond intellect's answerable questions)
ulimta shapirta — the Zohar Saba de-Mishpatim's 'beautiful maiden without eyes,' symbol of emunah/faith ('you are beautiful, my beloved... nurture faith'), hidden yet revealed

vow (neder) — a sacred verbal pledge/oath of dedication, as in Yaakov's vow (Gen 28:20), linked in LM 57 to 'pele' (wonder, per Num 6:2 'ki yafli lindor neder') and serving as the means to rectify the hands, restore faith in the Sages, and draw the light of the Patriarchs

uprightness of heart (yishrat lev) — the heart straightened from its crookedness of doubt, identified with faith (emunah) that enables prayer; per 'Your righteousness to the upright of heart' (Ps. 125:4) in LM I:55
ha'amadat ha-melekh — 'appointing the king,' the first of the three mitzvot upon entering the Land (Sanhedrin 20b), identified here as the aspect of emunah/faith
Jerusalem (יְרוּשָׁלַיִם) — the holy city, deployed as a symbolic aspect (bechina) of Malkhut/faith/holy speech/the heart, via 'Malki-Tzedek king of Shalem' and 'faithful city' (kirya ne'emana)

the worm (tolaʿ) of holiness — the humble self-effacement of 'I am a worm and not a man' (Ps. 22:7), identified as the aspect of faith (per 'ha-emunim alei tolaʿ', Lam. 4:5), of Abraham, and of chesed-within-gevurah / the olat tamid, which subdues the worm of the kelipah; not any literal insect or the scarlet dye as mere material
tikvah — 'hope' (and the tikvat-cord of scarlet thread of Rachav, Josh 2), identified as emunah, the 'end of days' foundation upon which all middot stand (Habakkuk's 'one')
ro'im — 'the shepherds' (the seven shepherd-tzaddikim) from whom emunah is drawn, approachable only through holy boldness (azut) attained via joy

the 'spirit within the heart' (ruach she-ba-lev) — the animating spirit dwelling in the heart, identified in Likutey Moharan I:10 with the tzaddik, whose stirring reveals the illumination of the hands and feet (clapping and dancing), nullifying arrogance and heresy and increasing faith
'ragli amdah be-mishor' (Ps 26:12) — 'my foot stands on level ground,' verse-emblem of emunah as firm standing, the leveling that nullifies idolatry/heresy
saviv — 'around/surrounding' (Targum: sechor, whence 'socher,' merchant), signifying emunah per Ps 89:9 'Your faithfulness surrounds You'

ishah — woman/wife as the feminine archetype (e.g., Chavah, Esther, the Shekhinah); in Rabbi Nachman's typology the receptive female partner paired with 'ish', standing for faith, fear, the Holy Tongue, or livelihood
drawing near and cleaving to them (the tzaddikim) — the act of hitkarvut/devekut to the generation's tzaddikim, through which one receives emunah, the 'faithful city' Jerusalem

complete/perfect faith (emunah shelemah) — wholehearted, unblemished trust in God, the state of faith in its fullness and perfection (as opposed to deficient or 'small' faith), associated with Jerusalem the 'faithful city'
've-alayikh yizrach Hashem' (Isa 60:2) — 'but upon you Hashem shall shine,' verse denoting faith in Godhood (emunat Elokut) as the light of the face piercing the darkness of livelihood-worry
emtza'i — 'intermediary': the Shekhinah as the middle mediating principle that receives the Torah's fire and water and channels spiritual and material abundance

the sun (shemesh) — the celestial luminary of daylight, used as a symbolic aspect (bechina) of wisdom/intellect, Jacob, peace, truth, charity, and the covenant; not shamash (attendant/sexton) or the verb shimesh (to serve)
El (אֵל) — divine name signifying truth, applied to Yaakov ('God is not a man that He should lie'), the Name of Yetzirah ('El Havayah in Yetzirah')
blessings (berakhot) — divine blessing/benediction, the bestowal of blessing as in liturgical blessings and God's blessing (root b-r-k; not berekhot 'pools')

Breaking the lust for eating (shevirat ta'avat akhilah) — the spiritual practice of subduing and overcoming the bodily craving for food, e.g. through fasting or minimizing/being exacting in one's eating, which brings truth, lifting of the Divine face, sweetening of judgments, and the power to work wonders

Joseph (Yosef), the biblical patriarch son of Jacob, as the archetype of the tzaddik who guards the covenant (shmirat/tikkun ha-brit) — associated in Likutey Moharan with peace (shalom), sexual holiness, mesirat nefesh, uniting mind and speech, and 'adding' (from the root y-s-f, per Gen 30:24); NOT the plain verb יוֹסִיף 'he will add'

tzitzit — the ritual fringes (with the tekhelet blue thread) worn on a four-cornered garment per Numbers 15, which in Likutey Moharan function as the aspect of guarding the eyes/covenant, protection from adultery and the serpent's counsel, and the aspect of tzimtzum/encompassing lights
purifying/clarifying the blood beforehand — prior refinement of the bodily blood (damim) as prerequisite for truthful perception
the impossibility of speaking truth — state in which truth cannot be uttered (when eyes/perception are dimmed by falsehood)

nodes.he: מתגברין בעזות גדול כנגדם, שזהו עזות דקדשה
nodes.gloss: overpowering opponents with great boldness — the act of holy brazenness (azut d'kedushah) directed against those who obstruct divine service
the spirit (ruach) that extends/lengthens its breath — patient spirit whose drawn-out breathing constitutes long-suffering (erekh apayim) and the sigh over a deficiency (LM I:8)

the sigh (anachah) — the deep groan of holiness over a lack or over one's sins, an extension of the breath that draws the spirit of life (ruach chaim) to fill the deficiency, purify the heavens, and break the body more effectively than fasting
that which one does not grasp intellectually — the unattained portion of understanding, corresponding to anpin chashukhin (darkened faces)

anpin chashukhin — the Aramaic kabbalistic term "darkened faces": the state of a dimmed/unilluminated countenance signifying concealment of divine knowledge, sadness, and the grip of evil desires (opposite of anpin nehirin, the illuminated face)

Sadness/melancholy (atzvut) — the depressive spirit of dejection, worry, and black bile that stems from the kelipot and the Other Side, opposes joy (simchah), strengthens the imaginative faculty and blocks prophecy; includes the biblical 'itzavon' ("in sorrow shall you eat") sorrow of livelihood, which Likutey Moharan explicitly identifies with atzvut
that which a person understands and grasps with his intellect — attained comprehension, corresponding to anpin nehirin (illuminated faces)

anpin nehirin — the Zoharic/Aramaic term "illuminated (shining) faces," the radiant countenance of holiness: the luminous face associated with life, joy, Torah comprehension, and the holiness of Israel, standing in opposition to anpin chashukhin (darkened faces) of the nations and evil traits

the face/countenance of holiness (panim di-kedushah) — the radiant, luminous divine countenance (anpin nehirin) that embodies life and joy, as in 'in the light of the king's countenance there is life'
'zeh ha-davar' ('This is the thing,' Num. 30:2) — Moshe's unique prophetic formula, signifying the clear lens (aspaklaria ha-me'irah)
aspaklaria ha-me'irah — the luminous/clear speculum, Moshe's unmediated level of prophetic vision ('zeh')

"Koh" (thus/so) — the adverb introducing non-Mosaic prophecy ("koh amar Hashem", "so said the Lord"), used in Likutey Moharan 5 as the emblem of the dim, non-luminous lens (aspaklaria she'einah me'irah): indirect, distant perception, as opposed to Moses' "zeh ha-davar"; not the letters kaf-heh as a numeral (25) or any other homograph
aspaklaria she-einah me'irah — the non-luminous/dim speculum, the mediated prophetic vision of all other prophets ('koh')
hastarah she-betokh hastarah — double concealment of God (concealment within concealment), symbolized by Esther ('haster astir')

Esther — the biblical queen of the Purim narrative (heroine of Megillat Esther), invoked as a symbolic figure (bechina) whose name evokes divine concealment (hester/'hastir astir') and who represents Malkhut/Shekhinah, faith, and the feminine partner to Mordekhai; not any other word from the root ס-ת-ר
se'orim (barley, of the Omer offering) — symbol of Esther's ruach ha-kodesh, linked to 'kis'irim' (Deut. 32:2) as a term for ruach/spirit

"Esther [was said] with the Holy Spirit" (Talmudic dictum, Megillah 7a, that the Book of Esther was composed under ruach ha-kodesh) — used as the aspect of prophetic spirit/wind linked to barley (se'orim/se'irim) and to the feet, paired with Mordekhai
'Ani chavatzelet' ('I am a rose,' Song 2:1) — verse-phrase identified with the greenish Esther (yerakroket)
Esther yerakroket — Esther's greenish complexion (Megillah 13a), aspect of the green line (kav ha-yarok) from Binah
resha'im (the wicked) — the wicked identified as the aspect of efer (ashes), in contrast to holy dust/afar

ashes (efer) — the powdery residue left after burning; emblem of utter lowliness and negation (Avraham's 'dust and ashes'), associated with the wicked and with what fire has consumed (e.g., the burnt Temple)
her ability to give birth — the capacity (of the barren/soul) to bear offspring, made possible within the seventy-souls root-structure
shemirat ha-dibbur — guarding one's speech from blemish, whose neglect (Babylonian blurring of speech) breeds pride and exiles the Shekhinah
lomed Torah — the act of Torah study as prerequisite for valid prayer ('one who turns his ear from Torah, his prayer is abomination')
the possibility of praying — capacity for prayer, conditional on Torah study (impossible for the am ha-aretz who shuns Torah)

azut — boldness/brazenness (עַזּוּת), the abstract noun for audacity of spirit; in Likutey Moharan primarily holy boldness (azut di-kedushah, 'be bold as a leopard') required to enter holiness, approach the true shepherds/tzaddikim, and stand in prayer, attained through joy and linked to the 'voice of strength' (kol oz); with its counterfeit counterpart, the brazenness of the Sitra Achra ('kingship without a crown')
the possibility of drawing near to holiness — approach to kedushah attainable only via boldness ('be bold as a leopard')

nodes.he: אם נתעורר תכף ומיד ושב בתשובה
nodes.gloss: awakening immediately and repenting right after sin — prompt teshuvah before straying far from the good path
the ease of returning to one's place — easy restoration to one's spiritual station granted by immediate repentance
being nothing and naught in one's own eyes (efes va-ayin) — self-nullifying humility that alone merits perfected honor and speech

the possibility of meriting/attaining holy speech (dibbur) — i.e., being granted the perfected faculty of sacred utterance, which in LM 11 is attainable only through complete honor, by regarding oneself as nothing

Complete honor/glory (kavod bi-shelemut) — the perfected, unblemished honor of God, attained when a person utterly nullifies his own honor and arrogance (holding himself as nothing) and guards the covenant; this perfected divine glory is what enables illuminating speech (Likutey Moharan I:11). Distinct from mere human honor, from כָּבֵד ('heavy', as in kevad peh), and from the liver (kaved).
making converts (gerim) — the act of bringing gentiles to conversion, effected through charity to Torah scholars ('wealth adds many friends')
Ekyeh spelled out to 161 (KS"A) — the holy Name Ekyeh in its 161-gematria expansion, aspect of 'expert in running' (baki be-ratzo) for ascent

the Vacated Space (chalal ha-panui) — the Lurianic-kabbalistic void formed when the Infinite Light was contracted (tzimtzum) to the sides, an emptiness seemingly devoid of Godliness within which all of creation could come into being
arbeh (locust) — the locust whose garment is 'from and of itself,' symbol of the Vacated Space (chalal ha-panui) and its self-generated garment/tzimtzum

cursed (arur) — the passive participle 'accursed', the state of being under a curse, as in 'Cursed be Canaan' (Genesis 9:25) and the cursing of the serpent (Genesis 3:14); the aspect of the accursed one linked to the slave and the serpent

Bone (עֶצֶם) — the hard skeletal bone as opposed to flesh (בָּשָׂר), carrying its extended homiletic sense of inner essence/core (the true sage as the 'bone' to the people's 'flesh'; 'all my bones shall say'); distinct from עֹצֶם (might/intensity) or the verb עָצַם (to shut/be mighty)
aryeh (lion) — the supernal lion that descends to consume offerings, identified with etzem (bone) per Tikkunei Zohar 3

Tikkunei Atik — the rectifications/adornments of Atik (Atika Kadisha, the 'Ancient Holy One,' highest partzuf of Keter); the Kabbalistic term Rabbi Nachman identifies with length of days and the aspect of the elder (zaken), through which the wealth of contemplation is received (Likutey Moharan I:60)
length of days — longevity, the blessing of a prolonged lifespan granted as a benefit (e.g., through witnessing the tzaddik's passing or through the merit of mezuzah)

mezuzah — the parchment scroll affixed to the doorpost (the mitzvah of 'you shall write them on the doorposts of your house'), which in Likutey Moharan I:23 is expounded (via the wordplay zuz/mezuzah and Shaddai as covenant) as a remedy that nullifies the craving for money and draws livelihood; not the plain architectural doorpost per se, nor coins (zuzim)
emunah identified with tefillah — faith as constituting prayer itself, the bow-drawing (drikhat ha-keshet) of rectified prayer
the right side/right hand (yamin) — the kabbalistic right, the side of Chesed (lovingkindness), associated with Avraham, embrace, Torah, and spiritual abundance
"tamid" — the adverb 'always/perpetually' (as in Deut. 11:12, 'the eyes of the Lord your God are always upon it'), interpreted as an aspect of the Land of Israel; constancy of Divine watchfulness
'lifnei Hashem Elokeikhem' ('before the Lord your God') — verse-phrase denoting the Land of Israel ('whoever dwells in it is as one who has a God')
the merit of the Torah one draws down — drawn-down Torah novellae as the merit through which one attains the Land of Israel

Peace (shalom) — the spiritual quality of harmony that unites and reconciles opposites (e.g., chasadim and gevurot, mind and speech, disputing parties), associated with Yosef, Da'at, and healing; not a greeting, payment (shillum), or completeness (shalem) in another sense
'eretz natnah yevulah' ('the earth has given its yield,' Ps. 67:7) — verse-phrase for peace/healing, opposite of dispute (Canaan)

fire (Hebrew אֵשׁ, the physical/spiritual element of fire, esh) — used as a symbolic aspect (bechina) identified with Torah ('Is not My word like fire'), divine glory/honor, harsh judgments (dinim), the heat of the evil inclination, and the purifying medium that rectifies Malkhut ('you shall pass through fire'); not any other word spelled אש
chamimut ha-yetzer — the heat/burning of the evil inclination, the impure fire into which fallen Malkhut is drawn ('nura bei Amram')

the fire of this angel — the fiery substance of the angel (created from one's Torah/holy speech, as taught in Likutey Moharan I:59) which is formed from the aspect of judgment (mishpat), i.e., from a person judging himself
adam shofet et atzmo — self-judgment: a person judging himself, generating the angel's fire of mishpat ('with fire God judges')
the heavens / sky (shamayim), the celestial firmament — homiletically read in Likutey Moharan as the fusion of fire (esh) and water (mayim), hence signifying awe-and-love, Tiferet, the tzaddik, etc.

fire and water (esh u'mayim) — the paired elemental opposites whose fusion constitutes shamayim (heavens), homiletically read as esh + mayim; symbolizing combined dualities such as fear/love and the totality of colors (gevanin)
malakh mazik — a destructive angel: the evil inclination disguised in mitzvot, white fire yet still a damaging agent

white fire (esh levanah) — the Hebrew rendering of the Aramaic 'tzutzita de-nura chivarta' (tuft of white fire) atop the ship-sinking wave in Rabbah bar bar Chanah's tale (Bava Batra 73a), symbolizing the evil inclination's deceptive garb of apparent holiness when it clothes itself in mitzvot, though it remains a destructive angel
tzutzita de-nura chivarta — the tuft of white fire atop the ship-sinking wave (Bava Batra 73a), the yetzer hara cloaked as mitzvah
shivtei Kah — the twelve tribes of God, the twelve oxen under Solomon's Sea, aspect of the God-fearing woman/Malkhut
the perfection/completeness of the letters of words of faith — wholeness of emunah-speech, symbolized by the wife of R. Chanina ben Dosa
ishto rishonah — one's first wife (whose death shortens one's steps), identified with Shabbat as Israel's designated mate
ishtama kala le-beriyata — the voice made heard to creatures: prayer-voice projected with force, becoming thunder that straightens the heart's crookedness

being incorporated (nikhlal) into the Ein Sof — the mystical absorption of one's self into the Infinite Divine, attained through confessing all one's heart before the Torah scholar who embodies ayin (nothingness) (LM I:4)
returning Malkhut to the Ein Sof — restoring kingship/desire to the Infinite (zarka cast back to its source) via self-nullification before the tzaddik
'tenu oz l'Elokim' ('Ascribe strength to God,' Ps. 68:35) — verse denoting arousal from below: holy boldness that empowers Above

arousal from below (it'aruta dil'tata) — the Zoharic/kabbalistic term for spiritual awakening initiated by human effort in the lower world, which stirs a corresponding divine response and empowerment from Above
ittetakh gutza — Talmudic dictum (Bava Metzia 59a) 'if your wife is short, bend down and whisper to her,' read as symbol of Malkhut/prayer in a state of smallness whose counsel must be heeded
emunah be-massa u-mattan — faithfulness/honesty in business dealings, the practice through which the light of life (or ha-chayim) is drawn
bo or ha-chayim — the arrival/influx of the 'light of life' (light of the Divine countenance, sign of long life) that comes through faithful commerce and mezuzah

well (בְּאֵר, a dug well of water, as in the Israelites' well in the wilderness, Numbers 21:18) — the physical water-well, which Rabbi Nachman homiletically links via wordplay to בֵּאוּר, 'elucidation of the Torah'; not the verb בֵּאֵר 'to explain' nor the noun בֵּאוּר 'explanation' itself
penei Hashem — the 'face of God' as symbol of Torah explanations and homiletic discourses, linked to the elder's beard and the thirteen hermeneutical middot/tikkunei dikna
the flowing of all divine effluences and blessings into the world — the state of universal shefa and berakhah descending (context of the imaginative faculty resting on repeaters of halakhot)
garments, clothing (begadim) — physical clothes as a mystical aspect of Malkhut/honor, which must be kept white and unstained

the physical body (guf) — the material, corporeal component of a person, paired against and contrasted with the soul (nefesh/neshamah); associated in Likutey Moharan with matter, animality, foolishness, darkness, death, forgetfulness, and the realm of Asiyah
the principle that whatever a person truly and intensely desires (choshek) he can inevitably bring from potential to actuality, no obstacle withstanding sufficient longing

nodes.he: בעולם הבא, כשיזכו להשגה יתרה באלקותו
nodes.gloss: the World to Come as the state of attaining superior comprehension of God's divinity, prompting repentance upon one's earlier repentance (honor of Olam ha-Ba)

nodes.he: מי ששומע תקיעת שופר מאיש ירא וחרד
nodes.gloss: one who hears shofar-blowing from a God-fearing, trembling man — the listener to the yarei's teki'ah, thereby protected regarding the year's thunders

nodes.he: בודאי לא ידאג כל השנה מרעמים
nodes.gloss: the assurance of not worrying all year about thunder — freedom from harm/fear of ra'amim granted by hearing shofar from a God-fearer
tza'ar ve-din b'olam-shanah-nefesh — suffering/harsh judgment manifesting in the three dimensions World, Year (time), and Soul (Sefer Yetzirah triad)

nodes.he: בודאי נגרע משמחת הקדוש ברוך הוא
nodes.gloss: the diminishment of the Holy One's own joy — God's grief ('He was saddened in His heart'; Shekhinah saying 'kalani me-roshi') caused by judgment in world-year-soul

the man who strives to draw people near and 'make souls' for God's service — the outreach worker/mekarev (like Avraham's 'souls made in Charan') who must guard against the kelipot of those he draws near
building the 'Holy Sanctuary' (heikhal ha-kodesh) — the edifice constructed spiritually by one who makes souls and brings people to divine service

kiddush Hashem — the sanctification of God's Name, specifically the readiness to sacrifice one's life (mesirat nefesh) rather than transgress the faith; combining flames of love (chasadim) with overcoming the inclination unto death (gevurot), and thus an aspect of peace/Yosef

"God builds Jerusalem" (Psalms 147:2) — the verse-phrase בּוֹנֵה יְרוּשָׁלַיִם ה', expounded in Likutey Moharan I:80 as the binding of the mind/consciousness (ה', mochin) to speech (Jerusalem), i.e. the mochin building the holy speech

destroying the good letter-combination (tzeruf) of the divine speech/commandment — the act whereby a transgressor demolishes the holy arrangement of letters of the prohibition's utterance (e.g., 'You shall have no other gods'), replacing it with an evil combination engraved on his bones (LM I:4)

building an evil letter-combination (בּוֹנֶה צֵרוּף רַע) — the act whereby a sinner, by transgressing a prohibition, constructs a wicked permutation of the letters of that commandment's utterance, which is then engraved upon his bones (Likutey Moharan I:4)

Shame / embarrassment (bushah) — the noun for the burning inner feeling of humiliation and disgrace before God or man, which changes the colors of one's face ('the red departs and the white comes'), is likened to bloodshed/shechitah, and is the root of repentance; not clothing (levush) or any other homograph
the joining of Emet and Emunah — union of truth (tzaddik's counsel, masculine) with faith (feminine), the coupling upon which redemption depends
the redemption depends on this — the teaching (Likutey Moharan I:7) that the final redemption (geulah) hinges on the joining of truth (emet) with faith (emunah), figured as the union of man and woman
ish ve-ishah — the pair man-and-wife as symbol of the union of Emet (truth/husband) with Emunah (faith/wife), 'woman equated to man'
purity (tohorah) — the state of ritual/spiritual purity as opposed to tum'ah (impurity); in Likutey Moharan the intermediary between holiness and impurity through which impurity is rectified

free will / free choice — the human faculty of moral choice between good and evil, which exists only where two alternatives stand opposed (as in the realm of nogah or the intermediary state of purity); not בָּחִיר 'chosen one' nor the act of election of a person

the ultimate purpose (tachlit) — the final goal/end of creation and of man, identified with the World to Come, the state of 'entirely good' and oneness; not any homograph such as tekhelet (the blue dye), which appears only as a partner concept

bittul — mystical self-nullification: the annulment of one's ego/selfhood (yeshut) into nothingness (ayin) so as to be absorbed into God's oneness; the state of transcending existence associated with the ultimate purpose (e.g., Eden, 'no eye has seen'), attained especially through hitbodedut

the intellect (seichel) — the rational faculty of the mind/mochin that perceives, rebukes, and grounds trust in God; the 'eyes' of wisdom and vitality of the person (not שִׁכּוּל 'bereavement,' despite the wordplay on 'oti shikkaltem' in lm1:17)
Bitachon — trust/reliance in God (confident hope that God will provide), the devotional virtue of placing one's security in Hashem alone

Shevarim (שְׁבָרִים) — the series of broken, moaning shofar blasts sounded on Rosh HaShanah (one of the three shofar sounds alongside tekiah and teruah), homiletically linked by Rabbi Nachman to the roots שבר/שֵׂבֶר: trust in God ('sivro al HaShem'), the birthstool/reproductive organs ('ha-ani ashbir'), and the shattering of false beliefs ('shaber teshaber')
the lung (re'ah) in its state of wholeness/perfection — the bodily organ whose intactness produces perfect trust (bitachon)
bitachon bi-shleimut — complete trust in God, dependent on intellect ('eyes') and on the wholeness of the lungs
the betrothal-bond (hitkashrut ha-zivvugim) — the engagement/connection of a couple, at which earthenware is broken, oriented toward procreation and holy bitachon
bitachon di-kedushah — trust of the side of holiness, which nullifies and breaks the counterfeit trust of the Sitra Achra at the betrothal
the act of studying and comprehending — the cognitive stage of learning-with-understanding that is itself called Binah (second of the three intellects)

tzeirei — the Hebrew vowel-point of two horizontal dots (ֵ), interpreted homiletically as the vowel of formation (va-yitzer/nitztayer), signifying judgment-and-mercy and the shaping of light by its receiving vessel

wine — the fermented grape beverage (yayin), invoked as a mystical symbol: its two aspects being the Oral Torah ('royal wine') and Binah, the joy of the heart ('wine gladdens the heart'), and, drunk in proper measure, a means of broadening da'at and magnifying the chasadim
Imma — the supernal 'Mother,' kabbalistic partzuf identified with Binah (paired with Abba/Chokhmah), the Heh of Y-H, seat of mochin reached by Yesod's ascent
the number forty — numerical symbol of Binah/Da'at (forty years of manna, mem = 40), signifying attained understanding
Binah va-Da'at — the paired sefirotic intellects Understanding and Knowledge, symbolized by the number forty and by the manna
motrot she-ba-moach — the surplus/waste-products of the brain-mochin, from which hair grows and from which enemies/external forces derive nurture
binah yeteirah — the 'extra understanding' given to woman (Niddah 45b), reinterpreted as the surplus of the mochin from which hairs and hostile forces suckle
binah libba — 'Binah is the heart' (Tikkunei Zohar dictum): Binah as heart-joy, one of the two 'wines' alongside the wine of Oral Torah/Malkhut
binah la-ittim — 'understanding of the times' (I Chron. 12:33), the aspect of the pilgrimage festivals (regalim) to which Malkhut is elevated through rebuke
grain and food (bar u-mazon) — the Aramaic/Hebrew pair denoting physical sustenance and provisions, used as an aspect (bechinah) of livelihood (parnassah), linked to the 'well' (beira) in LM 31
beira — Aramaic 'well/pit' as symbol of parnassah, grain and sustenance (bar u-mazon), the well of livelihood

nodes.he: יראה, שבאה לאדם מכח אדם עצמו
nodes.gloss: the lower fear — yirah aroused by the person's own effort/initiative (as opposed to supernal fear that descends of itself), the human-generated awe that awakens shefa
cypresses (beroshim) — the cypress tree of Isaiah 55:13 ('instead of the briar shall rise the berosh'), used homiletically as an aspect linked to carob (charuvin), Mordekhai, and birsha
birsha — Aramaic word for cypress/beroshim (from Rabbah bar bar Chana tale), tree-symbol expounded in the lesson

house (bayit) — the noun 'house/dwelling structure' used symbolically for an enclosed, settled domain of holiness: the Temple/house of prayer, the inner 'house' of da'at, the house whose 'head' (rosh bayit) is the mochin; distinct from any other word sharing the letters בית
