'lekhet' ('to walk,' from Micah 6:8 'hatznea lekhet') — exegeted as the sefirot Netzach and Hod (the two legs/full sukkah walls), paired with hatznea = Yesod
Netzach and Hod — the paired seventh and eighth sefirot (Eternity/Victory and Splendor) in Kabbalah, corresponding to the two legs/feet, associated with prophecy, walking, and Torah scholars
the simple supernal light becoming configured (nitztayer) according to the receiving vessel — the tzeirei-vocalization principle that the undifferentiated light takes the shape of its kli
the totality of the lower rung (klal ha-madregah ha-tachtonah) — the principle that any entire lower level is 'nefesh'/feminine relative to the rung above it
the feminine (nekevah) — the female principle in Kabbalah, the receptive lower aspect (identified with nefesh, the wife, the feet) relative to the masculine level above it
nekudah im vav — the melupum vowel-sign pictured as a point with a vav, symbolizing Yosef the ruler drawing from Chokhmah (yud-point) and Binah (vav-river)

being called 'adam' (man) — the honorific status of true humanity conferred through Torah ("This is the Torah — adam"; "You are called adam"), attained via illuminated countenance and freedom from evil traits and desires, in contrast to the nations who are not called adam
nikra'im chakhamim — being called 'wise ones': the title sages earn for silently enduring strife and insults (the geese shedding their feathers) without responding
ner — the candle/lamp as symbol of the soul (nefesh), per 'the candle of Hashem is the soul of man' (Prov 20:27), whose merged flames produce light and joy
kiyum ha-sekhel — the sustaining/maintenance of the intellect, kept alive like a burning lamp by bodily moisture preserved via the lungs, enabling trust (bitachon)
ner dolek — a burning/lit candle as image of the intellect, whose flame is fueled by the body's moisture guarded by the lungs against the heart's heat
nasa libo et raglav — 'his heart carried his feet' (Bereishit Rabbah 70): dancing driven by the spirit in the heart, via the tzaddik, nullifying arrogance and idolatry
devekut shel adam ba-Ein Sof — a person's mystical cleaving to the Infinite (Ein Sof), a state of nullified awareness that must alternate 'running and returning' to preserve his existence
dross of gold (Zoharic Aramaic suspita de-dahava): the slag/refuse left from refining gold, symbolizing the degraded residue of the gevurot — external (fallen) fear, as opposed to holy fear of Heaven

the voice/sound of a sigh (קוֹל אֲנָחָה) — the audible groan of holy yearning, identified in Likutey Moharan I:22 (on Psalms 102:6 'from the voice of my sighing') as an expression of holy boldness (azut di-kedushah) that breaks the body's brazenness and rejoins the soul to the flesh

marriage/marital union (nisu'in) — conjugal joining as a spiritual archetype in Likutey Moharan I:7, where receiving counsel (etzah) from another is likened to marital union and receiving seed (the kidneys that counsel being the vessels of procreation); holy union with tzaddikim vs. 'marriage in the kelipah' with the wicked, as in the serpent's counsel to Eve (hishi'ani as leshon nisu'in)

counsel/advice (etzah) — guidance received for one's path, esp. the spiritual counsel of the tzaddikim (the 613 counsels, counsel as seed/union), as opposed to the counsel of the serpent/wicked; not עֵצָה 'wood/timber' (Jer 6:6) nor עָצֶה 'spine'
atzot ha-nachash — the counsels of the primordial Serpent that Chavah received, an act of 'marriage' (hishi'ani/nisu'in) through which the Serpent injected pollution (zuhama) into her
ke-shemekabblin etzot me-resha'im — the act/state of receiving counsel from the wicked, which constitutes a union ('marriage') with the kelipah, opposite of receiving tzaddikim's counsel
nisu'in ba-kelipah — 'marriage within the husk': the illicit spiritual union effected by accepting the wicked's counsel, modeled on 'the Serpent hishi'ani' read as language of marriage

nishlam ha-dibbur le-shalom — the completion of the speech of peace: through Shabbat-eating delight speech attains peace, unlike the mute peace of a weekday fast ('they could not speak to him peaceably')
simchat ha-mitzvah — joy in performing a mitzvah, which completes holiness and raises the vitality trapped in the kelipot (the eleven incense spices), enabling grasp of the unattainable
nishlam ha-Torah — [here: charity being completed/illuminated on Shabbat] the completion/shining of tzedakah through Shabbat as emunah ('sun on Shabbat is charity for the poor')
Shabbat she-hu bechinot emunah — Shabbat identified as the aspect of faith (emunah), testifying to God's unity and creation, through which tzedakah is completed and shines
ke-she-nishlam ha-da'at — the state when Da'at (knowledge/awareness) is perfected, whereby all lacks are remedied ('if you acquired da'at, what do you lack?'), ending troubles and exile
nishlam kol ha-chesronot — the remedying/completion of all deficiencies that follows the perfection of Da'at, since troubles, suffering and exile exist only in proportion to lack of Da'at
nishlam pigmei ha-yirah — the repair/completion of the blemishes of fear (yirah) achieved by returning honor (kavod) to its root in fear, which then yields peace
mesame'ach et atzmo be-Elokav — the practice of gladdening oneself in one's God, the tikkun that completes all lacks stemming from the Shattering of the Vessels and elevates fallen sparks
the true sage (chakham ha-emet) — the genuine Torah wise man who, as the soul/essence of the people beneath him, draws them close; not wisdom in the abstract nor a false/external sage
neshamah le-ha'am — the true sage as the 'soul' of the people below him: he is the essence (bone) and the people are the flesh, broken by hearing his sighing voice
souls (neshamot) — the plural of neshamah, the divine soul; in Likutey Moharan the Jewish souls that are enclothed in the letters of Torah and ascend within prayer
kol ha-tov — 'all the good': the principle that all goodness in existence is nothing but the souls of Israel, including good held captive among the nations
nishmot Yisrael — the souls of Israel, identified as the totality of all good, portions of which lie captive within the nations and draw converts back to Israel's faith
ke-she-shome'a mi-peh ha-tzaddik — hearing Torah directly from the tzaddik's mouth as the aspect of 'nishma' (we will hear), the crown Israel retained, unlike book-study (na'aseh)

nodes.he: בימי רבן גמליאל היה הדור, שהיתה תורתם
nodes.gloss: bimei Rabban Gamliel — the generation of Rabban Gamliel, whose Torah was in the aspect of 'nishma'/prayer, hence they learned Torah standing (amidah = prayer)
ha-nistarot la-Shem Elokeinu — the verse 'The hidden things belong to the Lord our God' (Deut 29:28), expounded as the aspect of 'nishma' versus the revealed 'na'aseh'
nishmar min talmidim she-einam hagunim — being guarded from unworthy students: the protective function of a Torah scholar's ordinary conversation ('ve-alehu li-terufah' — to permit the mouth)
nishtaneh ha-teva — the changing/overriding of nature through prayer (the 18 blessings of the Amidah), nullifying the philosophers' 'nature, mother of all life (chai)'
nishtanah panav le-khamah gevanin — the face changing to many colors in shame, symbolized by the vav within the alef as the firmament (fire-and-water) comprising all hues

Drawing close to the tzaddikim — the devotional act of attaching oneself to the true righteous ones (seeing them, giving charity to them, confessing before them), which nullifies arrogance and rectifies everything
ribui ha-mitzvot — the abundance/multitude of mitzvot ('even Israel's sinners are full of mitzvot as a pomegranate'), whose collective light of joy overpowers the anxiety of sin

nodes.he: נתבטל הדאגה של החטא המונעת השמחה
nodes.gloss: nitbatel ha-de'agah shel ha-chet — the nullification of sin-anxiety that had blocked joy, dissolved by the blazing light of joy from one's many mitzvot, enabling confession

the nullification of charon af — the abatement of Divine fierce anger (burning wrath) in the world, effected by removing idolatry (whether literal idol-worship or the idolatry of money) through faith, based on the dictum 'as long as there is idolatry in the world, fierce anger is in the world'
nitbatel ha-cherpah ha-shorah al libo — the annulment of the disgrace resting on one's heart ('disgrace broke my heart,' Ps 69) by binding the heart to its timely point of holiness
nitbatel ha-ka'as ve-ha-akhzariut — the nullification of anger and cruelty through expanded Da'at, which multiplies peace ('the wolf shall dwell with the lamb, for the earth is full of knowledge')

the nullification of heresy — the abolishment of heretical denials of God (kefirot, equated with idolatry) effected through the tzaddik's revealed spirit via dancing and hand-clapping, which increases faith (emunah) (נִתְבַּטֵּל הַכְּפִירוֹת)

the nullification of the coveting of money (chemdat ha-mamon) — the state in which greedy desire for wealth is abolished, attained in Likutey Moharan I:23 through the mitzvah of mezuzah (corresponding to 'You shall not covet')
mitzvat mezuzah — the commandment of mezuzah, through which the craving for money is annulled (Shaddai = 'Who said dai/enough,' contentment with one's portion)
nitbatel machshevot akum — the annulment of idolatrous/foreign thoughts through hand-clapping in prayer, which places one in the atmosphere of the Land of Israel ('as one who has a God')

she-al yedei ha-tzaddik — [in exposition of 'Anokhi'] that through the tzaddik/divine agency one praises God equally in both names ('in YHVH I praise, in Elokim I praise'), all being 'He Who is good and does good'
nitbatel malkhutam u-memshaltam shel ha-akum — the nullification of the kingship and dominion of the idolatrous nations (all exiles named after Egypt) through 'I am the Lord your God'

nodes.he: נתבטל רצונו מפני רצון השם יתברך
nodes.gloss: nitbatel retzono mipnei retzon Hashem yitbarach — nullifying one's own will before God's will, the inner essence of fasting/tzedakah that annuls conflict and increases peace

she-mafshitin u-mashlikhin me-aleihem ha-begadim ha-tzo'im — stripping off and casting away the 'filthy garments' (sins), whereby all barriers and screens dividing one from holiness are removed (damming the Jordan)
the receiving of the Torah (kabbalat haTorah) — the act/event of Israel accepting the Torah at Sinai, as at the giving of the Torah, and the spiritual state of receiving Torah it represents

nodes.he: נתבטלין ונכנעין אלופי עשו, רברבי עשו
nodes.gloss: nitbatlin ve-nikhna'in alufei Esav — the subduing and nullification of the chieftains/magnates of Esav via receiving the Torah ('alfei shin'an' read as she-einan, 'that they are not')
histaklut al ha-takhlit — gazing at the ultimate purpose/end (as reaping is the goal of plowing), achieved by shutting the eyes to the sights of this world and focusing vision
nitbatlin kol ha-yisurin — the nullification of all sufferings ('afflictions of the soul,' nig'ei ha-nefesh) attained by closing the eyes and directing one's gaze to the ultimate purpose
studying or praying with dchilu u-rchimu (awe and love) — the devotional mode that joins the breath-heh and voice-vav to reveal divine Kingship
the gevanim (divine colors/hues) becoming revealed and shining — illumination of the color-lights within one's money rectified through tzedakah
knowing that God is hidden there — the da'at-awareness that Hashem is clothed even within concealment-within-concealment
doing teshuvah and removing one's foolishness (tipshut/ruach shtut) — the repentance-act that restores intellect and brings manifest shame to the face

nodes.he: מתפלל בכל כחו ומכניס כחו באותיות התפלה
nodes.gloss: praying with all one's strength and putting one's koach into the letters of the prayer — the devotional practice of investing bodily power in tefillah's letters
one's strength being renewed there (in the prayer-letters) — the renewal of koach per 'they are new every morning' (Lam. 3:23)
placing the bed between north and south — the Talmudic bedroom practice symbolizing zivug/prayer, equated with hand-clapping in prayer

the atonement/forgiveness of sins (avonot) — iniquities being wiped away and pardoned (nitkaperin, from k-p-r 'atone'), as an outcome achieved through spiritual means such as prayer or drawing near to the tzaddik
diminution of the blood in the left ventricle of the heart — weakening of the yetzer's seat achieved by turning dam (blood) into dom (silence)
chesed (kindness) being drawn into the world — the flow of divine lovingkindness released when the idolatry of money and its charon-af are nullified
enlightening others (le-haskil) — the act by the man of intellect of imparting sekhel in divine service to one poor in da'at
the arousal occurring also in oneself — the reflexive awakening in the enlightener when he stirs intellect/compassion in another
the heart being aroused — awakening of the lev by the thunder-voice, per 'sound arouses concentration' (kol me'orer ha-kavanah)
arousal of the compassion that is Da'at, together with prayer — awakening the greater Merciful One's rachmanut via tefillah for complete salvation
telling stories of tzaddikim — the practice whose told reshimu (impression) of the tzaddik's service inflames the heart toward God
'waters upon the mountains' (Chagigah 12b cosmology) — the heart-waters ('pour out your heart like water') upon which the prayer-pillars stand

the arousal/awakening of the Chesed (lovingkindness) of Abraham — the divine attribute of kindness associated with the patriarch Abraham being stirred into activity (in LM I:38, aroused through Torah, 'water upon the mountains')
elevating Malkhut of holiness from exile among the idolatrous nations — reclaiming the Elohim-kingship the nations suckle from
the 'legs' of Torah and prayer — Torah and tefillah as amidah/standing-feet (raglin), prefiguring Messiah's feet on the Mount of Olives

nodes.he: נתקרבו, בחינת: "ועמדו רגליו על הר הזיתים"
nodes.gloss: being drawn near — the messianic reconnection signified by 'His feet shall stand on the Mount of Olives' (Zech. 14:4) via the Torah-prayer legs
being healed from the falling sickness (epilepsy) — recovery from choli nofel caused by bloods surging and compressing the mochin
dam brit — the covenant-blood (of circumcision) that rectifies niddah-blood/lust for money, per 'also by the blood of your covenant' (Zech. 9:11)

nodes.he: תורה, שעל ידה נתעורר מדת אברהם
nodes.gloss: Torah as that which arouses the middah of Avraham (chesed) — nighttime Torah study drawing the thread of kindness that rectifies speech
everything being rectified (nitakken ha-kol) — the total tikkun effected by the three modes of closeness to tzaddikim
strife being rectified/nullified — resolution of machloket (Korach vs. Aharon, left vs. right) through hand-clapping uniting the sides
all one's money being rectified — the tikkun of one's entire mamon effected by giving tzedakah, becoming 'Mine is the silver and gold'
rectification of the World of Speech (olam ha-dibbur) — repairing Malkhut/speech through the joy of abundant mitzvot enabling confession
segol — the three-dot vowel-point symbolizing the three conditions of teshuvah: eye seeing, ear hearing, heart understanding (Isa. 6:10)
segol of KS"A (161, Ehyeh spelled with yuds) — the vowel/name-expansion of 'essak shamayim,' the expertise-in-ascent (baki be-ratzo)
gazing at the tzitzit — the act of looking upon the fringes (its threads, windings, knots) as a healing remedy for the sick
segulah for a sick person — the remedy for a choleh, namely gazing at the tzitzit, encoded in 'behold your son Yosef comes to you'
distributing tzedakah lavishly (pizzur) — scattering charity per 'pizar natan la-evyonim' (Ps. 112:9), whose initials spell nofel
segulah for the falling sickness (epilepsy) — the remedy for choli nofel, namely distributing charity (acronym nofel in Ps. 112:9)

The secrets of the Torah (sodot haTorah / sitrei oraita) — the hidden, esoteric dimension of Torah knowledge (the kabbalistic mysteries, called 'the hidden matters of the world,' kivshono shel olam), revealed to and attained by select individuals, especially through prayer; not the revealed/exoteric Torah teachings
Kena'ani — 'Canaanite' as merchant/trader (per Rashi on Hos. 12:8 'Canaan, in his hand deceitful scales'), emblem of commerce
socher — the merchant/trader figure (as in Rashi's 'Ishmaelite merchant'), emblem of commerce arising from lack of peace

the 'Ishmaelite merchant' (socher Yishmael) — the Arab trader (tayya) of Rabbah bar bar Chanah's desert tale, expounded in LM I:9 as the aspect of prayer (socher/sechor, faith surrounding) and of the tzaddik of the generation who encompasses all prayers like Mashiach

the end of the deed (sof ma'aseh) — the completed act as it emerges in actuality (po'al), which was contained first in the initial thought (machashavah techilah), per the phrase 'the end of the deed is in the initial thought'; symbolized by the final Yud (the Name Adonai)
Esav as the complete dross and refuse (sigim u-pesolet) — the waste-product born from Yitzchak's din, opposite of Yaakov's sweetened wisdom

Sinai — Mount Sinai, the mountain of the giving of the Torah (including its Talmudic use as an epithet, 'Sinai', for a master of the revealed Torah, Berakhot 64a), symbolizing revealed Torah and humility; a proper name, not any common noun
the waters of the chasadim — kindness-waters that are the sukkah sheltering from 'the strife of tongues' (Ps. 31:21)
sikhlut — foolishness as the body/animal/matter/darkness pole, opposite of chokhmah-wisdom (Eccl. 2:13)

rock, crag (sela) — the hard stone rock from which waters/speech/Torah-elucidations are drawn (as in 'he opened the rock and waters flowed'; 'upon the rock he dwells'), homiletically linked to the heart and the well; the biblical noun סֶלַע 'rock,' not e.g. the sela coin as a monetary unit
safun — 'esteemed/treasured,' the wordplay (safun ve-chashuv) underlying the 'ship' (sefinta) as Israel's grace and importance that the yetzer-wave seeks to sink
the supernal heart (lev shel-ma'alah) — the heart on high, identified with the Book of Remembrance, from which the yearning learner receives
Sefer Zikaron — the heavenly Book of Remembrance (Mal. 3:16) in which words of the God-fearing are written, identified with the supernal heart
the aforementioned gevanim (color-lights) as the greatness of the Creator — the divine hues whose perception the imaginative faculty blocks at the gate of intellect

nodes.he: סתירת הפתח, שהוא המדמה, שהוא הטמאה
nodes.gloss: setirat ha-petach — demolishing the doorway (from the elders-of-Athens riddle): the counsel of tearing down the medameh/imagination, identified with impurity, so one can enter the gate of holy intellect
Ayin-Bet Resh-Yod-Vav (72 + 216) — gematria pair of divine names (Chesed 72 / Gevurah 216) whose sum equals ibur (288, 'grain/pregnancy') in the Rabbi Yonah rain story
yare'ach — the moon as celestial body/symbol, called 'servant' (sihara) in the Zohar, ruling over the four elements beneath its sphere
the evil character traits (middot ra'ot) deriving from the four physical elements, termed 'servants' because the elements lie beneath the lunar sphere — nullified in 'out of the house of bondage'

the corruption/flaw of faith (kilkul ha-emunah) — a defect in one's trust in God's providence, which Rabbi Nachman equates with the aspect of idolatry and identifies as the root cause necessitating journeys
kefirot — heresies/denials of God, defined as an aspect of idolatry (avodah zarah)

Arrogance (gadlut) — haughty self-aggrandizement, the negative character trait of pride identified in Likutey Moharan 11 with idolatry (the 'seven houses of idol worship') and arising from the fall of the divine garment of splendor (tiferet); NOT the positive 'greatness/expanded consciousness' (gadlut ha-mochin)
shemirat ha-mo'ed — the act of guarding/honoring the festivals, whose neglect equals idol worship (Rashi on the juxtaposition of idolatry and festivals)
avodah tamah — 'complete/unblemished divine service,' the Temple-service term applied to festival observance as the opposite of idolatry
shishim (sixty) — the number sixty as the measure of nullification of forbidden food (bittul be-shishim), symbolizing the circle (igula), the letter samekh, the Throne of Glory, and 'sixty queens'
the practice of speaking words of Torah and prayer until the body is nullified — speech-devotion uniting body with holy speech ('they shall be one flesh')
the state of bodily self-nullification (bittul) attained through Torah and prayer speech — the body becoming null and naught, one with the word
boshet — shame/bashfulness as a spiritual quality, root of holy boldness, identified with Eden ('the shame-faced goes to the Garden of Eden')

Eden (עֵדֶן) — the proper name of the supernal paradise-source of Genesis 2:10 ('a river goes forth from Eden'), which in Likutey Moharan is the hidden realm 'no eye has seen' (Berakhot 34b): the transcendent source above nature and beyond grasp, homiletically identified with prayer, the ultimate purpose/nullification, and the supernal Eden — not the common noun עֵדֶן 'delight/pleasure' nor any other word from the root עדן
the or ha-ganuz — the hidden primordial light stored away for the righteous in the future, the 49 lights, 'Eden which no eye has seen'

"Eden — no eye has seen it" (עֵדֶן עַיִן לֹא רָאֲתָה, per Berakhot 34b on Isaiah 64:3): the concealed supernal Eden utterly beyond perception, identified in Likutey Moharan 8 with the light hidden away for the future and with prayer — not the earthly Garden of Eden, nor any other sense of 'eden' (delight/pleasure)
the 'od sheli' — the 'yet/more' one finds within oneself (from 'azamrah l'Elokai be-odi'), the residual good point enabling one to sing to God
the verse 'od me'at ve-ein rasha' (Ps 37:10) — 'yet a little and the wicked is no more,' judging oneself favorably by the small good point that renders one no longer wicked
zivchei Elohim — 'the sacrifices of God' (Ps 51:19), interpreted as the olah burnt-offering equated with a broken spirit (ruach nishbarah)
olah (ascent) of the two Houses — 'Mi with Zot ascends': the rising together of Binah (upper house, 'Mi') and Malkhut (lower house, 'Zot')
the ascent/rectification of speech (dibbur, called 'foot/regel') via Shabbat — 'if you restrain your foot on Shabbat,' repairing speech damaged by the serpent's contamination
the agency of 'these lights' (the aforementioned orot) — through which one ascends to delight in Shabbat, riding 'the high places of the earth' (Avraham and Yitzchak, the arms of the world)
the state of ascending and delighting in oneg Shabbat — Shabbat-delight attained via the lights and the patriarchs ('az titanag al Hashem')

nodes.he: עולים כל הניצוצות על־ידי אחד־עשר סממני הקטרת
nodes.gloss: the elevation of all fallen sparks via the eleven spices of the ketoret (incense) — raising sparks from among the idolaters through faithful commerce ('yod'ei teru'ah' as joining)
the divine name combination El-Havayah (E-l + YHVH) — signifying alma de-atei, the World to Come, drawn into this world
dibbur shel Shabbat — the speech of Shabbat ('ve-daber davar'), the World-to-Come speech that must be drawn into and complete weekday speech
olam-shanah-nefesh — the Sefer Yetzirah triad World/Year/Soul, the three statures (komot) that receive vitality from the mitzvot
osek be-dinei mamonot — engagement in monetary law/judgments, equated with the plain sense of Torah and honest commerce (the 'sleep' aspect of Rosh Hashanah)
the act of speaking with the Rebbe/master — the disciple's boldness-enabled conversation with his teacher, the measure of closeness to him
the state of doing and laboring much in divine service — abundant active worship, itself dependent on holy boldness (azut dikdushah)

making a vessel, boundary, and time — the act (in Likutey Moharan I:76) whereby gazing with trust toward God fashions a receptacle that delimits and schedules the ever-descending Divine influx (shefa), so the abundance arrives at the specific moment it is needed
histaklut be-vitachon — the gaze of trust: looking with one's eyes to God alone in bitachon ('the eyes of all look to You'), which fashions a vessel of boundary and time for the divine flow
the making of wings of holiness (kanfei dikdushah) — forming the six holy wings/handbreadths of the brit (circumcision-covenant), as in the six-winged seraphim
the act of taking speech from da'at (knowledge/awareness) — drawing the word from the mind so it contains the good that makes it heard and accepted
the act of putting the good into speech — infusing dibbur with tov so that it is heard and accepted ('the good — all desire it')
the transformative act of making tzedek into tzedakah — adding the heh of five chasadim via charity, elevating fallen Malkhut from 'her feet descend to death'
iza — the 'goat' of Rav Ashi's sea-goat (Bavli aggadah), read as oz (might/strength), i.e., fear of God, 'the glory of their strength'
azut de-sitra achra — brazenness of the Other Side, the profane bodily impudence (azut ha-guf) opposed to holy boldness

nodes.he: עבודתו שהוא עושה ועובד הרבה את ה
nodes.gloss: one's own divine service ('that he does and labors much for God') — the personal avodah about which one must boldly speak with the Rebbe
azut le-daber im ha-rav — the specific boldness to speak freely with one's Rebbe/teacher about all one's needs without shame, the measure of closeness
the verse 'im esak shamayim sham atah' (Ps 139:8) — 'if I ascend to heaven, You are there,' signifying ayil (entering), expertise in ratzo (running upward) in teshuvah
the phrase 'Ani le-dodi' (Song 6:3) — 'I am my beloved's,' read as the aspect of ayil (entering/ascending), the baki be-ratzo of repentance
eina chad de-rachamei — the Idra's 'one eye of mercy' of the future time (the single eyeball), the all-good Ein Sof gaze of 'wholly good and beneficent'
ir Elokeinu — 'the city of our God' (Ps 48), the aspect of 'house' to which prayer is elevated from mountain and field, revealing God's kingship to the nations
the phrase 'ir ve-kadish min shemaya nachit' (Daniel 4:10) — 'a wakeful holy one descended from heaven,' whose acronym spells Shimon, alluding to the tanna Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai
pirdah — the she-mule, a hybrid animal born of separation, symbolizing the idolatrous nations (akum) who dwell in peruda/disunity per the Zohar (Mishpatim 95a)
Sura — the Babylonian river/locale from the Talmudic phrase 'two rivers of Sura,' read as symbol of the idolatrous nations, from 'saru' (they turned aside quickly from the way, Ex. 32:8)
the evil middot (character traits) of the idolatrous nations — earthly traits to which the nations are bound, constituting the 'yoke of derekh eretz'
ol derekh eretz — the 'yoke of worldly ways' (Avot 3:5), identified as subjugation to the nations' evil earthly character traits

nodes.he: שיודע בדעת ברור שהכל בהשגחה מהשם יתברך
nodes.gloss: knowing with clear awareness (da'at) that everything happens through God's providence — the cognitive certainty of divine hashgachah that nullifies the feeling of suffering (Likutey Moharan I:250)
physical subjugation (shibud be-gashmiyut) — material servitude to the nations, identified as the 'yoke of government'
ol malkhut — the 'yoke of government' (Avot 3:5), i.e., political subjugation in the physical realm imposed on one who casts off the yoke of Torah
meriting the way of teshuvah through the double expertise (baki be-ratzo, baki be-shov), linked to the Name YB"K (=112) of the Elul kavvanot

frog (tzefardea) — the amphibian, as in Rabbah bar bar Chanah's 'akrukta', homiletically read as a compound of 'tzipor de'ah' (bird of knowledge), symbolizing the elevation of fear to its root in Da'at
the ascent of yirah (fear/awe) to its root in Da'at — symbolized by the frog (tzefardea = tzipor de'ah, 'bird of knowledge'), bird being the aspect of fear
the ascent/elevation of holiness (aliyat ha-kedushah) — accomplished essentially through joy, as in the future joyous exodus from exile that consumes the kelipot
amuda de-emtza'ita — the kabbalistic 'middle pillar,' identified with mishpat (judgment), the balanced aim that inclines neither right nor left
ve-kam ('and a scepter shall arise,' Num. 24:17) — the word 'arise' expounded as the aspect of amidah, standing (prayer), in the verse about the star from Jacob
goral — the 'lot' (Prov. 18:18) that ends quarrels, identified as the delight of Shabbat (oneg Shabbat), per 'you shall rest and stand for your lot' (Dan. 12:13)
receiving the Yom Tov (festival), which is Binah — welcoming festival holiness with joy as a segulah against arrogance, via Moshe's forty-nine gates of Binah

humility and lowliness (anavah u-shiflut) — the paired character trait of self-effacement and lowly self-regard, by which a person diminishes and conceals himself; associated with the aspect of ayin (nothingness) and leading to fear of Heaven
receiving the holiness of Yom Tov (festival sanctity, effected through Torah scholars who elevate Malkhut), which bestows humility and lowliness
Aron ha-Brit — the Ark of the Covenant in the Tabernacle, symbolizing the poor person (ani) who sits beneath the curtain and receives its bestowal (tzedakah)
lashon hara — evil/slanderous speech, a vice of the 'medaber' (human) element that brings poverty, paired with idle talk and pride
meni'ah — an obstacle/hindrance to holiness, identified as cloud-and-fog darkness, from choshekh meaning withholding ('ve-lo chasakhta,' Gen. 22:12)
anan va-arafel — 'cloud and thick darkness,' the dark screen symbolizing obstacles/withholding (choshekh as language of meni'ah)

the aforementioned clouds (הָעֲנָנִים הַנַּ"ל) — the seven clouds of glory discussed in Likutey Moharan I:21 that form the covering (sekhakh) of the sukkah of divine influx; identified with the seven lamps of the menorah and with the mist (אֵד) that rises from the earth, and characterized as holy (kodesh), not receiving impurity

"clouds that cover the eyes" (Aramaic Zoharic phrase, ananin dimekhasyan al einin) — the mystical image of cloud-like obscurations that veil the eyes of perception/da'at, blocking spiritual vision until torn away
the branches of the tree — one's allotted money/wealth as the anafim spreading out from the trunk that is the light of his soulmate's soul

The Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil (Etz HaDa'at Tov vaRa) of Genesis — the Edenic tree symbolizing the mixture of good and evil, associated in Likutey Moharan with Targum, the kelipah of Nogah, and the doubts/confusions preceding Torah clarity, in contrast to the Tree of Life
the Tree of Life (Etz HaChaim) — the paradisal tree of Genesis 2:9 as a kabbalistic symbol of unblemished divine vitality and the Torah itself, contrasted with the Tree of Knowledge/Tree of Death
the money of those immersed in wealth — riches under the curse 'in sorrow shall you eat' (be-itzavon), bringing sadness, melancholy, and darkened countenance
atzvut ve-atzlut — sadness and laziness, the serpent's bite arising from the element of earth/dust ('dust is the serpent's food,' Isa. 65:25)
damim akhurim — turbid/murky blood, the physiological source of sadness and lusts, expelled through salt (the tzaddik as 'covenant of salt')
sadness and lusts (atzvut ve-ta'avot) — the pair of afflictions arising from turbid blood, rectified via the tzaddik-salt
Har Sinai — Mount Sinai (tura de-Sinai of the Elders' riddle), symbolizing counsels (etzot), for there Israel received the 613 counsels of Torah
etzot niv'arot — foolish/senseless counsels, degraded advice of one whose heart is fouled like a privy by the filth of excess
atzat nashim — the 'counsel of women' (Gittin 45a, in the privy), symbol of impure, unreliable counsel arising from a filth-laden heart
straightening the crookedness of the heart (akmumiyut she-ba-lev) via thunder — i.e., the forceful voice of prayer, per Berakhot 59a, prerequisite for heart-joy
the essential extraction (birur) of holy sparks from the kelipot — accomplished through emunah/faith, which like Jerusalem dwells amid the nations
or nafshah — the light of the wife's (destined soulmate's) soul, which is the trunk of the tree whose spreading radiance is one's money
ikkar ha-ilan — the trunk/root of the tree in the wife-money-children allegory, identified with the light of the soulmate's soul from which the money-branches spread
da'at oto yitbarakh — knowing God Himself ('had I known Him I would be Him'), the cognitive union whereby the intellect, and thus the whole person, is where it thinks
the essence of being included in the One (nikhlal be-Echad) — merging with God attained through knowing Him, granting eternal life and perfection
aravah — the willow branch (Hoshana Rabba), resembling lips, symbol of speech without da'at, like one who stammers Torah without understanding (Zohar Kedoshim 85b)
arvin — 'guarantors' in 'a person's feet are his guarantors' (Sukkah 53a), punned with arvei nachal (brook willows), the feet as channels of water
willows of the brook (arvei nachal) — the willow branches of the Four Species (Lev. 23:40), homiletically linked via the wordplay arvin/arvei to the feet as 'guarantors' and to channels of water
'asa'ah ke-otzar — [Torah as] a treasury made through fear of Heaven ('the fear of the Lord is His treasure,' Isa. 33:6), the storehouse aspect linked to yirah

herbs / grasses — plural of עֵשֶׂב, the plants/vegetation of the field (which grow by rain under their appointed stars and serve as the source of medicinal remedies, and symbolically correspond to souls)
the souls of Israel who study and comprehend Torah — likened to the herbs and grasses growing in the garden (Torah), nourished by the spring of Chokhmah
asavin u-desha'in — the herbs and grasses growing in the garden (Tikkunei Zohar 14), symbol of Israel's souls who study and understand Torah
'like ones drunk on wine' (ki-shetuyei yayin) — the intoxicated appearance of the dead of the desert, aspect of ruddy Esav, the master of the kelipah
studying from a written book — Torah study in the aspect of Asiyah/'na'aseh' (the crown Israel lost), weaker to arouse than hearing from the tzaddik's mouth
ma'asekha — 'Your works' (Ps. 145:10), expounded as the aspect of Asiyah/action and the body, paired against 'Your pious ones' as the soul
wealth (ashirut) — material riches/prosperity as a spiritual attainment, granted through fear of Heaven and truth
charon af — 'fierce anger'/burning wrath, the divine (and human) attribute of anger that must be sweetened, imaged as smoke rising from the nostrils (Ps. 18:9)
the smoke issuing from His nostrils (Ps. 18:9 'smoke went up in His nose') — the bodily/anthropomorphic image of charon af, divine burning anger
asarah minei zimrah — the ten kinds of song/melody, corresponding to the ten expressions of Psalms, whose power nullifies the kelipah (basis of the Tikkun HaKlali's ten psalms)

nodes.he: עשרה לשונות שנאמר בהם ספר תהלים
nodes.gloss: the ten expressions (leshonot) with which the Book of Psalms was composed — Ashrei, Lamnatzeach, Maskil, Halleluyah, etc. (Pesachim 117a; Zohar)
asarah minei nigguna — the ten types of melody symbolized by the letter Yud (numerical value 10) within the Hei, linked to the future song (simple-double-triple-quadruple)
ishah ra'ah — the 'evil woman/wife,' a kelipah-figure identified with the 'evil time' (et ra'ah), counterpart to the evil maidservant opposing the Shekhinah

the "evil time" (et ra'ah) — the time/hour of evil, a designation for the domain of the Sitra Achra (identified with the evil woman and the evil maidservant, Malkhut of the Other Side) that rules when holiness is blemished
shifchah bisha — the 'evil maidservant' (Aramaic), the kelipah that usurps the Shekhinah/Malkhut, identified with the 'evil time' (et ra'ah)
sippurei ma'asiyot shel shanim kadmoniyot — telling stories/tales of ancient years, an activity that is the aspect of Atik (the most ancient partzuf), signified by the carob/elder

"abundant in kindness" (rav chesed) — the Divine attribute from Exodus 34:6 ("abundant in kindness and truth"), invoked here as equal in gematria to Mordekhai (274) and identified with the supernal aspect of Atik
'the one seated upon the throne' — the enthroned figure of the Chariot vision identified as Atik Yomin (Daniel 7:9 'and the Ancient of Days sat')
Atik Yomin — the 'Ancient of Days' (Dan. 7:9), the highest partzuf of Keter, here the one who sits upon the throne above the four chayot
shefer — 'beauty/fine' (from 'imrei shafer,' Gen. 49:21), wordplay-cognate of pe'er (glory), the aspect of tefillin and the illumination of Jacob's face

Pe'er — glory/splendor as sacred adornment: the noun פְּאֵר meaning beauty-of-glory, identified with the tefillin worn on the head (per 'פארך חבוש עליך'), the radiant crowning glory linked to the mochin and the Name of God resting upon Israel (not the verb לפאר 'to glorify' nor the tree פארה/branch)
pegam ha-begadim — the blemish/stain of the garments (the stain on one's clothing), external sign of blemishing the totality of the gidin (sinews), tied to pegam ha-brit
blemish/impairment of da'at (the mind/knowledge) — pegam ha-da'at, damage to one's spiritual faculty of knowledge, linked to fever-illness and to the blemish of the covenant
mitmasken — 'becoming impoverished,' the state of falling into poverty as punishment for blemishing Chokhmah by building a house without wisdom ('the poor man's wisdom is despised,' Eccl. 9:16)
eating like a glutton and drunkard (zolel ve-sovei) — coarse, unrestrained eating that blemishes the altar (mizbeach) of holy eating and feeds the kelipot
pegam ha-raglin — the blemish of the legs/feet, the state of unrectified sparks before elevation into holy speech, imaged as Jacob 'limping on his thigh' (Gen. 32:32)
chatzot — midnight, the practice/time of rising at halakhic midnight (six hours into the night) for lament and thanksgiving, propitious like a pidyon for sweetening judgments (Ps. 119:62)
pidyon — a redemption(-payment) that sweetens the dinim (harsh judgments); midnight is likened to it in efficacy
striking palm against palm — clapping the hands in prayer, whose 5×5+5×5=50 strikings of the finger-lights form the mouth (the Fifty Gates), a theurgic act
the mouth (peh) — the bodily/spiritual organ of speech, as in the mouth formed through clapping the palms and the mouth that 'speaks wisdom' (Ps. 49:4); not the adverb פֹּה ('here')

the voice a person brings forth with force/strength in his prayer — the forceful vocal exertion in praying which, per LM I:5, generates 'thunder' (re'amim) that straightens the crookedness of the heart
giving charity in secret (matan ba-seter) — the concealed act of tzedakah that 'subdues anger' (Prov. 21:14), tied to the six pei-sounds of the alphabet
expelling the bad bloods — the salutary action of salt (the tzaddik as 'covenant of salt') purging the turbid blood that breeds sadness and lusts
mishpetei ha-Torah — the civil/legal judgments (laws) of the Torah, embodied in the poskim, by which 'a king establishes the land' and sunken gates are revealed
poskim — the halakhic decisors/legal authorities, embodiment of the Torah's mishpatim through which the land's sunken gates are revealed
chittukh ha-yadayim — the 'cutting/articulation of the hands' (chatakh), the apportioning action hinted in the acrostic of 'Pote'ach et yadekha,' governing sustenance
'Pote'ach et yadekha' — the verse 'You open Your hand' (Ps. 145:16), whose final letters spell ChaTaKh, the divine name of parnassah/apportionment
Pachad Yitzchak — 'the Fear of Isaac' (Gen. 31:42), the sefirah Gevurah personified in Isaac, holy judgment born from Abraham's Chesed
Pishon — the first river of Eden, homiletically read as 'pi shoneh (halakhot),' the mouth that repeats halakhot
pi shoneh halakhot — 'the mouth that studies/repeats halakhot,' the act of reciting Jewish law, derived from the name Pishon

the double portion (pi shenayim) of the firstborn's birthright (Deut. 21:17), homiletically read as 'two mouths' — prayer's twofold speech comprising praise of the Omnipresent and petition for one's needs, linked to the double-edged sword (cherev pifiyot)

wonder/marvel (pele) — the hidden, transcendent 'wondrous' quality (as in Isaiah 29:14 'hafle va-fele' and Isaiah 25:1 'asita pele'), associated in LM I:57 both with the departure/concealment of the Sages' wisdom and with the vow ('ki yafli lindor neder', Num 6:2) that rectifies it; not the verb 'to separate/set apart' in other senses

the great light of the festival (Yom Tov) — the supernal illumination shining on a festival day, which one receives by honoring the festival and which is identified with the face of one's master/the tzaddik (Likutey Moharan I:135)
penei rabbo — 'the face of one's master,' whose greeting on the festival means receiving the festival's great light, since Yom Tov's holiness depends on the tzaddikim

face, countenance (panim, פָּנִים) — the frontal visage/presence, used as the kabbalistic aspect of revealed divine presence and illumination (as in 'hiding of the face', 'the face of the land'), to which prayer, truth, wealth, and Torah explanations are likened; not פְּנִים 'interior/inside'

kedem (קֶדֶם) — 'before/front': the forward/anterior direction, as in 'achor va-kedem tzartani' (Ps. 139:5), the frontal aspect opposed to achor (back/behind); paired with panim (face) and with straight alphabetical order (aleph-bet ki-seder)

matkela — the Zoharic 'scale/balance' (Aramaic מַתְקְלָא, from Sifra deTzniuta 'ad lo havei matkela'), the divine weighing-mechanism by which God weighed out the letters for each thing per His will ('to make a weight for the wind,' Job 28:25); identified in Likutey Moharan I:19 with the perfection of the Holy Tongue, prerequisite for 'face to face'

face-to-face (panim be-fanim) — the kabbalistic state of mutual face-to-face union/gazing between the supernal countenances (as in the Zoharic 'mashgichin apin be-apin'), the illumined encounter attained through the perfection of the Holy Tongue (matkela); not the plural noun 'faces' in an ordinary spatial sense

the shining/luminous face (panim me'irot) — the kabbalistic aspect of radiant divine countenance, identified with the face-to-face (panim be-panim) illumination attained through the perfection of the Holy Tongue (matkela), as opposed to darkened or averted faces
shoresh ha-emunah — the root of faith: the higher 'world of faith' from which emunah is drawn, which itself has faith in God; faith's inner source

the inner dimension of faith (penimiyut ha-emunah) — the interior core of emunah, identified in Likutey Moharan I:173 with the root of faith (the world of faith's own faith in God) and with the inner dimension of the soul
penimiyut ha-nefesh — the inner dimension of the soul (nefesh), equated with inner faith, since nefesh and emunah are one (Isa. 26:9 with Ps. 92:3, both 'in the night')
torot acherot — 'other torahs,' false teachings emanating from the Sitra Achra via unholy brazenness, the counterfeit opposite of holy Torah
pesilim — 'idols/carved images,' the name for Sitra Achra's counterfeit torah held by the brazen-faced, inverse of 'pesal lekha' (carve for yourself) of holy Torah
shortened steps (pesiot ketzarot) — the constricted gait of one whose first wife has died (Sanhedrin 22a), applied as the aspect of desecrating Shabbat (Shabbat being the first wife)
'his steps become shortened' — the shortening of a man's strides when his first wife dies (Sanhedrin 22a), applied to one who desecrates Shabbat (his 'first wife')
kafui ve-kal — 'floating and light,' the trait of a prayer/substance that rises to the top like scum, marking it as refuse (pesolet) versus worthy prayer
pesolet — refuse/dross, the waste element (light and floating) separated out from prayers/food, as opposed to the worthy essence

actuality / the actualized state (po'al) — the realized 'actual' as counterpart to potential (koach) in the philosophical pair 'from potential to actual' (mi-koach el ha-po'al); not the verb pa'al ('he acted') nor po'el ('worker/agent')
thinking good thoughts — revealing one's good middot within the heart's cleared empty space (chalal panui) after contracting its blaze, mirroring the cosmic void of creation

good deeds and good character traits (pe'ulot u-middot tovot) — the concrete righteous actions together with refined ethical attributes through which one serves God in measured, gradual devotion (Likutey Moharan I:49)
chokhmah she-ba-lev — the wisdom in the heart, the good attributes/secret of world-creation revealed within the heart's empty void after tzimtzum of its fiery ardor
awakening people from their sleep — the tzaddik's act of rousing those who 'sleep away their days' in dormant spiritual service, which effects pekidat akarot (remembering barren women)
sustaining one's Father in Heaven through prayer — Israel 'feeding' God via tefillah, in proportion to which one's own parnassah is granted through the twelve tribal prayer-paths
parnasah — livelihood/material sustenance: the provision of food and one's earthly means of support, granted by God (the noun פַּרְנָסָה, including suffixed forms like פַּרְנָסָתוֹ 'his livelihood')

Tikkun HaKlali as tikkun ha-brit — the general rectification, i.e., rectifying the covenant (sexual purity), the 'way of the eagle in the heavens' that yields effortless livelihood (bread from heaven/manna)
parnasah beli torach — livelihood without toil, the effortless sustenance (manna, 'bread from heaven') attained through tikkun ha-brit

in proportion to the magnification/expansion of Da'at (holy awareness) — the principle in Likutey Moharan I:56 that benefits (easy livelihood, peace) increase commensurately with the growth of one's consciousness of God
parnasah be-nakel — livelihood obtained with ease, a state of sustenance dependent on expanded Da'at (the less da'at, the more toil)

nodes.he: מרירותא דעלמא שצריך להמתיקה על ידי מלח
nodes.gloss: merirut'a de-alma — the bitterness of the world that must be sweetened by salt (Zohar dictum), applied to livelihood-in-sorrow as 'more bitter than death'

opening (patach) — the vocalized form פַּתָּח denoting an opening/aperture (with wordplay on the vowel-name patach), specifically the Vav inside the letter Aleph that 'opens' and separates the two Yuds (potential and actual) in LM I:66; not פִּתַּח 'he engraved' nor the verb 'to open'
tzeitekha — 'your going out' (Deut 33:18, 'Rejoice Zevulun'), the designation for commerce/business dealings as an outward activity vs. Torah's tents
zeh — the demonstrative 'this' (Eccl 12:13 'this is the whole of man') as a title/symbol for the tzaddik, for whom the world was created as companion
lulav — the palm branch of Sukkot's four species, symbolizing the tzaddik ('the righteous flourish like the date palm')
keshet ha-brit — the rainbow of the covenant (sign of Noah), symbolizing the tzaddik who guards the brit
efroach — a chick (Aramaic retzitza), symbol of the tzaddik via 'yifrach' — 'the righteous will flourish in his days' (Ps 72:7)
tov — 'good' as an epithet of the tzaddik (matza tov = finding the righteous one), not mere moral goodness
di-vchisha — 'that searches/burrows' (Aramaic, of the sea-goat in Rabbah b. bar Chanah's tale), symbolizing the tzaddik who constantly seeks out the beauty in every Jew
tzeror kaspo — 'his bundle of silver' (Gen 42:35 / Prov 7:20), a symbol for the tzaddikim per Rashi, found within the emptied sack
harim — mountains, as a symbol for the tzaddikim
gader — a fence/wall (Aramaic guda, the shore the fish was cast onto), naming the tzaddik as the one who fences the breaches of Israel
arba'ah she-nikhnesu la-pardes — the Talmudic episode (Chagigah 14b) of the four sages who entered the Pardes: R. Akiva, Ben Azzai, Ben Zoma, Acher

nodes.he: צדיק ורשע עובד אלקים ולא עבדו
nodes.gloss: tzaddik ve-rasha, oved Elokim ve-lo avado — the fourfold typology from Malachi 3:18 (righteous, wicked, server of God, non-server) mapped onto the four who entered Pardes
tzaddik ve-ra lo — 'a righteous one who suffers,' the theodicy category identified here with the tzaddik whose halakhic opinion is not followed
tzaddik she-ein halakhah kemoto — the tzaddik whose ruling is not accepted as halakhah, corresponding to 'the righteous one who suffers'
tzaddik ve-tov lo — 'a righteous one who prospers,' the theodicy category identified with the tzaddik whose halakhic opinion prevails
tzaddik she-halakhah kemoto — the tzaddik whose ruling is accepted as halakhah, corresponding to 'the righteous one who prospers'
yerdu tehomot — 'they go down to the depths' (Ps 107:26), the phrase denoting the lower tzaddik between whom and the upper tzaddik the Shekhinah rests
tzaddik tachton — the lower tzaddik (paired with the upper tzaddik), associated with kisses and 'dripping flowing myrrh'
nehorei de'ah — 'lights/paths of Da'at' (pun on Nehardea in Shmuel's saying), the illumined paths of knowledge linked to tzedakah-mercy
mercy / divine compassion (Aramaic rachamei, as in the Zoharic dictum 'nesher da rachamei' — the attribute of mercy identified with the eagle and with tzedakah); not רֶחֶם 'womb' or רַחֲמִי 'my womb'

the General Rectification (Tikkun HaKlali) — the all-encompassing rectification that repairs all blemishes at once, particularly identified with rectification of the covenant (tikkun ha-brit) and associated with charity in Likutey Moharan 29
keren — horn (Aramaic karna), symbolizing tzedakah as the enduring 'principal' (keren) stored up for the World to Come (Munbaz)
amud ha-shachar — the pillar of dawn/daybreak, a symbol for tzedakah ('then your light will break forth like the dawn,' Isa 58:8), which saves from wild beast and bandits
kotzim — thorns (which the traveler fears), symbolizing the vegetative element (tzome'ach) and its bad traits
tzome'ach — the vegetative kingdom, second of the four elements of creation (mineral-vegetable-animal-speaker), whose bad traits are nullified by gazing at the tzaddik
tzurah — form (vs. chomer/matter), the soul-side of the man/animal, wisdom/foolishness, light/darkness dyad
melaket ha-ruach — the gatherer of the spirit: the musician who ascends and descends the strings ('who gathered the wind in his palms,' Prov 30:4) to collect the good spirit
shekhem — the shoulder ('on the shoulders of both,' also the place Shechem in Gen 37:13), symbolizing tzitzit as guard of the brit against sexual sin
hargashat ha-yissurin — the felt sensation of sufferings, identified as the soul's thirst produced by saltiness/bitterness
tzim'on ha-nefesh — the thirst of the soul, the burning felt in suffering, quenched by new Torah insights born of self-nullification

nodes.he: כשצריך לעצה, ואינו יודע איך לעשות
nodes.gloss: needing counsel and not knowing how to act — a state of constricted intellect (tzimtzum), i.e., harsh judgments, sweetened by receiving advice from the sages
tzimtzum ha-or li-tzedadin — the Lurianic contraction of the infinite light to the sides, creating the Vacated Space (chalal ha-panui) for creation
tzimtzum shel chalal ha-panui — the contraction that formed the Vacated Space, source of the 'garments' (levushin) of divinity
tza'akat ha-yoledet — the cry of a woman in labor; the cry one raises in prayer/Torah when the mochin withdraw into gestation, birthing renewed mentalities
tza'ar kiflayim ka-yoledah — 'double the pain of a birthing woman': the anguish of worry and craving for livelihood (be-itzavon, dark countenance)
tzipor de'ah — 'bird of knowledge,' Rebbe Nachman's wordplay on tzefarde'a (frog) in Rabbah bar bar Chanah's tale, the melody-bird of holy da'at
dadei ha-malkhut — the breasts of Malkhut (Zohar), from which the impure birds of the kelipah suckle when a wicked musician draws his melody
the requirement that the letters of speech be complete — perfection of speech (via the World to Come) needed to bring potential into actuality
razin de-razin — 'secrets of secrets,' the designation for Kabbalah (vs. razin = Halakhah), which becomes enclothed within Halakhah
kibbelu ha-Torah — Israel's act of receiving the Torah at Sinai, possible only after casting away speculative wisdoms
hishlikhu me'itam kol ha-chokhmot — the act of casting away all secular/philosophical wisdoms, Israel's precondition for receiving the Torah at Sinai
the acceptance of prayers — prayers and requests being received (nitkabbel) Above, effected in LM I:1 through Torah study which raises grace (chen); not the act of praying itself

"beginning" (techilah) — the primal firstness that precedes creation; in Likutey Moharan I:22 the aspect of being "first"/before the creation, identified with ayin (nothingness) and Ein Sof, by virtue of which one who prays for his friend is answered first
tefillat Hashem — prayer of/for God, an aspect of the state 'before Creation' (ayin), whereby one praying for another is answered first
kedushah — holiness as such, symbolized by the letter Yud (the 'tenth'/tithe), drawn down into Malkhut
hatchalat ha-makom she-mishtalshel mi-sham ha-mamon — the supernal point of origin from which money devolves down the chain of worlds, itself pure holiness
kedushah ve-shefa kodesh — holiness and holy abundance, the sacred flow at money's root before it materializes below

the Supernal Intellect (sekhel ha-elyon) — the higher, transcendent divine intellect above all constricted/lower intellects, associated with the Holy of Holies and Chokhmah, source of the power to sweeten judgments and of settled da'at ('sons')
tzvi la-tzaddik (Isa. 24:16) — the verse-phrase 'beauty/glory for the righteous,' expounded as the sanctity of marital union of the tzaddik
kedushat ha-zivvug — the holiness of marital union/coupling, the tzaddik's sanctified sexuality (razin d'razin)
kedushat Yom Tov — the holiness of the festival day, which the tzaddik embodies and which one senses by attachment to him
kedushat Yisrael am kadosh — the intrinsic holiness of Israel the holy nation, the 'illuminated faces' (anpin nehirin) rooted beyond all traits and desires
vayarek (Gen. 14:14, 'he armed') — the verse-word expounded as the green line (kav ha-yarok) drawn from Binah, linked to Abraham's chesed
kav ha-yarok — the kabbalistic 'green line' extending from Binah that encircles the entire world
hon (Prov. 29:3, 'wealth') — the verse-word expounded as voice (kol), via 'honor God me-honkha = mi-gronkha' (from your throat)

kaneh — the reed/cane (which is also the windpipe, the hollow reed-like channel from which the voice issues): the symbolic reed of the aggadah 'Gabriel planted a reed in the sea,' expounded both as the throat producing voice (LM 1:5) and as wisdoms — holy ('acquire wisdom,' keneh chokhmah) versus the reed of the kelipot, external wisdoms ('rebuke the beast of the reeds') (LM 1:35); NOT the verb קָנָה 'to acquire' itself, though the homophony with קְנֵה is the basis of the wordplay
kol ha-yotzei me-ha-kaneh — the voice issuing from the windpipe (kaneh/reed), rooted in fear/gevurot, symbolized by Gabriel's reed planted in the sea
karna — the Aramaic 'horn' (of the donkey, in the Talmudic tale), expounded as the voice of the rebuker (mokhiach) that severs Malkhut from the cry

the voice of the rebuker (mokhiaḥ) — the sound of one who delivers moral reproof, likened to the blast of the shofar per Isaiah 58:1 ('Raise your voice like a shofar and tell My people their transgression')
shemu'ah tovah (Prov. 25:25) — 'good tidings from a far land,' expounded as the thunder-voice that heals the soul's distance from glory, like cold water on a weary soul
kol ha-re'amim — the voice of the thunders, which 'announce themselves in goodness' and repair the soul's estrangement, reviving soul and bones
perutah — the smallest coin (of charity), expounded via 'perita sifvateih' as the cooing voice of the turtledove (kol ha-tor)
kol ha-tor (Song 2:12) — the voice of the turtledove, likened by the Sages to the crier-bird whose lips split (perita), linked to the perutah of charity

the voice/blast of the shofar (ram's horn) — the piercing sound of the shofar as a symbolic aspect (bechina) of holy boldness and awakening rebuke, likened in Likutey Moharan I:22 to the voice of the reprover and the voice of melody (per Isaiah 58:1, 'Raise your voice like a shofar')
kol neginah — the voice of melody/music, a form of holy boldness equated with teruah and shofar ('play well with teruah')
mi she-yesh bo yir'ah — the one who possesses fear of Heaven, whose forceful voice becomes thunder that awakens the heart
kolo na'aseh re'amim — the transformation of a person's voice into thunders: speech striking the brain/mochin so the heart is aroused ('voice awakens kavvanah')

nodes.he: שכל מה שנותן צדקה ליותר אנשים
nodes.gloss: she-kol mah she-noten tzedakah le-yoter anashim — giving charity to ever more people, the practice that multiplies friends and purifies the air
koneh lo re'im yoter — acquiring more friends/loved ones, the soul-gathering effect of widespread charity (Munbaz: 'I stored up souls')

nodes.he: קורא את החיות לתוך הימים והמדות
nodes.gloss: korei et ha-chiyyut le-tokh ha-yamim ve-ha-middot — calling/summoning the life-force into the days and attributes via the Name (Torah), since a name bounds a thing's vitality
korin et ha-arikhut yamim — 'calling' length of days by the Name: invoking the Life of life through Torah (God's Name) to draw down life and longevity
ezov — hyssop, the lowly plant of purification, symbol of the 'small of stature' (ketanei komah)
ketanei komah — those of 'small stature': people whose refined intellect exceeds their good deeds, so their heart cannot contain their mind
kiyyumo shel ha-da'at — the sustaining/endurance of da'at (knowledge), maintained through the Patriarchs = Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet
sechok — mockery/laughter (hit'alalti = 'I mocked'), the mimicry of the kelipot which ape holiness like a monkey imitating a man
ta'avot — bodily desires/lusts, defined as superfluities (motarot) and hence kelipot, husks around the fruit of the body's true needs
shochad (Deut. 16:19) — the bribe that 'blinds the eyes of the wise,' emblem of corrupted judgment producing alien thoughts in prayer
ye'avver — the verb 'blinds' (from 'a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise'), the blinding of the eyes/judgment that spawns alien thoughts
or ha-pashut ha-ba mile'eil — the undifferentiated simple light descending from Above, 'closed and concealed' (kamitz u-setim) until shaped by the receiving vessel
kamitz u-setim — Zoharic term 'clenched and sealed': the closed, concealed state of the supernal simple light before it is configured in a vessel
kamatz — the vowel-point kamatz, symbol of that which is clenched/closed and hidden (kamatz u-setim), linked to concealed supernal mochin
kamatz u-setim — 'clenched and sealed,' the concealment-state signified by the kamatz vowel: hidden supernal light closed off from disclosure
hirhurim ra'im — evil/lustful ruminations of the mind, identified as the 'reed (kaneh) of the Sitra Achra' that leavens the brain
kaneh de-sitra achra — the 'reed of the Other Side' (chayat kaneh, Ps. 68:31): the demonic windpipe/reed embodied in evil thoughts, whose chet must be broken into heh (chametz→matzah)
suf — the word 'Suf' (as in Yam Suf, Sea of Reeds), expounded as ketz kol basar, 'the end of all flesh' — the terminus/end-point

The 'storm wind' (ruach se'arah, cf. Ezekiel 1:4) — the tempestuous spirit of the kelipah/Other Side that acts as the great accuser: it draws sustenance from flawed speech, empowers the wicked (spirit of impurity of Esav), manifests as the spirit of folly, and inflames a person's fire beyond proper measure

nodes.he: תפלה, שהוא בחינות יראה, בחינות מאמר השלם
nodes.gloss: tefillah as yirah / ma'amar ha-shalem — prayer identified as the aspect of fear/awe and as the 'complete utterance' (Bereishit = yarei boshet), linked to building Jerusalem/emunah

the radiance/shining of the skin of the face (keirun or ha-panim, from Exodus 34:29 'karan or panav' — the beams of light on Moses's face after Sinai), which Likutey Moharan 38 identifies with the aspect of tefillin and with holy shame (busha); not to be confused with קֶרֶן meaning animal horn or corner
keren ha-shofar — the horn of the shofar as symbol of the rebuker's voice, per 'Raise your voice like a shofar and tell My people their transgression' (Isaiah 58)
hearing melody from a wicked musician — the act/state of listening to neginah played by a menagen rasha, which harms one's divine service
difficulty in serving the Creator — the spiritual impairment (kasheh lo la'avodat haBorei) caused by hearing a wicked musician's melody
'tzarah ke-mavkirah' (Jeremiah 4:31) — verse-phrase 'anguish like a woman birthing her first', symbolizing difficult labor (kishui leileid) in the birth of the soul

the rainbow (keshet) — the arc seen in the clouds as the sign of God's covenant after the Flood, symbolizing the tzaddik whose merit protects the generation (Ketubot 77b; 'I will see it to remember the eternal covenant')
sight / the faculty of seeing (רְאִיָּה, visual perception with the eyes) — not רְאָיָה 'proof, evidence'
Rabbi Akiva — the Tannaitic sage who entered the Pardes in peace and exited in peace (Chagigah 14b), archetype of the tzaddik
parsah — the hoof (of an animal), taken as the aspect of the foot/leg (regel)
the feet of holiness enclothed in this world — raglei ha-kedushah, the lowest divine level ('the earth is My footstool') vested in physicality
sheluchei ha-din — the emissaries/agents of judgment, called 'runners' (ratzim) in the Zohar, corresponding to the legs that grow heavy under harsh judgments
bat zugo — a man's destined wife/soulmate, his nefesh-aspect and 'feet' (Zohar: 'the feet of His pious ones — this is the wife'), through whom his money comes

pillars (amudim) — supporting columns upon which something stands (e.g., the earth), used homiletically as the aspect of legs/heels and of prayer; plural of amud (pillar), not to be confused with pages (amudim of a book) or the verb 'standing' (omdim)
hit'halekh ('Walk before Me', Genesis 17:1) — the verb of walking as the aspect of legs and of livelihood/money ('the substance at their feet')
mochichei ha-dor — the rebukers of the generation, called 'feet' as limudei Hashem who counsel God and go on His mission to rebuke Israel; the outer seal
kiymu ('they fulfilled', Shabbat 88a on Esther 9:27) — the word 'fulfilled' of Purim's re-acceptance of Torah, read as the aspect of the feet/legs
raglin — legs/feet as the kabbalistic locus of birur ha-nitzotzot (clarifying sparks) until Mashiach, whose 'feet will stand on the Mount of Olives' (Zechariah 14:4)
loving one another — the state of mutual love between souls/tzaddikim so strong it equals constantly seeing each other
seeing one another — the state of constant mutual beholding that expresses and measures the strength of love between them

eagle (nesher) — the bird of prey, used as a Zoharic symbol (e.g. of spirit/ruach or mercy/rachamei), as in 'ka-nesher ya'ir kino' (Deut 32:11) and 'derekh ha-nesher ba-shamayim' (Prov 30:19); not to be confused with homographs such as נָשַׁר 'to fall off/shed'
dofek ('knocks', Song of Songs 5:2) — the beloved's knocking identified in Tikkunei Zohar as the aspect of ruach (spirit/pulse) that reveals the illumination of the hands
panav — the face, specifically the nose ('the recognition of their faces' = the nose, Yevamot 120a), as the seat of the ruach/breath blown into the nostrils
ruach dil'tata — the 'lower spirit' of the paired upper/lower spirits, corresponding to po'al (actualization) as against potential, formed by sweetening fierce anger
the pulsing spirit (ruach ha-dofek) — the beating/pulsating wind-spirit of the heart, felt as the pulse, which in Likutey Moharan 56 is linked to thunder and the holy spirit
ruach tzefonit — the north wind that never blew in the wilderness (Yevamot 72a), representing the holy spirit of life (ruach chaim dikedushah)

the spirit hidden (tzafun, צָפוּן = concealed) within a person's heart — Rabbi Nachman's wordplay in LM I:8 on 'north wind' (ruach tzafon), identifying it as the concealed ruach-chaim (spirit of life) residing in the heart
speaking between oneself and one's Maker — private hitbodedut speech to God, defined as an aspect of ruach ha-kodesh, from which David founded the Psalms

the spirit of Mashiach (ruḥo shel Mashiaḥ) — the messianic spirit that hovered over the waters (Genesis 1:2, per the Midrash identifying 'the spirit of God' with the spirit of the Messiah), identified in Likutey Moharan with holy speech, the Shekhinah, the Holy Spirit, and the spirit of zealousness against immorality
arba tzitzit — the four fringes of the garment as the spirit of life from 'the four winds' (Ezekiel 37:9), subduing the storm-wind of the opponents
sighing over a lack and extending one's breath — the act of the anachah as arichat ha-neshimah/erekh apayim that draws the ruach-chaim to fill the deficiency
makif — the encompassing/surrounding light (the tallit), identified with the spirit of life, 'round and round goes the wind' (Ecclesiastes 1:6)
the melody of David's harp — the niggun of the kinnor of David played by the north wind, embodying the spirit of life in the tzitzit-corners
the vitality of a given thing — the chiyut sustaining each particular thing, located in its ruach; where a lack occurs, the lack is in this vitality
the spirit-of-life of a given thing — the particular ruach-chaim that sustains each thing, the true locus of any deficiency in it
nekudot tovot — the good points still within a person, equated with the good spirit (ruach tovah) to be gathered out of the evil spirit in hitbodedut

the good spirit (ruach tovah) — the positive, holy portion of the spirit mixed within a person, which must be gathered and clarified out of the evil/melancholy spirit; identified in Likutey Moharan I:54 with the good points within a person and with the spirit of prophecy/holy spirit (per Psalms 143:10, 'Your good spirit shall lead me')
romach — the lance/spear, expounded as ruach + mem (spirit + the forty/worlds), in the Rabbah bar bar Chanah tale of the Arab riding under the raised knee
the spirit from the four winds (Ezekiel 37:9) — the ruach gathered from arba ruchot, embodied in the four-cornered tallit and the Thirteen Attributes

broken/crushed spirit (ruach nekhe'ah, cf. Proverbs 17:22) — the dejected, stricken spirit listed in LM I:54 among the evil spirits of sadness (alongside atzvut ruach and ruach ra'ah) that the melody played by hand must separate from the good spirit
ruach nishbarah ('a broken spirit', Psalms 51:19) — the broken spirit of a contrite heart, identified as the true olah-offering ('the sacrifices of God')

the evil spirit (ruach ra'ah) — the melancholic spirit of folly and sadness identified with the imaginative faculty, which opposes and confuses the good spirit of prophecy (as with Shaul in I Samuel 16)
sin'ah — hatred as a middah, identified as ruach ra'ah / turbulent air (Judges 9:23 with Rashi) that prevents speech from being heard
shiga'on — madness, the spirit of folly (ruach shtut) that enters a person, driven out by subduing the evil inclination
all the tzaddikim of the generation — the collective of generation's righteous, each one a shepherd (ro'eh) containing an aspect of Moshe and making a Mishkan

the shepherds of holiness (רוֹעִים דִּקְדֻשָּׁה) — the true tzaddikim who spiritually shepherd and lead Israel (as in 'you shall shepherd My people'), approachable only through holy boldness; not literal flock-herders
having compassion on others — the practice of actively showing mercy to another person, which in turn arouses Heavenly mercy upon oneself ('whoever has mercy on creatures, mercy is shown to him')

Mercy/compassion (rachamim) — the divine attribute of mercy that tempers strict judgment (din), associated with the name YHVH, Jacob, and the shining of the divine face, and likewise the quality of compassion aroused toward or shown by people
panekha ('Your face', Psalms 30:8) — God's face as the aspect of mercy/compassion, whose hiding (hastarat panim) characterizes exile
rachamim va-chasadim — mercy and lovingkindnesses as the quality of gadlut ha-mochin (expanded consciousness), 'da'at set between two divine Names' where El = chesed

simple mercy (rachamim peshutim) — the ordinary, limited divine mercy identified with plain mercy of Ze'ir Anpin, which humans can arouse through prayer and which itself must pray to and arouse the unbounded 'great mercy' (Likutey Moharan I:105)
rachamim stam of Ze'ir Anpin — plain/ordinary bounded mercy of the configuration Ze'ir Anpin, all humans can arouse, which must itself pray to awaken the great mercy
compassion (rachmanut) — the quality of mercy/pity that a person feels and shows toward others, which in turn arouses Divine mercy upon him

crown (atarah) — a royal diadem/coronet used as a symbolic aspect of honor and kingship (e.g., the crown of precious stones identified with compassion, and the crown made for the King from beautiful words)
ri"v din — the number 216 spelling 'din' (judgment), the gevurah-aspect of the veins (veridin/mantzpakh letters)
reisha — the head (Aramaic), in the Zoharic dictum 'and this menorah is the head', the seat of the brain/mochin
rinah — joyous song as a term for prayer ('to hear the rinah', I Kings 8:28), the heart's joy enabling the mountains/tzaddikim to sing
ra gamur — 'complete evil': the status of the seventy nations' languages as unmixed, total evil (unlike Nogah, which contains good to extract)
machaloket as verbal abuse — conflict defined as people reproaching/insulting a person, which brings on spiritual hunger and is the aspect of the foreskin (orlah)

Ra'ava d'Ra'avin — the Zoharic Aramaic term "Will of Wills," the supernal Divine Will of the Ein Sof from which all wills derive vitality, revealed at the time of Shabbat Minchah (when Moses passed away)
ra'avin — Aramaic 'wills' (as in ra'ava d'ra'avin, the Will of wills of Atika); here Malkhut is identified as the aspect of 'wills'

thunder (ra'am) — the audible thunderclap, in Likutey Moharan I:5 the sound produced when the voice/gevurot strike the brain ("the voice of Your thunder in the sphere"), from which spiritual 'thunders' are made to awaken the heart

nodes.he: מה שנותנין כבוד לזקן ששכח תלמודו
nodes.gloss: the act of giving honor to an elder who has forgotten his Torah learning (Berakhot 8b) — the deed that generates spiritual thunder, which brings cold reviving waters

the ways of God (darkhei Hashem) — the plural construct of derekh (way/path) with the Divine Name, denoting God's ways of conducting and governing the world, as in Hosea 14:10 'the ways of the LORD are straight' and Moses' request 'make known to me Your ways'
mi-sitra d'Yitzchak — 'from the side of Isaac': kabbalistic attribution of the gevurot (severities/thunders) to Isaac's left-side sefirotic lineage
hir'im — the verb 'He thundered' in Scripture, expounded (per Zohar) as the aspect of the supernal thunders (re'amim) born of gevurot
healing / medicinal remedy (refu'ah) — the cure of illness, whether bodily or spiritual, effected through means such as peace, faith, herbs, joy, or the shining sun
Shavuot, the Festival of Weeks — the holiday of the giving of the Torah (not שְׁבוּעוֹת 'oaths' nor generic 'weeks')
healing/remedy for the lungs (refu'ah le-ha-re'ah) — a cure for the lung organ (the five-lobed re'ah that moistens the body), effected e.g. by Shavuot/Torah or by oil; not any generic healing
medicinal remedies / cures (רְפוּאוֹת, plural of רְפוּאָה) — healing agents for bodily illness, such as herbal medicines; not 'healing' as an abstract act nor any other root
other people's wills that oppose one's own will — the inner definition of machaloket (conflict), annulled by fasting per 'nullify your will before His will' (Avot 2)
he'arat ha-raglayim — the illumination/light of the feet, revealed through dancing (rikkudin), paired with the illumination of the hands in clapping
'Adonai sefatai tiftach' (Psalms 51:17) — the verse opening the Amidah, 'O Lord, open my lips,' expounded as the aspect of wedding dancing
rikkudin shel chatunah — wedding dancing as a mystical act drawing the alephs/light of the heart down through the feet to the bride (Malkhut), sweetening her 320 judgments
reshimah — an engraved mark/inscription, like the letter tav inscribed on foreheads ('ve-hitvita tav,' Ezekiel 9:4); the trace-imprint sense of the root
rasha ve-ra lo — 'a wicked man who fares badly' (Berakhot 7a theodicy category): here the wicked person attached to the tzaddik whose halakhic opinion is NOT followed

nodes.he: רשע שמקרב להצדיק שאין הלכה כמותו
nodes.gloss: the wicked person who is drawn close to the tzaddik whose halakhic ruling is not accepted — the referent of 'rasha ve-ra lo' in the theodicy scheme
rasha ve-tov lo — 'a wicked man who prospers' (Berakhot 7a theodicy category): here the wicked person attached to the tzaddik whose halakhic opinion IS followed
the wicked person who is drawn close to the tzaddik whose halakhic ruling is accepted — the referent of 'rasha ve-tov lo' in the theodicy scheme
five times din — gematria device: din (64) × 5 = 320 (ShaKh), the harsh judgments of the bride/na'ar before the heh is drawn to her making five times 'Adonai'
tamar of the Sitra Achra — the demonic counterpart date-palm (temurah, 'exchange'), embodiment of the totality of harsh judgments opposing 'the tzaddik flourishes like a tamar'
se'or ke-kotevet — 'leaven the size of a date' (halakhic Yom Kippur measure, Berakhot/Yoma): leaven = concentrated judgments, the kotevet-date marking the Other Side's tamar
the phenomenon that one disciple is closer to the Rebbe than another — explained as due solely to his greater holy boldness (azut di-kedushah) to speak with him
the person who senses a slight impurity confusing him — one just outside/behind holiness (after the twelve tribes), disturbed by minor tumah, in the Rabbah bar bar Chanah tale
the aforementioned Jewish man's (the Israelite who had strayed) awakening/arousal to repentance (teshuvah), which restores even the wicked as a throne for holiness (Likutey Moharan I:4)

book (sefer) — a written sacred volume/text, as in a book of questions-and-answers formed from dispute, or the holy book equated by gematria with the Divine Name (not sfar 'border', sapar 'barber', or safar 'counted')
she'elot u-teshuvot — 'questions and answers' (responsa): the book generated from every dispute, punning teshuvah-answer with teshuvah-repentance
the attainment of the tachlit — meriting to reach the ultimate purpose/end, for whose sake the soul must ultimately leave the speech and 'glean in another field'

nodes.he: שבילי התורה, שיש בהם התבוננות גדול מאד.
nodes.gloss: shevilei ha-Torah — the hidden pathways of Torah containing very great contemplation, attainable only through great wealth ('if there is no flour, there is no Torah')

the breaking of the heart (shevirat ha-lev) — the heart shattered by shame/disgrace, as in 'cherpah shavrah libi' (Ps. 69:21), linked to forgetfulness and paralleled to the breaking of the Tablets ('the tablet of your heart')
shevirat ha-luchot — Moses' breaking of the Tablets, identified with the broken heart via 'write them on the tablet of your heart' (Proverbs 3)

the rectification of the coinage (tikkun ha-matbe'a) — Jacob's establishing/rectifying of coinage for the city (per the Talmudic reading of "vayichan penei ha-ir", Gen. 33:18), signifying in Likutey Moharan 23 the spiritual repair of money and the breaking of the craving for wealth through the shining light of the face
ruach nedivah — 'a generous/willing spirit' (Psalms 51:14): tzedakah as the cooling spirit that descends to quench the heart's burning craving for money
sheva gildei eina — the seven membranes/layers of the eye (Tikkunei Zohar), corresponding to Samson's seven locks and the seven middot of the mochin
sheva middot — the seven emotive attributes (lower sefirot) that pass fleetingly (cholfin) through the thought of the brain, matching the seven locks/eye-layers
shiv'ah gildei eina — the Tikkunei Zohar doctrine of the eye's seven layers (Intro 12, Tikkun 70), basis for the eyes being 'hairs'/seven machlefot of the head
shiv'im lashon — the seventy languages of the nations, identified with the storm wind/spirit of folly that rises via Targum-sleep to suckle from the Holy Tongue
shiv'im panim la-Torah — the seventy 'faces' (modes of interpretation) of the Torah, each distinct, clothed in stories to awaken the sleeper
shiv'im shanim — the seventy years (of a human lifespan), each different from the next, corresponding to the seventy faces of the Torah
shiv'ah ananim — the seven Clouds of Glory that form the sukkah, identified with the seven lamps (of the menorah) through which one attains divine influx
shiv'at yemei ha-mishteh — the seven days of wedding feasting after the chuppah, corresponding to the seven lamps/attainments of the surrounding light
shivrei luchot — the fragments of the broken first Tablets, the root of forgetfulness ('had the first Tablets not been broken, Torah would not be forgotten,' Eruvin 54)
b'nes — 'by miracle/sign': expounded as Shabbat, the eternal sign ('ot hi le-olam,' Exodus 31:17), the miraculous supra-natural order
the joy and delight of the World to Come — the future bliss identified with Shabbat ('a taste of the World to Come')
tefillah bi-dvekut — prayer said in devoted attachment to God, when the words flow willingly, elevating all previously scattered prayers
'shegurah tefillati be-fi' — R. Chanina ben Dosa's dictum (Berakhot 34b) 'my prayer is fluent in my mouth,' the sign of accepted prayer/devekut
the state in which God Himself prays — one's prayer becoming God's own prayer ('that He, blessed be He, will pray'), attained through Torah study
Lowliness/humility (shiflut) — the spiritual trait of holding oneself lowly, beneath one's own place and level, breaking one's pride before all others and even before one's own attained level

nodes.he: שומרת מההפך של עשירות, דהינו עניות,
nodes.gloss: the protective function of yirah guarding against poverty — fear of God as the treasure-house (otzar) that preserves wealth from its opposite, want
shokayim — the thighs/legs of the divine stature, symbolizing concealment ("the thigh is hidden"), identified with Esther as counterpart to Mordekhai's hands
shokin ve-raglin — thighs-and-legs as limbs of the supernal structure built through words of Torah and prayer, the "standing" aspect that elevates fallen sparks from food, drink, and clothing
the practice of reviewing one's learning 101 times — repetition of received teaching, contrasted with hearing the sage's fresh innovation directly
remembering what one receives from one's master — retaining the teacher's teaching, likened to ink whose clarity depends on hearing at the moment of innovation
the black of the eye (pupil, bat ayin) — the dark part of the eye that contracts and encompasses vast objects, symbol of holy tzimtzum/limitation
Shacharit — the morning prayer instituted by Avraham (Berakhot 26b), linked here to the "blackness" (shacharut) of dawn/Malkhut elevated through kindness

nodes.he: שצריך כל אחד לדבר בינו לבין קונו
nodes.gloss: the devotional practice of hitbodedut — each person speaking privately between himself and his Creator to make the point of wisdom shine and nullify the heart's foreskin

nodes.he: להמשיך את עצמו תמיד אל האמת לאמתו
nodes.gloss: the imperative to constantly draw oneself toward absolute truth (emet la-amito) — orienting one's descents and openings toward genuine truth so falls become ascents
guarding oneself from falsehood — avoidance of sheker as the condition for God's providence ("My eyes are on the faithful of the land") and closeness to divine Oneness
