nodes.gloss: the act of drawing up and revealing the deep waters, i.e., the counsels (eitzot) hidden in the heart — work of the ish tevunot (Prov. 20:5)
ikkar ha-refu'ah — the essence/mainspring of healing, which sprouts at daybreak through revealed counsel and grown faith (Isa. 58:8)

the revelation/disclosure of the counsel (hitgalut ha-eitzah) — the emergence into openness of the hidden divine counsel/advice, likened to light dispelling the darkness of 'absence of counsel' and to 'deep waters' drawn out, through which faith grows (Likutey Moharan II:5)
the incremental growth of faith — emunah growing greater as night is progressively pushed away toward daylight ('Your faithfulness in the nights')

counsels (eitzot) — divine/spiritual advice and guidance for the soul, the 'counsels from afar' (Isaiah 25:1) likened to waters from the depth of the heart through which faith grows (Likutey Moharan II:5)
the state of being rectified and receiving healing for the 'wondrous blows' (makkot mufla'ot) — cure of the incurable wounds via restored faith

the growth/flourishing of faith (גְּדֵלָה הָאֱמוּנָה, 'faith grows') — emunah increasing and being nurtured, in Likutey Moharan II:5 specifically as the result of the waters of counsels (etzot), per Isaiah 25:1 'counsels from afar, faithful and true'; from גָּדַל 'to grow', not any homograph of גדלה (e.g. גְּדֻלָּה 'greatness')
the restorative return whereby all the aforementioned aspects (faith, rain, herbs, healing) are rectified again through revealed counsels
eitzot revealed in the world — counsels made publicly known so each person can counsel his own soul, the source from which faith grows

nodes.he: לחתר ולמצא המים, שמשם גדלה האמונה
nodes.gloss: the act of digging/searching to find the waters from which faith grows — excavating the deep well of counsels (tikkun for fallen faith)
zekhut avot — the merit of the Patriarchs becoming revealed (an effect of restored faith/counsel)

nodes.he: הסדר של הזרעים לפי הזמן והמקום
nodes.gloss: the temporal-and-spatial ordering of seeds (seder ha-zera'im) — the divinely arranged conditions of when and where herbs grow and are harvested, effected through faith, which gives medicinal herbs their power to heal (Likutey Moharan II:5, citing 'emunah — this is Seder Zera'im', Shabbat 31)
the healing power possessed by herbs — their capacity to cure, conferred by their faith-ordained seasonal-spatial order
seder zera'im — the 'Order of Seeds' arrangement of plantings by time and place, identified with emunah (Shabbat 31a), the ordering that empowers herbs to heal

nodes.he: הסדר שיש להם לפי הזמן והמקום
nodes.gloss: the specific order herbs have according to time and place — the temporal-spatial arrangement of growth that gives medicinal potency
the herbs' principal power to heal — the essential curative force of medicinal plants, dependent on faith
ha-seder she-yesh la-zera'im — the divinely ordained order/arrangement governing seeds and their growth, the natural regularity sustained by faith that lets herbs sprout for healing
koach ha-refuah — the healing power/efficacy inherent in medicinal herbs, whose potency depends on faith-drawn rains
the sprouting/growth of herbs (צוֹמְחִים עֲשָׂבִים) — medicinal plants growing from the earth as a result of rainfall brought by faith, the source of all remedies (LM II:5)
rain (גֶּשֶׁם) — the precipitation that falls from heaven in the merit of faith, causing healing herbs to grow (Ta'anit 8); not גֶּשֶׁם in the sense of physical body/materiality (גשמיות)
asavim ha-gedelim — medicinal herbs as growing plants, the vegetal source of all remedies that sprout only through rains drawn by faith
sweat (זֵעָה) — bodily perspiration, especially the 'good sweat' produced through exertion in holiness, which expels the murkiness/venom of the blood and thereby generates joy (Likutey Moharan II:6)
the sick person's sweating — the clinical moment when a choleh breaks into sweat and joy is immediately drawn upon him, empirical sign that sweat produces simchah
good sweat (zei'ah tovah) — perspiration produced through exertion in a matter of holiness, which purifies the blood and generates joy (Likutey Moharan II:6)
simchat Yom Tov — festival joy, 'v'samachta b'chagekha' (Deut 16:14), the rejoicing of a 'good day' produced by holy sweat (extended to any day that is bechinat tov)
the expulsion of the murkiness/turbidity of the blood (akhirat ha-damim) from the body — as through good, holy sweat — leaving the blood pure and thereby producing joy (Likutey Moharan II:6)
damim zakim — clear/pure blood, the physiological state of unclouded blood that is the bodily substrate of joy
expulsion of the venom (eres) lodged in the murky blood — the toxin in turbid spleen-blood being discharged outward via sweat
chalashut — weakness/faintness, the debilitated bodily state caused by blood disorder, opposite of vigor and joy
the murkiness of blood confined in due measure to the spleen — turbid blood kept in its proper organ-boundary (the techol) rather than spreading
the blood remaining clear (damim zekhim) — the resulting purified-blood state once murkiness is confined to the spleen, enabling joy
sweating through a holy matter — the act of exerting oneself to perspiration in a davar shebikdushah, the 'good sweat' that generates joy

nodes.he: שנכנס בים החכמה, ששם נתגלה בחינת מלכות
nodes.gloss: entering the Sea of Wisdom where Malkhut is revealed — R. Yehoshua's vision of the great light in the yam (Bava Batra aggadah), Leviathan = Malkhut disclosed within supernal Chokhmah

nodes.he: התלמיד צריך שיהיה נכלל בבחינת בן
nodes.gloss: inclusion of the student within the aspect of son — the talmid being incorporated into bechinat ben ('mah'-perception) so that he attains yirah

reviewing/repeating aloud the novel Torah teaching (chiddush) innovated by the wise man of the generation — the practice (etza) of going over his chiddush, which arouses and reveals the Sea of Wisdom, draws sustenance to Malkhut, and awakens fear (LM II:7)
Yam ha-Chokhmah — the kabbalistic Sea of Wisdom, supernal Chokhmah as ocean from which Malkhut receives parnasah

nodes.he: כשמעינים ומדברים מאיזה חדוש, שחדש החכם שבדור
nodes.gloss: studying and discussing a chiddush of the chakham ha-dor — the act of reviewing the generation's sage's novel Torah teaching, which arouses the Sea of Wisdom

nodes.he: נופל יראה על זה שמדבר ומעין בהחדוש
nodes.gloss: fear falling upon the one who studies the chiddush — the yirah that descends on the reviewer because Malkhut (source of fear) arrives to draw sustenance

nodes.he: וכשהשמנים של הראה הם במזג השוה
nodes.gloss: the fats/oils of the lung in balanced temperament (mezeg ha-shaveh) — equilibrium of the re'ah's shemanim that makes the light of the countenance shine ('to brighten the face from oil')

Chanukah (חֲנֻכָּה) — the festival of dedication, understood in Likutey Moharan II:7 as the dedication/inauguration of the Holy Temple, effected through the Yom Kippur plea 'selach na' and revealing the light of the Divine countenance (or ha-panim)

The dedication of the House (chanukat ha-bayit) — the inaugural consecration of the Holy Temple, through which the Temple's aspects (son and student, the encompassing lights, the light of the Countenance) are activated to draw down sustenance; not the private house-warming celebration nor the festival of Chanukah per se

the inclusiveness/unification of the aspects of 'son' and 'student' (kelaliyut ben ve-talmid) — the merging of these two modes of receiving and revealing Godliness taught in Likutey Moharan II:7, through which the surrounding lights (makifim), the light of the countenance, illumination of the will at eating, and sustenance are drawn down

nodes.he: נעשה בחינת חנכת הבית, בחינת חנכה
nodes.gloss: chanukat ha-bayit / Chanukah — the dedication of the Temple effected through 'selach na' on Yom Kippur, the festival Chanukah as rectification of the churban
'Selach na' — Moshe's plea 'please forgive' (Num 14:19), the Yom Kippur forgiveness-petition whose letters hint at Chanukah

nodes.he: נמשך הפרנסה על ידי המלכות כנ"ל
nodes.gloss: the drawing down of parnasah via Malkhut — sustenance channeled through the sefirah Malkhut, which gathers everyone's trust and receives food from the supernal 'hands'

dominion (memshalah) — the measure of rulership/authority a person holds, a share in the aspect of Malkhut (kingship), through which sustenance (parnasah) is drawn down, as in 'and he shall rule over you' (Gen 3:16)
the ability to draw down sustenance through dominion — the husband's/ruler's memshalah ('he shall rule over you') empowering him to channel parnasah to dependents
et ha-akhilah — the time of eating, the meal as the occasion for receiving the illumination of the will (he'arat ha-ratzon)
illumination of the aspect of 'mah' — the shining of the unknowable 'what'-perception (wordless longing for God) received at eating by the ish chayil

nodes.he: כדי שלא יתבטל במציאות, ויהיה לו יראה
nodes.gloss: so that he not be nullified out of existence and instead have yirah — the protective purpose of interincluding son/student: preventing bittul bimtziut and preserving fear
meriting to raise up many students (ha'amadat talmidim harbeh) — the pedagogic achievement through which one attains the makifim
attaining the makifim — meriting to grasp the surrounding/encompassing lights, understanding what was previously beyond one's intellect

nodes.he: כשזוכה להשגה כזו, להאיר בגדולים וקטנים
nodes.gloss: Attaining the spiritual perception (hasagah) that enables the wise man to illuminate both the great and the small — lowering the lofty with the perception of 'What have you seen?' (mah) and raising the lowly with 'the whole earth is full of His glory' (Likutey Moharan II:7)
'all need him' — the universal dependence of great and small alike on the sage who can illuminate every level, hence his many students

nodes.he: יש לו כח ללמד עם כלם
nodes.gloss: the sage's power to teach everyone — his capacity to learn with all, high dwellers and low, giving each the perception suited to him
'he will raise many students' — the certain outcome that the sage with such attainment establishes numerous talmidim (fulfilling Avot 1:1)
shetok — the divine command 'Be silent! So it arose in thought' (Menachot 29b), silence as fence before the trans-temporal makifim

nodes.he: שלא יבוא למקיפים, שאין צריכין להשיגם
nodes.gloss: not entering makifim that need not/cannot be grasped — the restraint against penetrating surrounding lights above time whose questions time cannot resolve
revealing the inner intellect (sekhel penimi) — the act of disclosing one's internalized understanding to students, which vacates space for new light
a new further intellect arising in thought — the fresh makif-sekhel that 'ascends in machshavah' to replace the inner intellect once revealed
the sage's makifim entering inward — the surrounding lights of the chakham ha-dor becoming internalized when he instills his da'at in students (bechinat length of days, World to Come)

that the Torah teacher (tzaddik) reveal his wisdom and understanding to his students — the counsel of teaching/disclosing one's Torah insights to disciples ('my mouth speaks wisdoms, the meditation of my heart is understanding', Ps 49:4), which draws the hidden 'surrounding lights' (makifim) inward (Likutey Moharan II:7)

nodes.he: נתרוקן מחו מהשכל והדעת שהיה לו
nodes.gloss: the emptying of one's brain/mind of the intellect and da'at it previously held — by imparting one's understanding to another through speech/teaching — thereby vacating space for the surrounding lights (makifim) to enter as new, higher comprehension (Likutey Moharan II:7)
the surrounding intellect entering within (sekhel makif nikhnas lifnim) — the general dynamic whereby teaching a friend da'at and yirat shamayim internalizes one's makif
'his fear of sin precedes his wisdom' (Avot 3:9) — yirat cheto as prerequisite ordering, fear before chokhmah so one's words endure
'whoever has fear of Heaven, his words are heeded' (Berakhot 6b) — yirat shamayim in the speaker as the condition making speech effective and lasting

nodes.he: שלמד עמו תורה והכניס בו דעת
nodes.gloss: teaching him Torah and instilling da'at in him — the formative act by which a master makes his student into an 'adam' (before which he was mere human likeness)
'one who teaches his friend's son Torah' (Sanhedrin 99b) — the Talmudic case defining the teacher-as-maker, grounding student = son
'as if he made him' (ke'ilu asa'o) — the Talmudic dictum crediting the Torah teacher with creating the student's very being/body
shidaber im chavero b'yirat shamayim — the practice of speaking with one's fellow about fear of Heaven, the conversation-act that makes one a raiser of 'students'
l'hakhnis da'at ba-chavero — the act of instilling da'at (holy awareness) into one's fellow, the spiritual parallel to begetting children for the world's endurance
the relational state in which one's fellow is reckoned as a 'talmid' (student) toward him at the moment he enlightens him with a word of yirat shamayim

nodes.he: נחשב כאלו הוא בעצמו ממש נשאר בעולם
nodes.gloss: the halakhic-spiritual equivalence whereby leaving one's da'at below in a son/student counts as if the person himself literally remained in the world

nodes.he: צריכין להשאיר אחריו בן או תלמיד
nodes.gloss: the obligation to leave behind after one's death a son or a student who carries one's da'at, so the soul retains presence below

nodes.he: צריך שישאיר אחריו ברכה, בן או תלמיד
nodes.gloss: leaving behind a 'blessing' — a son or student — so that at departure the soul is simultaneously above and below, its true perfection
the state of the medameh (imaginative faculty) being clarified and rectified, the precondition for validly ascribing praises to God

nodes.he: יכולים לסדר שבחים ותארים לו יתברך
nodes.gloss: the resulting capacity to arrange praises and descriptive epithets (te'arim u-shevachim) for God, which operate only via the imagination since He is beyond all attributes
emunah as rectified faith — faith repaired through tikkun of the imaginative faculty, symbolized by 'chag' (festival/compass)
'ba-chodesh' (at the new moon) in Psalm 81:4 — homiletic symbol of chiddush ha-olam, the renewal of the world and the future new song
'tik'u' (blow!) in Psalm 81:4 — symbol of the revelation of divine glory, via 'I will fix him (u-teka'tiv) as a peg... a throne of glory' (Isa 22:23)

the revelation/disclosure of the Divine glory (hitgalut ha-kavod) — God's honor (kevod Hashem) becoming manifest in the world, which in Likutey Moharan II:8 is the aspect of tekiah ('u-teka'tiv yated... le-khise kavod', Isa 22:23), likened to the sun's shining ('u-khevod Hashem alayikh zarach'), and the root of souls from which prophecy spreads
kol Yaakov — the voice of Jacob, the holy voice/song that subdues the grip of Esau's power
the act of subduing the 'heel' (ekev) of the Sitra Achra — crushing the lowest hold of the Other Side via the future song's leap

watering the garden — the act (מַשְׁקֶה אֶת הַגָּן) by which the voice/melody, likened to the river issuing from Eden (Gen 2:10), irrigates the supernal garden where fragrances and awe/fear grow (Likutey Moharan II:8)
fragrances that grow in the garden — holy scents (symbolized by mountains and hills) nurtured in the supernal garden
harim u-geva'ot — 'mountains and hills' of Song 2:8, symbol of fragrances over which the future song leaps
the Ten Utterances (asarah ma'amarot) — the ten divine sayings of Genesis 1 through which the world was created and is sustained, the 'tools' of the work of Creation
the revelation of the Divine glory (kavod) — the disclosure of God's honor effected through the 'staff of strength' (the true leader's power), which in turn enables prophecy (Likutey Moharan II:8)

the 'staff of strength' (mateh oz, Psalms 110:2) — the forceful, judgment-charged prayer of the spiritually mighty person (baal koach), which lodges in the throat of the Sitra Achra forcing it to disgorge the swallowed holiness of Da'at, subdues Amalek, and reveals the Divine glory (Likutey Moharan II:8); מַטֵּה = staff (not מִטָּה, bed)

the prayer of the ba'al koach (person of great spiritual power, e.g. Pinchas) — a prayer deliberately offered in the aspect of constriction/judgment (din) that lodges in the Sitra Achra's throat and forces it to disgorge the swallowed prayers (Likutey Moharan II:8)

constriction and judgment (kimmutz va-din) — the contracted, severity-laden quality characterizing the prayer of the ba'al koach, likened to the 'staff of strength' and wordplay on kumtza (ant/handful) in LM II:8

nodes.he: שהסטרא אחרא שיש לה יניקה מן הדעת
nodes.gloss: the Sitra Achra insofar as it draws nurture (yenikah) from holy Da'at — the demonic parasitism on the knowledge of holiness, exemplified by Og
Og king of Bashan — the giant whose grip is in the 'right side,' sucking from holy Da'at, who uprooted the three-parasang mountain against Israel
the three kinds of compassion (shloshah minei rachmanut) drawn from the three mochin (intellects), which correspond to the three daily prayers, in Likutey Moharan II:8

the three daily prayer services (Shacharit, Minchah, Maariv) — the fixed thrice-daily prayers, which in Likutey Moharan II:8 are drawn from the three mochin and correspond to the three kinds of compassion

the three mochin (the three brains/mentalities — the kabbalistic triad of intellects, Chokhmah-Binah-Da'at, in the head), from which prayer and the three kinds of compassion are drawn, each serving as a spread-out partition (mechitzah perusah) guarding against sexual lust; vocalized מִשָּׁלֹשׁ הַמֹּחִין, 'from the three mochin'
mechitzot perusot — 'spread-out partitions,' the wordplay on 'parsei' (parasangs): the three brain-membranes/partitions guarding the camp's holiness
'tura' — the mountain of the Og aggadah (Berakhot 54b), interpreted as prayer, per 'My holy mountain... My house of prayer' (Isa 56:7)

nodes.he: בחינות תלתא פרסי, הינו תלת מחין
nodes.gloss: 'telata parsei' (three parasangs) as the telat mochin — the three brains/mental faculties from which prayer and the camp's guarding derive
guarding against the lust of adultery — the sexual self-guarding that constitutes the holiness of the camp of Israel
shemirah from ta'avat ni'uf via the three mochin — protection from sexual lust (nocturnal emission) effected by the three brains
garon — the throat, the bodily organ emerging from the lung, seat of 'honor God mi-geronekha' (from your throat)
the imaginings/fantasies that come upon a person during sleep — dream-images generated by the cold-moist imaginative faculty
the rainy season — the cold-damp time when sleep falls upon a person, physiological trigger of sleep and imagination
the falling of sleep upon a person — the state of drowsiness induced by cold and moisture (as in rainy weather)
sleep-and-imagination as a paired phenomenon — both dependent on the cold-moist lung, the physiological root of dreaming

the spreading/diffusion of prophecy (hitpashtut ha-nevuah) — the flowing forth of the prophetic spirit into the world, which in Likutey Moharan II:8 issues from the revelation of glory (root of Israel's souls), is identified with the wind of the lung's wings ('the spirit of Hashem spoke through me'), and rectifies the imaginative faculty and thereby true faith
the wind/breath (ruach) of the wings (lobes) of the lung — the airy spirit moving within the lung's lobes, identified in Likutey Moharan II:8 as the aspect of the spirit of prophecy
the essential sustaining (kiyum) of da'at/intellect — maintained through the body's fat delivered by the lung's breathing
shamnunit ha-guf — the fat/oiliness of the body, the fuel on which the intellect burns like a candle-flame

breathing (neshimah) — the respiratory breath of the lung, which raises and sustains the body's fat/oiliness to fuel the brain and Da'at (as in LM II:8), linked homiletically to neshamah; not the soul itself (נְשָׁמָה)
the essence of the brain and da'at as dependent on bodily fat raised to the brain by the lung's respiration
the sustaining of all the body's fat through breathing — respiration preserving the intellect's oily fuel

raising the body's fat (shamnunit ha-guf) up to the brain — the lung's function, via its breathing, of conveying the bodily fat that fuels the intellect (which burns like a candle) up to the moach, thereby sustaining Da'at (Likutey Moharan II:8)

the fat/oiliness of the body (shamnunit ha-guf) — the bodily fat that serves as fuel for the intellect, which burns like a candle upon it, raised to the brain by the lung's breathing (Likutey Moharan II:8)
the essence of da'at and the mochin (mentalities) — rooted physiologically in the body's fat, hence perfected via the lung
the lung's function of cooling the body's heat — tempering bodily fire, part of its wholesome constitution
tzinah u-kerirut — chill and coldness, the cold-moist quality of the lung underlying sleep and imagination
extracting all the swallowed holiness from the Sitra Achra — the mighty one's din-prayer (like Pinchas) that reclaims captured kedushah

the nullification/abolition of false beliefs (bitul emunot kozviyot) — the breaking down of idolatrous, deceitful faiths, associated in Likutey Moharan II:8 with the shevarim shofar-blast ('you shall surely break their monuments') and paired with the rectification of holy faith
hashra'at ha-Shekhinah — the indwelling of the Divine Presence, signified by 'teruah of the King' (Targum: 'the Shekhinah of their King is among them')
the moment of extraction from the Sitra Achra of what it swallowed — when even its own life-essence is drawn out with it

nodes.he: מוציאין גם עצמות חיותו, שהוא בחינת גרים
nodes.gloss: drawing out the Sitra Achra's very life-vitality along with the swallowed holiness — this essence being the aspect of gerim (converts)

the state in which da'at (holy knowledge/awareness) and the brain/mind are restored to wholeness and perfection — attained when the swallowed holiness of da'at is recovered from the sitra achra; identified with Rosh Hashanah as rectification of the head and mind (LM II:8)
the Sitra Achra's returning of the swallowed holiness of Da'at — whereupon the mind/Da'at becomes whole (Rosh Hashanah, tikkun of the 'head')

prayer in the aspect of judgment (din) and justice (mishpat) — the Rosh Hashanah mode of prayer that, as 'the judgment belongs to God,' forcibly extracts the life-force and sustenance the Sitra Achra drew from Israel's Da'at and prayers (LM II:8)
mismus — the 'melting/crushing' wordplay on 'mas oved' (Gen 49:15): Issachar's tribute-service read as the dissolution linked to bearing prophecy's yoke
ha-niggun, bechinat shir chadash — the melody as aspect of the 'new song' (shir chadash) of the future redemption, the song of wonders/providence
nittaken ha-rei'ach — the rectification of the sense of smell, the faculty restored through prophecy/rebuke (scent of the souls)
the "new song" (shir chadash) — the eschatological song of the future, associated in Likutey Moharan II:8 with melody/niggun and the renewal of the world, to be awakened in the time to come
the making of converts (gerim) and the consequent revelation of God's glory (kavod) — the paired effect wrought by prayer in Likutey Moharan II:8, which in turn causes prophecy to spread
nifla'ot shelo ke-derekh ha-teva — wonders/miracles beyond the natural order, i.e., conduct by pure Divine providence rather than nature
yitnaheg ha-olam al yedei nifla'ot — the future state in which the world will be conducted solely through wondrous providence after the renewal of the world
lehitkarev le-manhig amiti — the act of drawing close/attaching oneself to a true leader (tzaddik), sought through searching and prayer
she-yizkeh le-emunah amitit bi-shleimut — the goal of meriting true, complete holy faith (emunah), attained via closeness to the true leader
she-zokheh lehitkarev la-manhig ha-amiti — the merit/state of being drawn close to the true leader, whereby one's imagination and faith are rectified
nittaken ve-nitbarer etzlo bechinat ha-medammeh — the rectification and clarification of the imaginative faculty (koach ha-medammeh) effected in the follower by the leader's prophetic spirit
ha-ruach ha-kodesh she-yesh le-ha-manhig ha-amiti — the true leader's measure of holy spirit (ruach ha-kodesh), his 'different spirit' that is an aspect of prophecy

nodes.he: נתחזק ונתתקן אצלם האמונה האמתית דקדשה
nodes.gloss: nitchazek ve-nittaken etzlam ha-emunah ha-amitit di-kedushah — the strengthening and rectification of true holy faith in those who draw near the true leader
nittaken ha-medammeh — the rectified state of the imaginative faculty, achieved when it is 'in the hand of the prophets' (Hosea 12:11)

nodes.he: שנתקבצין ונתרבין ביותר נפשות ישראל ביחד
nodes.gloss: she-nitkabtzin ve-nitrabin beyoter nafshot Yisrael be-yachad — the gathering/aggregation of many Jewish souls together (kibbutz of Israel), which magnifies prayer

nodes.he: נתרבה ונתגדל ביותר מאד מאד בית התפלה
nodes.gloss: nitrabeh ve-nitgadel beit ha-tefillah — the exceeding enlargement of the 'house of prayer,' prayer magnified by each added Jewish soul/neighbor
u-khe-she-nislach he-avon — the state following forgiveness of sin, when the darkening cloud is removed and the sun shines to heal
selichat he-avon — forgiveness of sin, effected by abundance of prayers that disperses the sin-cloud so the healing sun shines

nodes.he: העננים, שהם הסטרא אחרא והקלפות, כלים והולכים
nodes.gloss: ha-ananim, ha-Sitra Achra ve-ha-kelipot kalim ve-holkhim — the dissipation of the 'clouds' (the Other Side and husks) through prayer, allowing the glory to be revealed
zerichat ha-shemesh — the shining/rising of the sun as symbol of the revelation of God's glory that brings healing (Malachi 3:20)

rectifying and subduing the war of Amalek — the tikkun that repairs and vanquishes Amalek's spiritual assault, i.e. the defilement of sexual lust (nocturnal emission) that Amalek draws from the blemished Da'at, accomplished through the aspect of the splitting of the Sea of Reeds (Likutey Moharan II:8)

nodes.he: התפלה של הבעל כח בחינת פינחס
nodes.gloss: ha-tefillah shel ha-ba'al koach, bechinat Pinchas — the forceful judgment-prayer of the man of spiritual power (aspect of Pinchas), the 'staff of strength' lodged in the Sitra Achra's throat
shibbarta rashei taninim al ha-mayim (Ps 74:13) — the breaking of the sea-serpents' heads, i.e., subduing the swallowing Sitra Achra to force it to disgorge holiness
nikhna bechinat ekev de-Sitra Achra — the subjugation of the 'heel' of the Other Side, its lowest grasp humbled through the rectifying voice
gedelim sham kol ha-reichot — the garden (watered by the voice/river from Eden) as place where all holy fragrances and fears grow
ke-she-ha-mokhiach ra'ui lehokhiach — the qualified rebuker: one fit to give rebuke, whose reproof adds fragrance to souls rather than fouling their scent
mosif ve-noten rei'ach tov be-ha-neshamot — the effect of worthy rebuke (like Moshe's after the Calf) that adds a good scent to the souls ('my nard gave forth its fragrance')
klei melakhah shel ma'aseh bereishit — the 'tools' of the work of Creation (symbolized by the ten-cubit axe, narga), instruments of the world's fashioning
mezona de-nishmata — Zoharic term: the 'food of the soul,' the sustenance of the neshamah (fragrance/spiritual nourishment) as opposed to bodily food

nodes.he: בטול אמונות כזביות ותקון האמונה הקדושה
nodes.gloss: bittul emunot kozviyot ve-tikkun ha-emunah ha-kedoshah — the nullification of false beliefs and rectification of holy faith, effected via the shofar sounds/rectified imagination

nodes.he: כשרואה אדם שבוער ביותר חוץ מהמדה
nodes.gloss: ke-she-ro'eh adam she-bo'er beyoter chutz me-ha-middah — the state of seeing oneself burning with fervor beyond proper measure, the storm-wind over-inflaming the heart (harisah, 'breaking through')
ve-chozer u-vo'er la-Shem yitbarakh — the heart's renewed, regulated burning toward God after the lung-wind cools its excess fire
afruriyut — earthiness/dusty sluggishness, the coarse element that dampens the heart's fervor (source of melancholy)
marah shechorah — black bile/melancholy, the depressive humor that clouds the mind and prevents guiding the brain at will
liba de-khol alma — Aramaic: the 'heart of the whole world,' the tzaddik/leader who functions as the cosmic heart
liba — Aramaic 'the heart,' the bodily organ of the Tikkunei Zohar passage that would burn the whole body without the lung-wings' breeze
manhigei ha-dor — the leaders of the generation, who correspond to the lung-wings cooling the world's heart
bedichah da'atah — cheerfulness/merriment of mind (Talmudic term), the joyous mental state enabling settled awareness
lema'lah na'aseh mi-zeh yichud gadol — the great supernal unification (yichud) effected Above by one's joy in his good point/Jewishness

the liberated mind (ha-moach meshuchrar) — the state in which the brain/intellect is freed and unfettered, achieved by binding joy to one's mind, enabling settled awareness (yishuv ha-da'at); from Likutey Moharan II:10
yishuv ha-da'at — settled mind/composure of thought, the deliberate mental clarity whose lack keeps people far from God
she-mekasher ha-simchah le-mocho ve-da'ato — the act of binding joy to one's brain and awareness, so that the mind can be governed at will
she-motzeh be-atzmo eizeh nekudah tovah — finding in oneself some good point (nekudah tovah, per 'azamerah' Torah 282) as the path to joy

one's mind and awareness becoming free (ben chorin) — the state, attained through joy (the world of freedom, 'for with joy you shall go out'), in which the mind and da'at are liberated from the exile imposed by melancholy, enabling one to direct the mind at will and settle one's thoughts (Likutey Moharan II:10)

nodes.he: יוכל להנהיג את מחו כרצונו ולישב דעתו
nodes.gloss: yukhal lehanhig et mocho kirtzono u-leyashev da'ato — the capacity, given by joy (world of freedom), to direct one's brain at will and settle one's mind
ke-she-mekasher simchah el ha-mo'ach — the condition of joining joy to the brain, the prerequisite state for attaining yishuv ha-da'at

nodes.he: נעשין בן חורין ויוצאין מן הגלות
nodes.gloss: na'asin ben chorin ve-yotz'in min ha-galut — the state of becoming a free person and exiting exile, attained through joy which is the world of freedom
olam ha-cherut — 'the world of freedom,' the kabbalistic realm (Binah/liberation) identified with joy, which enables one to direct the mind at will
the ability to direct/steer one's mind (moach) at will — mastery over one's own thought processes, which is possible only through joy and impossible under melancholy (Likutey Moharan II:10)
ve-yukhal le-yashev da'ato — the resulting capacity to settle one's mind (yishuv ha-da'at), achieved via joy governing the brain
be-vadai yashuv el HaShem — the certain outcome of returning to God once one settles the mind on the purpose of all worldly desires
sichah — prayer designated as 'conversation,' linked to siach ha-sadeh (Gen 2), the field-plants that join and empower one's prayer
praying in the field — the practice whereby all the grasses enter into and strengthen one's prayer (basis of hitbodedut outdoors)

secharchar — 'going round and round' (Psalms 38:11, 'libi secharchar,' my heart reels); the dizzying encircling of the heart by confused thoughts, which R. Nachman links via the Aramaic 'sechor sechor' (around) to kelipat Nogah that surrounds ('ve-nogah lo saviv') and twists the heart

the 'sealed utterance' (ma'amar satum) — the hidden, undisclosed first creative utterance of Genesis, identified with the word 'Bereishit' itself (one of the Ten Utterances of creation, but concealed rather than explicit), the supernal source from which vitality flows even to the lowest, filthy places (Likutey Moharan II:12)

Kelipat Nogah (קְלִפַּת נֹגַהּ) — the 'glowing husk,' the intermediate kabbalistic shell of Nogah (Ezekiel 1:4, 'and a brightness [nogah] around it'), which in LM II:12 is the kelipah that twists and encircles the heart with confusions (bechinat 'libi secharchar'), linked to the realm of Targum

the supernal glory belonging to the supernal utterance — the exalted divine glory (kavod elyon) associated with the hidden/sealed utterance 'Bereishit' (the ma'amar satum), identified with the question 'Ayeh mekom kevodo' ('Where is the place of His glory?'), the concealed source from which vitality flows even to the filthy places (Likutey Moharan II:12)
sustaining oneself from the vitality of holiness — drawing life from the hidden divine life-force even in impure places (e.g., the great city of Rome)
Torah itself — the Torah as an entity that walks before a person on his path ('when you walk it shall lead you,' Prov 6:22)

nodes.he: קדם שמחדשין יש כמה ספקות ובלבולים
nodes.gloss: the doubts and confusions preceding chiddushim — the state of uncertainty and mental turmoil that precedes every Torah innovation

"Ayeh" (אַיֵּה) — the interrogative "Where?", specifically the seeker's cry "Where is the place of His glory?" (אַיֵּה מְקוֹם כְּבוֹדוֹ), the aspect of searching for God's hidden glory from places of concealment/filth, as expounded in Likutey Moharan II:12 (linked to "Where is the lamb for the burnt offering," Gen. 22:7); not the bird אַיָּה (falcon/kite) nor the proper name Ayah
seh la-olah — the lamb for the burnt offering (olah), the korban that atones for sinful thoughts/musings of the heart

nodes.he: הוא חוזר ועולה אל הכבוד העליון
nodes.gloss: returning and ascending to the Supernal Glory — the ascent effected when one asks 'Ayeh — where is the place of His Glory?' after falling into filthy places
'he will surely never stumble' — the guaranteed protection from error attained by walking in simplicity (temimut) rather than following one's own cleverness

"his lips" (siftotav) — the possessed plural of שָׂפָה (lip), specifically as quoted from Song of Songs 5:13 "His lips are roses, dripping with flowing myrrh," expounded as an aspect of holy speech issuing from the mouth
'abirei lev ha-rechokim mi-tzedakah' (Isa 46:12) — the 'stout-hearted far from charity,' the hard stone-heart of those who withhold tzedakah
lev even — the 'heart of stone' (Ezek 36:26), the hardened heart that tzedakah/water transforms (rock turned into a pool of water)
YaBoK (yud-bet-kuf) — acronym Yichud-Berakhah-Kedushah (Unity, Blessing, Holiness), the river Yabbok as kabbalistic cipher formed through charity
rose (shoshanah) — the rose/lily flower of Song of Songs 5:13 ("his lips are shoshanim"), used as a mystical symbol (e.g., of holy speech, of Esther/the Shekhinah); not the personal name Shoshanah
torei — the ox (Aramaic 'tora') of Shabbat 77b with its long tail, symbol of the great tzaddik to whom the false-prophet 'tail' attaches
tzaddikim ha-gedolim — the great (publicly wondrous) tzaddikim, whose greatness gives the lying imposters a point of attachment
navi u-moreh sheker — the false prophet and lying teacher (Isa 9:14), identified as 'the tail' attached to the great tzaddikim
zanav — the tail (Isa 9:14), body-part symbol of the false prophet/hypocrite trailing after the great tzaddik (the long-tailed ox)
gamla — the camel (Shabbat 77b, short-tailed), symbol of the simple tzaddik ('like a weaned child,' ke-gamul, Ps 131:1) who serves in silence
tzaddik ha-pashut — the simple/plain tzaddik who acts with simplicity and silence, not speaking great and wondrous things

the fact that the aforementioned liars exist — i.e., the existence of the fraudulent imitators of the true tzaddikim (Likutey Moharan II:15), whose presence is paradoxically a benefit to the true tzaddik by diverting the tainted charity of the wicked toward themselves

nodes.he: נצול הצדיק האמת מפגם הצדקה שלהם
nodes.gloss: the true tzaddik being saved from the flaw of the wicked donors' charity — protection from the blemish in tzedakah given by resha'im, effected via the imitators
YaBoK in holiness — the holy configuration of Yichud-Berakhah-Kedushah produced when charity reaches the true tzaddik
YaBoK as acronym — Yichud (unity), Berakhah (blessing), Kedushah (holiness), three aspects all stated of water/tzedakah
the holy mouth of the tzaddik — the tzaddik's faculty of holy speech, received from charity-givers ('nidvot pi,' Ps 119:108)
agam mayim — the 'pool of water' (Ps 114:8) into which the rock-heart is turned; water as symbol of tzedakah
lev rakh — the soft/tender heart, the generous heart melted like water, opposite of the stone heart, source of tzedakah
nedivei lev — the 'generous of heart' (freewill donors), from whom the tzaddik receives the speech of his mouth
ba'alei tzedakah — givers of charity, the donors who supply the true tzaddik's holy speech
seeing the King in His crown — beholding the King in beauty and greatness ('a king in his beauty your eyes shall behold,' Isa 33:17), not in smallness
imrei shefer — 'goodly/beautiful sayings' (Gen. 49:21): the beautiful words of prayer/speech refined from the 'royal delicacies,' which ascend to form a crown for the King

berurim — the kabbalistic 'refinements': the progressive sifting and extraction of holy sparks from food/sustenance (as in Likutey Moharan II:16, where grain is refined stage by stage from animals to the nations to Israel, culminating in blessings and prayer, the aspect of the ketoret); plural of בֵּרוּר (refinement/clarification), not בָּרוּר 'clear/evident' nor 'chosen ones'

nodes.he: התחברות שמתחברין האמרי שפר עם המלך
nodes.gloss: the joining of the imrei shefer with the King — the union of the 'beautiful words' (blessings/prayers from food) with the King, forming His crown
chatunah — the wedding day ('on the day of his wedding,' Song 3:11), the day of the crown/union of King Solomon, symbol of the joining above
ketoret — the incense offering, kabbalistically the aspect of berurim (refinements/sifting of sparks) from food
ma'adanei melekh — 'royal delicacies' (Gen 49:20), the refined food from which imrei shefer (blessings) and the King's crown are made
the essence of the honor and greatness of kingship — malkhut's true glory, achieved specifically through humility ('before honor, humility,' Prov 15:33)
ikkar ha-malkhut — the essence of kingship itself, established through anavah (humility)

nodes.he: שכל הפרנסה של ישראל צריכין לקבל
nodes.gloss: that all Israel's livelihood must be received via the King — parnassah channeled through malkhut (the tree with 'food for all,' Dan 4:17)
a person doing good — the good deeds a person performs, which God regards while overlooking the bad ('He beheld no iniquity in Jacob,' Num 23:21)
God guiding him with hashgachah — divine providence directing the person as a result of judging favorably/looking only at the good
on Shabbat through joy — the Shabbat state in which simchah frees one from weekday servitude, making Da'at whole and fear of God complete

elevating the fallen fears — the spiritual practice/process of raising degraded, misdirected awe (fear mixed with foolishness, e.g. fears of worldly things) back to their root, restoring them as complete fear of Heaven joined with Da'at (as taught in Likutey Moharan II:17)
yere Shabbat — one who fears Shabbat: fear of God attained in the Shabbat state, contrasted with weekday fear mixed with foolishness (LM on Shabbat-yirah with Da'at)
ta'anug ve-simchah shel Shabbat — the delight and joy of Shabbat as a devotional state, source of complete fear-with-Da'at, opposed to weekday servitude

freedom (cherut) as the absence of servitude (shi'bud) and exile (galut) — the liberated state characteristic of Shabbat, in which the mind (da'at) is unconfused and complete, unlike the weekday state of bondage that muddles awareness (LM II:17)
yirah bi-shleimut im Da'at — fear of God in completeness, i.e. fear joined with mature awareness (Da'at), free of the foolishness of Job 4:6

Amalek (עֲמָלֵק) — the biblical nation/archetype of heresy, here specifically as the spiritual force of philosophical denial and godless intellect: the 'stumbling stone' of heretical wisdom that denies faith and fear of God
ha-pilosofim ve-ha-kofrim — the philosophers and heretics as a class of persons who allegorize the whole Torah and its practical mitzvot into mere 'form and intellect'
even negef be-khol chokhmah — the 'stumbling stone' lurking within each of the seven secular wisdoms, identified as the aspect of Amalek that causes the inquirer to fall into heresy

the essential/primary attainment of the ultimate purpose (ikkar hasagat ha-takhlit) — the true means of reaching life's final goal, achieved through simple faith and practical mitzvot rather than philosophical inquiry
mitat ha-ishah ha-harah — the death of the struck pregnant woman (Ex 21:22 'ason'), symbolizing destruction of the hidden path/wisdom itself as punishment-scenario, not mere miscarriage
ha-derekh chokhmah be-atzmo — the 'way of wisdom' itself (Prov 4:11), the new spiritual path in gestation, which strife may ruin along with its premature offspring
ishah harah — the pregnant woman of Ex 21:22 as symbol of a spiritual path still in gestation/concealment before its revelation to the world
ha-mefursamim she-na'asin kodem zemanam — leaders who become famous before their time, spiritual 'stillbirths' (nefalim) expelled prematurely by strife, punished with death or poverty
yotze kodem zemano — emerging before one's time: premature exit from the hidden gestation (ibbur) of a new path, producing a nefel-like figure
beginning to enter a path — the initial entry into a not-yet-revealed spiritual way, constituting the state of herayon (conception/pregnancy) requiring concealment
herayon — pregnancy as kabbalistic symbol: the gestation-stage of a new spiritual path/teaching still concealed (linked to Prov 4:11 'be-derekh chokhmah horeitikha')

nodes.he: ללמד פוסקים קדם החדוש שמחדש ואחר כך
nodes.gloss: studying poskim (halakhic codes) before and after innovating chiddushei Torah — the protective practice surrounding Torah novellae

nodes.he: נעשין בחינת אנשי חיל מלפניהם ומלאחריהם
nodes.gloss: anshei chayil formed before and behind — the guard of 'men of valor' (cf. Song 3:7-8) generated by poskim-study, stationed around Torah novellae so no stranger (zar) approaches
when a person is joyful — the state of simchah in which melancholy and sufferings are pushed aside to the periphery (setting of the dance-circle parable)

nodes.he: המרה שחרה ויסורים נסתלקים מן הצד
nodes.gloss: the melancholy (marah shechorah) and sufferings withdrawing to the side — the displaced-but-not-transformed sorrow standing outside the circle of joy
simchah ve-ha-rikkudin — the joy and dancing (the machol/dance-circle) that heals and into which even the bystander-sorrow is forcibly drawn; foretaste of the future dance
cholah/machol — the dance-circle of the righteous in the World to Come, at whose head God will stand (Yerushalmi Sukkah wordplay rosh cholah)
tikkun ha-cholah — rectification via the dance-circle (machol), the future perfected joy that heals illness (choleh) born of melancholy
making Torah into prayer — the practice of turning learned Torah into personal supplication during hitbodedut, which generates great delight above
sha'ashu'im gedolim le-ma'alah — the great supernal delight aroused Above by hitbodedut speech and turning Torah into prayer
attaining great stature — the high spiritual level reached by every soul, small or great, through the practice of hitbodedut
the 248 limbs (ramach evarim) — the body's limbs corresponding to the 248 positive mitzvot, each clothed with Moshe who reminds it of its mitzvah
hitlabshut Moshe ba-evarim — Moshe Rabbeinu's enclothement within every limb of each Jew, prompting each limb to its mitzvah (forgotten through drunkenness)
hitlabshut ha-Da'at ba-chasadim — the kabbalistic enclothement of Da'at within the chasadim (kindnesses), the structure affected by measured drinking
mitpateh u-mitpayes — being appeased and conciliated: the softening/sweetening effect on judgments when Da'at is elevated through proper measured drink
when the Da'at is elevated — the state of uplifted awareness/mind (via moderate drink) that raises the chasadim clothed within it
the chasadim being elevated and magnified — the growth of the kindnesses that accompanies the broadening and elevation of Da'at
drinking in measure according to one's capacity — moderate wine-drinking suited to one's level, which broadens Da'at rather than causing drunkenness
one's mind broadened and brain elevated — the cognitive expansion (harchavat ha-da'at) produced by properly measured drinking
a little drinking according to need — the small, necessary quantity of drink that benefits and broadens the mind (vs. excess)
leharchiv da'ato — broadening one's Da'at/mind: expansion of consciousness as the beneficial effect of minimal drink
meriting the annulment of vows (hatarat nedarim) — attaining release from one's vows, whose delay otherwise causes idolatry, sexual immorality, bloodshed, and evil speech (Likutey Moharan II:27)
being saved from the four traits — deliverance from idolatry, sexual immorality, bloodshed, and evil speech (the four evils of the delayed vow, per Vayikra Rabbah on Jacob)
assessing each person fairly — the just leader's practice of weighing each individual to apportion the communal burden rightly, which nullifies the four evil traits

nodes.he: יכול להכיר את איש ישראלי בין האמות
nodes.gloss: the ability to recognize a Jew among the nations — the discernment power (parallel to distinguishing which Torah may be written) to identify an ish Yisraeli among the gentiles
ha-yichudim ve-ha-zivvugim — the supernal unifications and couplings (of divine partzufim), all of which are the aspect of 'nullifying the forbidden' (bittul issur)
bittul issur — halakhic nullification of a forbidden admixture in the permitted, serving as symbol of supernal unification (forbidden becoming permitted, as arusah→nesuah)

The destruction and uprooting of the books of the heretics (sifrei ha-minin) — the on-high kal vachomer outcome in Likutey Moharan II:32 whereby, since even God's holy Name/holy books may be erased for the sake of peace, the heresy-spreading books that cast hatred and strife among Israel are all the more surely blotted out and eradicated
the loss of holy books — the burning/perishing of tzaddikim's sacred writings, likened to the Sotah scroll's divine Name erased for marital peace

nodes.he: שבשביל השלום שביניהן נמחין ונאבדין הספרים
nodes.gloss: books erased and lost for the sake of peace between them — the sacrifice of holy writings ('My Name written in holiness') to preserve the peace of the supernal holy couple
when the books are burned and lost — the tzaddikim's deliberate concealment/destruction of their Torah writings to remove the ruach kin'ah (spirit of jealousy) threatening the holy couple's union

nodes.he: הצדיקים הגדולים להעלים תורתם, לשרפן ולהאבידן
nodes.gloss: the great tzaddikim's concealing of their Torah by burning and destroying it — a deliberate act to remove the spirit of jealousy and protect the peace of the holy couple
godel ha-ahavah — the greatness/intensity of love, the cause on account of which the spirit of jealousy arises even among the pure
the act of being jealous over her — the spirit of jealousy's zealous guarding of the beloved (the holy couple), an expression of true love per the Zohar
ruach kin'ah — the 'spirit of jealousy' (Numbers 5:14), identified as the spirit of Mashiach that is zealous against adultery

The 'spirit of God' (ruach Elokim) — the divine spirit that hovered over the waters (Genesis 1:2) and filled Bezalel with wisdom (Exodus 31:3); in Likutey Moharan the God-given prophetic/inspired spirit identified with the spirit of Mashiach, the comprehensive spirit (ruach ha-kollel) of the true leader (Moshe), and the mochin — not 'wind' in the meteorological sense, nor a human spirit as such
bechinat Mashiach — the 'aspect of Mashiach,' a messianic quality/level present within a person or a tzaddik's Torah-book
'according to his holiness and purity' — the measure of a person's sanctity and purity that determines the degree of the aspect of Mashiach he possesses
the state of possessing an aspect of Mashiach — having a share of the messianic spirit by virtue of one's holiness

nodes.he: שמי שנכתב בקדשה, ונתפשט בעולם ועושה שם
nodes.gloss: 'My Name that was written in holiness' (sotah-scroll phrase) — the divine Name inscribed in sanctity that spreads through the world and makes a name, identified with the holy book (sefer = shem by gematria)

the Name of God (Shem Hashem, שֵׁם ה') — the divine Name of the Tetragrammaton as a sacred entity/presence, e.g. 'a strong tower is the Name of God' (Prov. 18:10), identified with the holy book (sefer = shem in gematria) and with the tefillin/pe'er ('the Name of God is called upon you')
hitnotzetzut — the sparkling/flashing of light that flashes from one joy to its fellow when joys are included together
the growing and increase of the light — the intensification of joy's radiance produced by joys being merged at their root
kelaliyut — the inclusiveness whereby one joy is incorporated into its fellow, the mechanism that magnifies joy's light
the maximal magnification of the light of the joys — the greatly increased radiance resulting from all joys being included together at their single root
coming to mochin de-gadlut — the transition to expanded consciousness (kabbalistic 'mentalities of greatness'), identified as hamtakah (sweetening of judgments)
seeing the tzaddik in his beauty and splendor — beholding the true tzaddik at the time of the gathering (kibbutz), the fulfillment of 'the king in his beauty shall your eyes behold' (Isaiah 33:17)
merchakim — 'far distances' (Isaiah 33:17 'eretz merchakim'), a name for chokhmah/wisdom perceived from afar, linked to the Land of Israel

truthfully gazing upon the true tzaddik — attentively beholding the genuine tzaddik (who, by drawing people to God's service, embodies God's glorying in Israel), the practice by which one comes to 'see' the divine self-glorification and receive its glory/mochin (LM II:40)
receiving from the hitpa'arut — obtaining pe'er (glory) and mochin from beholding God's glorying in Israel, which forms tefillin within the beholder
bechinat einayim — the 'aspect of eyes': spiritual eyes formed when the tefillin-mochin break through, becoming like the eyes of Hashem that watch over the Land

The watchful providence of God, blessed be He — His supervising 'gaze' (hashgachah) over the world, aroused through Israel in whom He glories, which in Likutey Moharan II:40 generates the holiness of the Land of Israel
hitpa'arut — God's glorying/taking pride (in Israel), the divine self-adornment from which the tefillin-pe'er and divine 'eyes' of providence are formed

nodes.he: נשמות ישראל, שהשם יתברך מתפאר בהם
nodes.gloss: the souls of Israel as the object of God's glory — nishmot Yisrael in whom God takes pride ('Israel in whom I glory,' Isaiah 49:3), the source arousing divine providence
hitpatchut ha-chokhmah — the opening/unfolding of wisdom, the intellectual expansion produced by the air of the Land of Israel that makes wise

nodes.he: שהשם יתברך מסתכל בארץ ישראל תמיד
nodes.gloss: God's constant gazing at the Land of Israel — perpetual divine providence over Eretz Yisrael ('the eyes of Hashem are upon it from year's beginning to year's end')
the sanctity of the Land of Israel and its wisdom-conferring air — Eretz Yisrael's property of sanctifying and its atmosphere that 'makes wise' (avira de-Eretz Yisrael machkim)
speaking faith aloud with the mouth — the verbal articulation of emunah, which itself constitutes faith and brings one to faith ('I will make known Your faithfulness with my mouth,' Ps 89)
ha-nekudah ha-penimit — the inner point: Shabbat as the central point from which the six weekdays (the surrounding circles) draw sustenance; symbol of the true tzaddik one travels to
the obstacles, incitements, and enticements — the kelipah-generated hindrances that block one from reaching the tzaddik, mere illusions like the Baal Shem Tov's imaginary walls
chomot — the illusory walls of the Baal Shem Tov's parable, conjured by the king around his treasure; obstacles that are only achizat einayim (optical illusion)
speaking of the salvation of Israel — discourse about yeshu'at Yisrael, the holy speech near which the subtle kelipah lurks at the giving-over of Torah
the fleeing of the subtle kelipah — the escape/dispersal of the fine husk that borders holiness when it is denied nurture during the tzaddik's Torah teaching

nodes.he: ולעשות עניני שטות וצחוק או קפיצות ורקודים
nodes.gloss: doing acts of silliness, laughter, jumping and dancing — deliberate foolish merriment used as a device to attain and maintain joy
'and then it will depart' — the withdrawal of the disturbing thought/evil inclination when one stubbornly refuses to attend to it
the evil inclination's departure — the yetzer hara giving up and going away when a person is firm-minded and obstinate against it

nodes.he: אי אפשר שנבין ונשיג בשכלנו הנהגתו יתברך
nodes.gloss: The impossibility of humanly comprehending or grasping with our intellect God's conduct/governance of the world (hanhagato yitbarakh), owing to His exaltedness beyond our understanding — the principle in LM II:52 that questions against God are therefore fitting and inevitable
the fittingness of there being unanswerable questions upon God — kushiyot on the Blessed One as proper and beautiful given His exaltedness beyond our minds

nodes.he: מעצם גדלתו ורוממותו, שהוא מרומם מאד מדעתנו
nodes.gloss: God's immense greatness and exaltedness beyond our understanding — the very transcendence that makes it necessarily impossible for our minds to grasp Him, hence the questions

the interspace between mitzvot (בֵּין הַמִּצְווֹת) — the precious connective aspect existing between one mitzvah and the next, which links each mitzvah to its fellow so that 'mitzvah draws along mitzvah' (Likutey Moharan II:59)
revealing chasadim — the disclosure of divine kindnesses effected through revealing novel Torah insights (chiddushei Torah)

nodes.he: שמה שנמשך אלקותו יתברך, כביכול, ברהטי מחין
nodes.gloss: the flowing of God's divinity, as it were, into the 'runnels of the brains' (rehatei mochin) — Godliness drawn down into the channels of the mind through Torah innovation
tefisah — the prison/imprisonment: Rabbi Akiva's incarceration, attributed by Rabbi Shimon to his expounding Torah publicly before unworthy hearers
the drawing down of Elokut — divinity being drawn into the world through revealed Torah innovations ('that they take for Me an offering')
kesil — the 'fool': the unworthy hearer of Torah (also the star-name Kesil/Orion), into whom honor is diverted when unfit students listen
talmid she-eino hagun — an unworthy/unfit student whose hearing of publicly taught Torah causes withholding of rain

mar kilus — the Sages' etymology of the idol-name Markulis (Merkurius) as "exchange of praise/honor" (chiluf ha-kavod), i.e. honor inverted into degradation, cited re teaching Torah to an unworthy student (Chullin 133a)
chiluf ha-kavod — the exchange/diversion of honor: glory passing from the Torah to the unworthy, disrupting the cloud-and-rain flow that depends on kevod HaShem
Markulis (Merculis) — the Roman idol Mercury, paradigm of idolatry served by stone-throwing; named as the archetypal avodah zarah

the honor/glory of the Torah (kevod ha-Torah) — the dignity accorded to the Torah itself, which when upheld draws down rain (paralleling the glory of God appearing in the cloud) and is damaged by teaching Torah to unworthy students

Rain (גְּשָׁמִים, plural of גֶּשֶׁם) — the literal precipitation that waters the earth, formed from vapors rising from the ground and drawn down through the cloud and the honor/glory of God and the Torah; its withholding (עֲצִירַת גְּשָׁמִים) is a punishment. Not גַּשְׁמִי/גְּשָׁמִים in the sense of 'corporeal/material things' (physicality), nor the personal name Geshem.
the cessation of invading troops and wars — the state in which armies and warfare stop (so the vapors again produce rain, not bloodshed)
the vapors/mists rising from the earth (Gen 2:6 'ed') — the meteorological-symbolic source from which rain is formed
the principle that the greater the intellect — the measure of an expanded sekhel, which correspondingly shrinks time
time diminishing and becoming nullified — the contraction of the category of time as intellect grows toward God who is above time
mas'ei Bnei Yisrael — the journeys of the Children of Israel (Num 33:1), travels from place to place that atone for the blemish of idolatry
that God grant us compassion (rachmanut) — the sought bestowal of divine mercy upon Israel through the journeys

the state/condition in which the blemish of idolatry (pegam avodah zarah — the corruption of faith counted as idolatry even absent actual idol-worship) has been atoned for, e.g., through the journeys of Israel (Likutey Moharan II:62)
the drawing down of mercy (rachmanut) — compassion flowing from above as a result of atoning for the idolatry-blemish
the sweetening of the charon af — mitigation of God's burning wrath aroused by the blemish of idolatry
turning aside from God — the state of deviation from Hashem (flawed faith) that constitutes the blemish of idolatry
nesiot — physical travels/journeyings from place to place, the concrete acts embodying 'the journeys of Bnei Yisrael' that atone
mazon — food/sustenance ('food for all is in it,' Dan 4:9), nourishment flowing through the king-tree who holds the complete melody
the clarification/separation of the human spirit from the animal spirit — effected by the shepherd's melody
being saved from the animalistic spirit — the shepherd's rescue, via his melody, from descending to ruach ha-behemah
the song and melody each shepherd knows — the unique niggun corresponding to the grasses and place where he pastures

nodes.he: נותן כח בעשבים, ויש מרעה לבהמות
nodes.gloss: the melody's giving power to the grasses so there is pasture for the animals — niggun as vitalizer of vegetation and grazing
onashim — punishments generally, all reckoned as an aspect of death (e.g., poverty, Ex 4:19), which uproot a person from the root of his vitality
the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He (Aramaic Zoharic phrase 'shema de-Kudsha Brikh Hu', Zohar Yitro 88b, cited as the teaching that Shabbat is God's Name)
the act of coming to the tzaddik and seeing him (Isa 30:20) — beholding the tzaddik's face so as to find one's own middot reflected within him

the 'simple foundation' (yesod ha-pashut) — the single, undifferentiated primal element/foundation underlying the four elements and all creation, which the true tzaddik embodies as the root of the world (cf. tzaddik yesod olam); not a physical building foundation nor the sefirah name in isolation

the three colors of the eye together with the pupil (bat ayin) — the Zoharic/kabbalistic aspect of the eye's components (tlat gevanin de-eina u-vat ayin), drawn from the four-letter Divine Name and corresponding to the mochin, the power of sight, and the letters of Shabbat (shin = three colors, bat = pupil), as expounded in Likutey Moharan II:67
the beauty and splendor (yofi u-pe'er) of the world — the epithet in Likutey Moharan II:67 for the true tzaddik (identified with Yosef) as the world's aesthetic glory and adornment

"Rosh Bayit" (Head of the House) — Rabbi Nachman's homiletic reading of "Bereishit" (בראשית = ראש בית) in Likutey Moharan II:67, denoting the true tzaddik as the head/master of the house of the world, from whom all generations are drawn and through whom the Temple and the dwellings of Israel are sustained

the Master of the House of the world (baal ha-bayit shel ha-olam) — the true tzaddik as the world's householder/proprietor, the 'head of the house' (rosh bayit = Bereishit) from whom all generations are drawn and through whom the Temple and Israel's dwellings are sustained (LM II:67)
the true tzaddik (הַצַּדִּיק הָאֱמֶת) — the singular authentic righteous leader of the generation, the Yosef-figure who is the beauty and splendor of the world and its 'master of the house'

the power/faculty of sight (koach ha-re'ut) — the visual capacity of the eye, which in LM II:67 is drawn from the divine Name (the four letters), the source of the three colors of the eye and the pupil
the 'head' of the Sitra Achra — the counterfeit chief of the Other Side, demonic counterpart to the tzaddik who is the head of holiness
the famous men of falsehood (mefursamim shel sheker) — leaders with false, undeserved renown who oppose the true tzaddik and draw their status from the side of impurity

the light/luminary of the eyes (me'or ha-einayim) — the illuminating power of eyesight, identified in Likutey Moharan II:67 with the 'luminaries of light' (me'orei or) and with the three colors of the eye plus the pupil, all drawn from the Name of God
shem ha-kodesh — the holy divine Name, clothed and partnered within the tzaddik's name ('His Name is joined with our name')
pe'er ve-hiddur — splendor and adornment (as in hiddur of the etrog), the beautification-quality flowing from the tzaddik who is the head
the names of impurity of the chitzonim — defiled names belonging to the external/demonic forces, opposite the holy Name
all the members of the generation — the people of the dor, who are all drawn from the tzaddik who is 'head' (koreh ha-dorot me-rosh)
bnei bayit — members of the household: the generation as the 'house' relative to the tzaddik who is its rosh bayit (head of house)
Noach — the biblical righteous man ('ish tzaddik tamim'), figure of the tzaddik who departs and is concealed, subject of the Bereishit-eulogy
the endurance/upkeep of the houses and dwellings of Israel — sustained through the true tzaddik, the world's ba'al ha-bayit
the endurance/sustenance of the Beit HaMikdash — the Temple's standing, maintained through the tzaddik (Yosef, rosh bayit)
the endurance of Israel's dwellings — the preservation of Jewish homes, dependent on the tzaddik as master of the house
being saved from fires/conflagrations — protection from destructive burning attained by mourning the Temple (subduing me'orei eish)

dwelling (dirah) — a residence/abode, specifically the dwelling-place of the Divine Presence below, as embodied in the Holy Temple (and illuminated by Shabbat); not any verbal or other homographic form

mourning (hitpael, mit'abel) — actively grieving over the destruction of the Holy Temple / Zion, the mourning that subdues the luminaries of fire and strengthens the luminaries of light (Likutey Moharan II:67)
mourning over the Beit HaMikdash — the practice of avelut for the destroyed Temple, whose initials hint 'kindle no fire in your dwellings'

nodes.he: מכניע מאורי אש, ומתגברין מאורי אור
nodes.gloss: the subduing of the luminaries of fire (me'orei eish) and strengthening of the luminaries of light (me'orei or) — the Shabbat-light dynamic effected by mourning Zion
the battim of the tefillin — the housings/boxes of the head-tefillin, 'house' vessels for the mochin/pe'er

nodes.he: כשנתגלה הפאר והיפי של הצדיק האמת
nodes.gloss: the revelation of the splendor and beauty of the true tzaddik — the event of his pe'er being disclosed, whereby mochin and sight are made and eyes opened
the colors (gevanin) that shine in the Temple — the eye-colors/Shabbat-lights illuminating the Beit HaMikdash
the magnification of the tzaddik's name — his fame growing in the world, within which God's own Name is clothed
the magnification of God's Name (shemo yitbarakh) — the divine Name growing great as a consequence of the tzaddik's name growing great
the revelation of this tzaddik — his becoming known and famous in the world, the 'shem' through which God's Name is magnified

nodes.he: יכול לראות ולהסתכל בגדלת השם ולהסתכל בעולם
nodes.gloss: the capacity to see and gaze upon God's greatness and upon the world — opened eyes/power of sight granted through the tzaddik's revealed splendor
the verse 'from there it divides and becomes four heads' (Gen 2:10) — the Eden-river splitting into four, source-text for the four elements/middot
the four elements (fire, air, water, earth) — the arba yesodot from which all the character traits (middot) are drawn
nahar yotze me-Eden — 'a river goes out of Eden' (Gen 2:10), the supernal flow/shefa issuing from Eden, symbol of the tzaddik as channel of the world's beauty
the act of drawing close to the true tzaddik — attaching oneself to the genuine righteous leader who is the world's beauty and grace
bekhiyah — weeping/crying, the mournful response linked to the destruction and the dominance of the luminaries of fire
weeping/crying (bekhi) — the act of shedding tears, which in LM II:67 causes the light of the eyes to depart, per Shabbat 151b
the departure/dimming of the light of the eyes (loss of eyesight caused by weeping, per Shabbat 151b), likened to the sun's light setting in the west
berakhah — the spoken blessing customarily given (with drink) to the messenger who carries wine/mead to guests or a wedding
niset ve-noset — Zoharic category (Pekudei 242a) of a thing that is 'carried yet carries,' borne by another while itself bearing/supporting

nodes.he: תקונם של אלו המחין של חוץ לארץ
nodes.gloss: the tikkun (rectification) of the 'mentalities of outside the Land' — repair of the chutz-la'aretz mochin damaged by the blemish of honor, effected when Supernal Pleasantness flows
the flowing of No'am ha-Elyon — the streaming of Supernal Pleasantness/Delight whose influx reveals divine honor and enables tikkun

shalhovin di-rechimuta — the Zoharic Aramaic term for 'flames of love,' the fiery arousal of passionate love awakened from the Supernal Pleasantness (No'am ha-Elyon), through which procreation (holadah) comes about

the Supernal Pleasantness (No'am HaElyon) — the divine delight/sweetness of the higher realm, from which flames of love (shalhovin dirchimuta) are aroused and through which procreation comes about (Likutey Moharan II:71)
mochin shel chutz-la'aretz — the diaspora mentalities/consciousness, aspect of 'chovlim' (destroyers, Zech 11:7), Torah scholars outside the Land who wound each other in halakhah

Chovlim ("Destroyers/Wounders") — the staff named in Zechariah 11:7 ("one I called Pleasantness and one I called Chovlim"), interpreted per Sanhedrin 24a as the Torah scholars outside the Land of Israel who wound each other in halakhic debate; in Likutey Moharan II:71 it designates the mochin (mentalities) of outside the Land, opposite the mochin of the Land of Israel which are No'am (Pleasantness). Distinct from חֲבָלִים (ropes/pangs) and from חוֹבְלִים as sailors (רַב הַחוֹבֵל).

No'am — 'Pleasantness' (נֹעַם), the divine sweetness/delightfulness of Zechariah 11:7 ('One I called No'am'), identified in Likutey Moharan II:71 with the mentalities (mochin) of the Land of Israel and with the Supernal Pleasantness (No'am HaElyon) whose flow arouses the flames of love; not the proper name Naomi (נָעֳמִי) nor any verbal form of נ־ע־ם
Yaakov and Yosef as a paired figure — the patriarch Jacob together with Joseph, joined aspects in the flow of Supernal Pleasantness and generosity

becoming/forming a vessel (keli) to receive the flow of the Supernal Pleasantness (No'am HaElyon) — the opening of the heart's pathways, chiefly through tzedakah, that enables one to receive the flames of divine love from the ever-flowing supernal delight (Likutey Moharan II:71)

the heart being opened and moved to give generously (שֶׁנִּפְתָּח וְנִתְנַדֵּב הַלֵּב) — the inner act of generosity of heart in giving charity, which opens the pathways of the heart to become a vessel for the flames of divine love (LM II:71)

generosity of heart (nedivut lev) — the willing, freely-moved impulse of the heart to give, identified with charity/terumah (per Exodus 25:2, "whose heart moves him"), whereby the heart is opened and becomes a vessel for the Supernal Pleasantness
shefir ve-shilya — the amniotic sac and placenta, embryological terms for the membranes accompanying birth, imagery of the birthing of the mochin
chevlei leidah — birth pangs, the pains of labor (wordplay on chovlim), the travail accompanying the birth/rectification of the diaspora mentalities

inheritance/heritage (נַחֲלַת, construct of נַחֲלָה) — the hereditary portion or estate, as in 'nachalat Yaakov' (the boundless heritage of Jacob, Isaiah 58:14) and 'nachalat' of Psalms 16:6, linked in LM II:71 to tzedakah and the flow of the Supernal Pleasantness

beautiful of form (yefeh to'ar) — the biblical epithet of physical comeliness/handsome appearance (as said of Joseph, Gen. 39:6), used in LM II:71 as an aspect of beauty (linked to Shifrah, 'making beautiful') connected to the revelation of honor and the Supernal Pleasantness

"who are pleasant [to one another] in halakhic discussion" (she-man'imim ba-halakhah) — the Talmudic description (cf. Sanhedrin 24a) of Torah scholars of the Land of Israel who treat each other graciously in halakhic debate, linked here to no'am (Supernal Pleasantness) as the aspect of the rectified 'mentalities of the Land of Israel,' in contrast to the 'destroyers' (chovlim) of outside the Land

pleasantness (noʿam) — the Supernal Pleasantness (nōʿam ha-ʿelyon), the sweet delightful divine flow associated with the mentalities of the Land of Israel; not the proper name Naʿam or naʿim as adjective

terumah — the dedicated offering/heave-offering (as in the Tabernacle donation, 'you shall take My terumah'), which Rabbi Nachman identifies with charity given from generosity of heart, forming a vessel to receive the Supernal Pleasantness (its letters being the final letters of 'lachazot be-no'am H' u-levaker be-heikhalo')

greatness (gedulah) — the noun for exalted stature, eminence, and majesty that a person receives (identified with the sefirah Malkhut and, at its core, with humility); not the feminine adjective gedolah ('large/great')
nedivei ha-am — 'the nobles/generous ones of the people' (Num 21:18), the generous-hearted donors of Israel who 'excavate' the well of Torah
chafaruha — 'they dug it' (Num 21:18), the act of digging the well, i.e., drawing forth Torah elucidations by the officers of Israel
matanah — 'a gift' (Num 21:18, 'from the wilderness a gift'), Torah insight received as a free gift via self-abasement (midbar/wilderness)
hitnotzetzut ha-moach — the sparking/flashing of a person's mind, its illumination kindled when the comprehensive sage gazes at him

nodes.he: מקבל כל אחד גדלה כפי מדרגת מחו
nodes.gloss: each individual's receiving of greatness according to the level of his mind — apportionment of gedulah measured by one's sparked mochin via the sage's gaze

the sparking/illumination of one's mind (mitnotzetz mocho) — the flash of mental enlightenment kindled in a person's individual intellect when the comprehensive sage (chakham ha-dor) gazes upon him, which is the channel through which he receives greatness (LM II:72)
mekabel gedulah — the receiving of greatness/eminence, obtaining one's rank through being seen by the comprehensive sage (tzaddik)
chakham ha-kolel — the comprehensive sage, the generation's all-inclusive mind (moach kelali) from whom all individual mochin receive

chiddushin de-Oraita — original novel Torah insights/novellae (Aramaic: 'novelties of the Torah'), the new interpretations and elucidations of Torah that the tzaddik-leader of the aspect of Moshe attains through the sparkling of his mind

nodes.he: חוזר ונחיה השפלות של כל אחד
nodes.gloss: the reviving of each person's dormant humility — reawakening the shiflut of Moshe embedded in every limb, which lies as if dead until aroused
bushah u-teshuvah — shame paired with repentance, the salutary embarrassment that arouses return to God
the qualification to be a leader of Israel — that only one purified of sexual desire, with clarified 'visions,' can serve as manhig Yisrael

nodes.he: מחיב שירגיש כל אחד שפלותו באמת
nodes.gloss: the obligating of each person to genuinely feel his own lowliness — the tzaddik's Torah compels true felt shiflut in every hearer
the Torah that the true tzaddik draws down — his channeled Torah teaching, which draws shame/humility on hearers as at Sinai

nodes.he: שבא אצל צדיק אמתי ושומע מפיו תורה
nodes.gloss: the act of coming before the true tzaddik and hearing Torah from his mouth — direct oral reception from the genuine righteous one
bushah ve-shiflut gadol me'od — very great shame and lowliness, the state fittingly drawn upon one who hears the true tzaddik's Torah (sign of authenticity)

fear and shame (yir'ah u-vushah) — the paired experience of awe of God and shame at one's distance from Him, which together constitute the essence of repentance and are identified with Shabbat (via the Tikkunei Zohar anagram of Bereishit: 'fears shame / fears Shabbat')

the eternal life (chayim nitzchiyim) of the World to Come (Olam HaBa) — everlasting afterlife-existence, which repentance and Shabbat embody as a foretaste ('Repent and live'; 'those who taste it merit life')
the state when the dormant humility is revived — the moment Moshe's implanted shiflut comes alive within a person
each person's seeing and feeling his own lowliness — the experiential perception of one's shiflut in every limb
the revival of every individual's humility — the collective quickening of the Moshe-humility rooted in each Jew from Sinai
meriting to originate chiddushim in Torah — attaining novel Torah insights (chiddushin de-Orayta) through the revived spirit

the comprehensive/all-inclusive spirit (ruach ha-kollel) — the collective ruach possessed by the true leader of Israel (the aspect of Moshe), which encompasses and knows how to engage the individual spirit of each and every person (Numbers 27:18, 'a man in whom there is spirit'), identified with the spirit of God and the mochin (Likutey Moharan II:72)

the true leader (manhig ha'amiti) of all Israel — the singular authentic tzaddik-leader of the whole Jewish people, identified with the aspect of Moshe and the comprehensive spirit (ruach ha-kollel) who knows how to engage the spirit of each individual (Likutey Moharan II:72)

The comprehensive Da'at (da'at ha-kollel) — the all-encompassing, collective knowledge/mind embodied by the true leader of Israel (the aspect of Moshe), identified with the comprehensive spirit (ruach ha-kollel) and the mochin, from which every individual's mind/spirit receives
seeing oneself together with the tzaddik — the act of being seen with/by the true tzaddik, which itself confers greatness even without hearing Torah
chayim nitzchiyim — eternal life, the unbounded life of the World to Come beyond all limit (gevul)
one who tastes the delight of Shabbat — the person experiencing oneg Shabbat, a semblance of the World to Come, earning a boundless inheritance

lowliness and humility (shiflut va-anivut) — the self-abnegating trait of meekness that renders a person like absolute nothingness (ayin) and thus without limit, the paired virtue-term for humble self-effacement in LM II:72
bilti gevul — limitlessness, the state of being without boundary that characterizes the spiritual pleasure of the World to Come

the fiftieth day (yom ha-chamishim) — the day following the forty-nine days of the Omer count, the day of the giving of the Torah at Sinai (Shavuot), corresponding to the fiftieth gate of repentance and God's own teshuvah
the teshuvah of God Himself — the fiftieth gate: repentance/return attributed to Hashem as it were ('Return to Me and I will return to you,' Mal 3:7)
the 49 days of Sefirat ha-Omer — the counting of forty-nine days from Egypt to Sinai corresponding to the 49 gates of teshuvah
meitzar ha-garon — the 'strait of the throat,' kabbalistic locus of constriction (wordplay on Mitzrayim), site of teshuvah ila'ah per the Arizal

Teshuvah Ila'ah — the kabbalistic 'higher/supernal repentance' (Aramaic ila'ah, 'upper'), the elevated level of return associated with Binah in Lurianic Kabbalah, here identified with the constriction of the throat (meitzar ha-garon) symbolized by Egypt; distinct from ordinary/lower repentance (teshuvah tata'ah)

the Fiftieth Gate (Sha'ar HaChamishim) — the fiftieth gate of understanding/repentance beyond the forty-nine gates of teshuvah, identified with God's own 'return' (ve-ashuvah aleichem) at the giving of the Torah on the fiftieth day
amirat Tehillim — the recitation of Psalms as a practice with segulah-power to arouse and attain teshuvah
being regularly accustomed to reciting Psalms — the habitual practice of Tehillim recitation recommended for one seeking teshuvah
Purim — the festival named for the pur (lot, Esther 9:26), stage preceding Parashat Parah and preparation toward Pesach (pur → parah)

the freedom (cherut) of Passover — the spiritual liberation from bondage/exile that Pesach embodies, toward which Purim (via Mordechai) is a path and preparation; not charut ('engraved,' as on the Tablets)
histaklut ba-tzaddik — gazing upon the face of the tzaddik, itself a great practice since the Torah scholar is greater than the Torah scroll
kedushah — holiness as a state/quality; here the sanctity in which eating and the tzaddik's presence are invested, distinct from mere separateness

eating in holiness (akhilah bi-kedushah) — the spiritual practice of consuming food in sanctity and fear of Heaven, which sweetens daily suffering and harsh judgments and elevates the mouth from an animal state to the stature of Adam

nodes.he: נעשה המתקה, שלא יתגבר הצער ביותר
nodes.gloss: the sweetening effected through eating in holiness so that daily suffering (tza'ar) does not overwhelm — an act of hamtakah (mitigation of pain/judgment)

fear/awe of the side of holiness (yirah di-kedushah) — the holy fear of God, counterpart of fallen fear (retzu'ah bisha), identified in LM II:77 with the holy tefillin strap passing through the ma'abarta
retzu'ah dikedushah — the 'strap of holiness': holy fear (yirah) figured as the tefillin strap, counterpart to the evil strap
retzu'ah bisha (Zohar, Intro 11b) — the 'evil strap': the demonic lash of fallen fear that inflicts suffering and judgment
yirah nefulah — fallen fear: awe of Heaven degraded into worldly fears/anxieties, identified with the evil strap

nodes.he: רצועה שעוברת בתוך המעברתא של תפלין
nodes.gloss: the tefillin strap (retzuah) that passes through the ma'abarta, the hollow passage-loop at the back of the tefillin box — in Likutey Moharan II:77 the physical strap threaded through this channel, homiletically identified with holy fear (yirah) passing through and binding to the mochin (the tefillin as mind/intellect)

nodes.he: ממתיק הצער והדין הבא מרצועה בישא
nodes.gloss: the act of sweetening/mitigating the suffering and judgment (din) that descends from the evil strap (retzu'ah bisha), accomplished via holy eating
the transformation whereby eating in holiness makes the mouth into the 'stature of Adam' (komat adam) — human, not animal, per 'Who placed a mouth for man' (Ex. 4:11)
the resulting state: the mouth rendered into komat adam (full human stature) by bringing Malkhut/fear into it during holy eating

nodes.he: שאוכל עם יראת־שמים, בקדשה ובטהרה כראוי
nodes.gloss: the practice of eating with fear of Heaven, in holiness and purity as is fitting — the devotional mode of eating that draws Malkhut into the mouth
making from the mouth the stature of Adam (fashioning the full spiritual 'komat adam' out of the mouth/speech through eating in holiness and fear of Heaven, Likutey Moharan II:77)

the leather strap of the tefillin (רְצוּעָה שֶׁל תְּפִלִּין) — the binding strap attached to the phylactery boxes, which in LM II:77 embodies fear/Malkhut (Yehudah) entering the mochin/da'at of the tefillin (Binyamin); not a whip-strap of punishment nor any other strap
